title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
陝西鄉試錄序
萬曆癸酉天下又當大比士
于鄉寔我
皇上龍飛之初之第一舉也在三
秦抱藝而思利見者飈奮雲
烝盛矣廵按陝西御史蔡〔廷〕
臣
司監臨祇奉
===
明命矢公矢慎有加往昔而考試
提調監試以及諸執事亦罔
弗公焉罔弗慎焉旣得士爲
錄且
獻〔太和〕作而言曰思皇多士生
此王國王國克生維周之楨
此非豐鎬岐周間詩乎〔太和〕
punctuated:
陝西鄉試錄序
萬曆癸酉，天下又當大比士于鄉，寔我皇上龍飛之初之第一舉也。在三秦抱藝而思利見者，飈奮雲烝，盛矣！廵按陝西御史蔡〔廷〕臣司監臨，祇奉明命，矢公矢慎，有加往昔；而考試、提調、監試以及諸執事，亦罔弗公焉，罔弗慎焉。旣得士，爲錄且獻，〔太和〕作而言曰：「『思皇多士，生此王國。王國克生，維周之楨。』此非豐、鎬、岐、周間詩乎？〔太和〕
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shaanxi Provincial Examination

In the guiyou year of the Wanli reign (1573), the empire once again reached the time for the great triennial examination of scholars in the provinces; this was in truth the very first examination held since His Majesty ascended the throne. Throughout the Three Qin regions of Shaanxi, those who possessed literary mastery and longed to advance and present themselves rose up like whirlwinds and gathered like clouds—how flourishing indeed! The Regional Investigating Censor of Shaanxi, Cai Tingchen 蔡廷臣, served as Supervising Official. Reverently upholding the illustrious imperial mandate, he vowed to act with fairness and circumspection even more than in past times; and the Examiners, Proctors, Monitoring Officials, and all the various functionaries were likewise without exception fair and circumspect. Once the scholars had been selected and the record compiled to be presented to the throne, I, [Taihe 太和], rose and said: "'August is the host of scholars, born in this royal kingdom. The royal kingdom is able to bring them forth; they are the supporting pillars of Zhou.' Is this not a poem from the region of Feng, Hao, Qi, and Zhou? I, [Taihe]…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
嘗誦此詩輒慨然興感有慕
於其地焉思見之矣維兹關
中固昔之王國地也〔太和〕旣
幸酬夙願又幸獲叨與掄材
則嘆關中人才之盛而竊有
國士之期焉何者詩稱西周
之才不曰才曰楨此其意嘗
===
於版築之間而知之矣版築
者之築墉也捄度畚鍤秩然
具矣苟楨榦弗峙庸詎能言
言仡仡高且堅乎是故墉有
楨榦則震撼不搖墉乃固國
有賢才則窺伺不作國乃寧
詩蓋稱其鉅者哉故夫楨榦
punctuated: 嘗誦此詩，輒慨然興感，有慕於其地焉，思見之矣。維兹關中，固昔之王國地也。〔太和〕旣幸酬夙願，又幸獲叨與掄材，則嘆關中人才之盛，而竊有國士之期焉。何者？《詩》稱西周之才，不曰「才」，曰「楨」，此其意嘗於版築之間而知之矣。版築者之築墉也，捄度畚鍤，秩然具矣；苟楨榦弗峙，庸詎能言言仡仡、高且堅乎？是故墉有楨榦，則震撼不搖，墉乃固；國有賢才，則窺伺不作，國乃寧。《詩》蓋稱其鉅者哉！故夫楨榦
translation_en: …Whenever I recited this ode, I was always deeply moved and stirred, admiring the region and longing to behold it. Now, this Guanzhong region is indeed the territory of that royal domain of antiquity. Having had the good fortune to fulfill my long-cherished wish, and having further had the good fortune to share unworthily in the selection of talent, I have marveled at the abundance of talented men in Guanzhong, and privately hold expectations that they will be men of state-wide eminence (guoshi). Why is this? When the Book of Odes (Shijing) praises the talents of the Western Zhou, it does not call them "talents" (cai), but calls them "pillars" (zhen); the meaning of this I once came to understand from the work of rammed-earth construction. When builders of rammed earth construct a city wall, the scooping baskets, measuring lines, hods, and spades are all set out in orderly array; yet if the end-posts and side-stakes (zhengan) do not stand upright, how could the wall rise lofty and imposing, both high and solid? Therefore, when a wall has its end-posts and side-stakes, it does not waver under shock and shaking, and thus the wall is firm; when a state has worthy talents,opportunistic designs do not arise, and thus the state is at peace. The Odes were surely praising what is great! Now, as for end-posts and side-stakes,…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
者木之碩大而堅實者也非
凡材倫也乃若楨國之才豈
以彼文具緣飾追趨逐者者
所可幾哉要必有淳厚端實
宏碩剛毅之士斯可以借彈
壓而托倚毗也夫淳厚端實
宏碩剛毅固西周之士之素
===
稟而恒習者其能楨國也固
宜士至於楨國斯足以語國
士矣周而下士不見重然發
為文辭猶深厚雄偉千載之
下稱為秦漢間文字與魏晉
以降數代者不同日道也關
中風土所從來其盛如此
punctuated: 者，木之碩大而堅實者也，非凡材倫也。乃若楨國之才，豈以彼文具緣飾、追趨逐者者所可幾哉？要必有淳厚端實、宏碩剛毅之士，斯可以借彈壓而托倚毗也。夫淳厚端實、宏碩剛毅，固西周之士之素稟而恒習者，其能楨國也固宜。士至於楨國，斯足以語國士矣。周而下，士不見重，然發為文辭，猶深厚雄偉，千載之下，稱為秦漢間文字，與魏晉以降數代者不同日道也。關中風土所從來，其盛如此。
translation_en: … are timber that is massive and solid, not of the same class as ordinary wood. As for talents that serve as pillars of the state, how could they be approached by those who merely adorn themselves with superficialities and chase after trends [?]? In short, there must be scholars who are pure, generous, upright, solid, grand, and resolute; only then can one rely on them to maintain order and entrust them with vital support. Now, being pure, generous, upright, solid, grand, and resolute were indeed the innate endowments and constant habits of the scholars of the Western Zhou; that they were able to serve as pillars of the state was certainly fitting. When a scholar reaches the point of serving as a pillar of the state, only then is he worthy of being spoken of as a scholar of the state. From the Zhou onward, scholars were no longer held in such esteem, yet when they expressed themselves in literary composition, it was still profound, rich, and magnificent. A thousand years later, it is praised as the writing of the Qin and Han periods, not to be spoken of on the same day as that of the several dynasties from the Wei and Jin onward. Such is the flourishing tradition from which the local customs and character of Guanzhong have long derived.

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
明興二百餘年
祖宗培養澤深鉅才代起其以道
德節義功業擎柱
巖廊擅名海寓者後先相望信
方古國士之篤諸士生於其
鄉而習聞之矣况又自得於
風土者厚也故今諸士之文
===
時文也而奇氣古意往往見
於筆墨畦徑間謂依俙有先
秦西漢之風非耶寧獨如是
意必有負淳厚端實宏碩剛
毅如西周者在所收之中而
為我
明之楨矣乎誠望之也然又竊慮
punctuated: 明興二百餘年，祖宗培養澤深，鉅才代起。其以道德、節義、功業擎柱巖廊，擅名海寓者，後先相望，信方古國士之篤。諸士生於其鄉，而習聞之矣，况又自得於風土者厚也。故今諸士之文，時文也，而奇氣古意往往見於筆墨畦徑間，謂依俙有先秦、西漢之風，非耶？寧獨如是？意必有負淳厚端實、宏碩剛毅如西周者，在所收之中，而為我明之楨矣乎？誠望之也！然又竊慮
translation_en: For over two hundred years since the rise of the Ming, the nurturing grace of our Imperial Ancestors has been profound, and great talents have arisen in every generation. Those who by their moral virtue, integrity, and achievements have served as pillars of the imperial court and won renown throughout the realm have succeeded one another in unbroken view, truly matching the devotion of the "scholars of state" of antiquity. Born in this native land, the gentlemen have long been familiar with hearing of them—how much more so since what they themselves have absorbed from the local customs and soil is so rich! Thus, though the writings of these gentlemen today are contemporary examination essays, an extraordinary spirit and ancient ethos often appear within the paths of their brush and ink; is it not right to say that they faintly possess the style of the pre-Qin and Western Han? And how could it be merely thus? Might I suppose that among those selected there must be men endowed with pure thickness, upright solidity, grand breadth, and resolute fortitude like those of the Western Zhou, who will serve as pillars for our Ming? This I truly hope for! Yet I also privately worry…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
之世代既逖僭爵王途紛華
易奪安知淳厚者不化而爲
靡薄端實者不化而爲曲譎
宏碩剛毅者不化而爲委瑣
選耎矣乎苟有之則文雖近
似實失其所以爲關中者而
有負玆土之產
國家何賴焉
聖天子紹統
御極方在冲年卽數
召輔臣
平臺非風雨罔不
夙臨
經幄親賢圖治日亹亹不倦眞不
punctuated: 之。世代既逖，僭爵王途，紛華易奪，安知淳厚者不化而爲靡薄，端實者不化而爲曲譎，宏碩剛毅者不化而爲委瑣選耎矣乎？苟有之，則文雖近似，實失其所以爲關中者，而有負玆土之產，國家何賴焉？聖天子紹統御極，方在冲年，卽數召輔臣平臺，非風雨罔不夙臨經幄，親賢圖治，日亹亹不倦，眞不
translation_en:
… about this. Since the eras are now far removed, and along the paths to noble rank and royal service, dazzling luxury easily steals away one's resolve, how can we know that those who are simple and generous will not degenerate into extravagance and superficiality, that those who are upright and sincere will not degenerate into crookedness and deceit, and that those who are broad-minded, great, firm, and resolute will not degenerate into pettiness and timidity? Should there be such men, then even if their writings closely resemble the ancients, in reality they have lost what makes them men of Guanzhong, failing what this land produces—and how can the State rely upon them?

The Sacred Son of Heaven has succeeded to the line and ascended the throne. While still in his youth, he already frequently summons his chief ministers to the Platform Hall (Pingtai); unless there is wind or rain, he never fails to attend the Classics Mat early in the morning. Drawing close to the worthy and planning for good governance, day after day he exerts himself tirelessly—truly a…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
世出之
主也頃者蒐拔四方摧廢之士至
數十百人且申嚴大比科條
意至惓切者凡以冀獲鉅才
如周之楨國者而用之也諸
士幸際玆奇遘忍負之乎誠
能感時思奮亢志前修益培
===
其淳厚端實宏碩剛毅之體
於凡靡薄曲譎委瑣選耎諸
流俗卑卑者心賤之而足不
蹈焉養成忠義之幹異日者
疏附後先鬱爲時棟詎直嗣
芳近哲即周之多士不得專
美於前矣主司且自慶得國
punctuated: 世出之主也。頃者蒐拔四方摧廢之士至數十百人，且申嚴大比科條，意至惓切者，凡以冀獲鉅才如周之楨國者而用之也。諸士幸際玆奇遘，忍負之乎？誠能感時思奮，亢志前修，益培其淳厚、端實、宏碩、剛毅之體；於凡靡薄、曲譎、委瑣、選耎諸流俗卑卑者，心賤之而足不蹈焉。養成忠義之幹，異日者疏附後先，鬱爲時棟，詎直嗣芳近哲，即周之多士不得專美於前矣。主司且自慶得國
translation_en: …a sovereign who appears but once in generations! Recently, He has sought out and promoted scores and even hundreds of scholars from the four quarters who had been broken and cast aside, and has moreover reiterated and tightened the regulations for the triennial examinations; His intent is most earnest and urgent, all in the hope of obtaining great talents—like those who served as the pillars of the state in the Zhou—and employing them. You scholars are fortunate to meet with this extraordinary juncture; how could you bear to fail it? If you can truly be moved by the times to rouse yourselves, elevate your ambitions toward the worthies of the past, and further cultivate a substance that is pure and generous, upright and solid, broad and great, firm and resolute; and as for all those vulgar and base tendencies that are frivolous and shallow, crooked and deceitful, petty, and timid and weak, despise them in your hearts and never set foot in them—then you will nurture a trunk of loyalty and righteousness. On a future day, drawing the distant closer and serving before and behind the sovereign, you will flourish as the ridgepoles of the age. How would this merely be a matter of continuing the fragrant renown of recent sages? Even the "many officers" of the Zhou would not be able to monopolize glory in the past! We, the chief examiners, will moreover congratulate ourselves on having obtained for the state…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
之楨而又何暇於異代慕也
雖然尤有辨焉朱紫之閒毫
釐千里苟或好高自負大言
無當以血氣事事而不要諸
理甚至恣睢剛愎怒喜異同
若此者自許國士去國士霄
壤矣苟能厎厲名節沉浸道
===
德貞義徇國不有我不利害
怵毀譽搖卽不自負國士人
以國士歸之矣是故爲士者
非名之貴而無實之患取士
者非無士之患而得國士之
難丘陵之原易爲崒嵂渥洼
之種可屬纖離何者有其具
punctuated: 之楨，而又何暇於異代慕也？雖然，尤有辨焉。朱紫之閒，毫釐千里。苟或好高自負，大言無當，以血氣事事，而不要諸理，甚至恣睢剛愎，怒喜異同，若此者，自許國士，去國士霄壤矣。苟能厎厲名節，沉浸道德，貞義徇國，不有我，不利害怵、毀譽搖，卽不自負國士，人以國士歸之矣。是故爲士者，非名之貴，而無實之患；取士者，非無士之患，而得國士之難。丘陵之原，易爲崒嵂；渥洼之種，可屬纖離。何者？有其具
translation_en:
… pillars of the state; what need would they have to yearn for those of bygone eras?

Even so, there is a further distinction to be made. Between true vermilion and purple, a hair's breadth leads to a difference of a thousand miles. If someone aims high out of self-conceit, makes grand pronouncements without substance, handles affairs through mere impulsiveness without grounding them in principle, and even goes so far as to be overbearing and obstinate, growing angry at dissent and pleased by agreement—though such a person may style himself a scholar of national standing (guoshi), he is as far from being a true scholar of national standing as earth is from heaven. Conversely, if one can whet one's integrity and reputation, immerse oneself in the Way and its virtue, devote oneself to the state with steadfast righteousness, remain free of egoism, and neither be intimidated by personal advantage or harm nor swayed by slander or praise—then even if he does not pride himself on being a scholar of national standing, others will recognize him as such.

Therefore, for those who are scholars, what matters is not the prestige of reputation, but the peril of lacking substance; for those who select scholars, the concern is not a lack of scholars, but the difficulty of obtaining true scholars of national standing. From the high plateaus of hills and mounds, it is easy to rise to lofty peaks; from the stock of the Wowa River, one can expect fine steeds like Xianli. Why is this? Because they possess the requisite…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
也關中之士其淳厚端實宏
碩剛毅者是國士之具也故
茲於諸士始進雖其文有先
秦西漢之風不具論論所以
楨國者蓋本其風土之素而
以國士爲諸士期諸士勗之
哉主司者固緦緦日冀幸之
矣是舉也〔太和〕與學正宋〔崇〕
〔獻〕司考試教諭何〔宏〕賓〔仲矩〕
===
唐〔廷燦〕阮〔純如〕司同考試乃
巡按御史陳〔文煥〕先期所禮
聘左布政使侯〔東萊〕右布政
使秦〔鈁〕司提調副使張〔大忠〕
李〔良臣〕司監試而六十五人
punctuated:
也。關中之士，其淳厚、端實、宏碩、剛毅者，是國士之具也。故茲於諸士始進，雖其文有先秦、西漢之風，不具論；論所以楨國者，蓋本其風土之素，而以國士爲諸士期。諸士勗之哉！主司者固緦緦日冀幸之矣。

是舉也，〔太和〕與學正宋〔崇〕〔獻〕司考試，教諭何〔宏〕、賓〔仲矩〕、唐〔廷燦〕、阮〔純如〕司同考試，乃巡按御史陳〔文煥〕先期所禮聘。左布政使侯〔東萊〕、右布政使秦〔鈁〕司提調，副使張〔大忠〕、李〔良臣〕司監試。而六十五人
translation_en:
… As for the scholars of Guanzhong, their pure and generous, upright and substantial, vast and great, and firm and resolute qualities are the very makings of scholars of state caliber (guoshi 國士). Therefore, now as you scholars make your initial advancement, although your writings possess the style of the pre-Qin and Western Han periods, I shall not discuss that in full; instead, I discuss the means of serving as pillars of the state, basing my remarks on the inherent qualities of your local customs and terrain, and holding up the standard of scholars of state caliber as my expectation for you. Strive hard, scholars! Those in charge of the examination certainly hope for this day after day with earnest solicitude.

In this examination, I (Taihe 太和) and Department Director of Schools Song Chongxian 宋崇獻 served as Examiners, while District Directors of Schools He Hong 何宏, Bin Zhongju 賓仲矩, Tang Tingcan 唐廷燦, and Ruan Chunru 阮純如 served as Associate Examiners, all having been courteously invited in advance by Regional Inspector Chen Wenhuan 陳文煥. Left Administration Commissioner Hou Donglai 侯東萊 and Right Administration Commissioner Qin Fang 秦鈁 served as Proctors, while Surveillance Vice Commissioners Zhang Dazhong 張大忠 and Li Liangchen 李良臣 served as Surveillance Officials of the Examination (Jianshi 監試). And as for the sixty-five men…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
者則巡按御史暴〔孟石奇〕董
暨提學副使劉〔有誠〕陸〔光祚〕
先後所選士二千有奇而拔
其儁云時總督軍務兵部尚
書兼右副都御史戴〔才〕閱視
邊務兵部左侍郎兼右僉都
御史王〔遴〕巡撫陝西右僉都
===
御史部〔光先〕巡撫寧夏右僉
都御史先朱〔笈〕今羅〔鳳翔〕巡
撫延綏右僉都御史張〔守中〕
巡撫甘肅右僉都御史廖〔逢〕
〔節〕撫治鄖陽右副都御史湯
〔賓〕綏宇宣猷咸興文教巡按
監察御史茶馬趙〔煥〕清軍李
punctuated: 者，則巡按御史暴〔孟石奇〕董，暨提學副使劉〔有誠〕、陸〔光祚〕，先後所選士二千有奇，而拔其儁云。時總督軍務兵部尚書兼右副都御史戴〔才〕、閱視邊務兵部左侍郎兼右僉都御史王〔遴〕、巡撫陝西右僉都御史部〔光先〕、巡撫寧夏右僉都御史先朱〔笈〕今羅〔鳳翔〕、巡撫延綏右僉都御史張〔守中〕、巡撫甘肅右僉都御史廖〔逢節〕、撫治鄖陽右副都御史湯〔賓〕，綏宇宣猷，咸興文教；巡按監察御史茶馬趙〔煥〕、清軍李
translation_en: … were the outstanding talents selected from among more than two thousand scholars previously and successively chosen by Regional Inspector (xun'an yushi) Bao Mengqi 暴孟奇 [transcribed as 孟石奇], together with Education Intendant Vice Commissioners (tixue fushi) Liu Youcheng 劉有誠 and Lu Guangzuo 陸光祚, who supervised the selection. At this time, Supreme Commander of Military Affairs (zongdu junwu), Minister of War (bingbu shangshu) and concurrent Right Vice Censor-in-Chief (you fudu yushi) Dai Cai 戴才; Inspector of Frontier Affairs (yueshi bianwu), Left Vice Minister of War (bingbu zuo shilang) and concurrent Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief (you qiandu yushi) Wang Lin 王遴; Grand Coordinator (xunfu) of Shaanxi and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief郜 Guangxian 郜光先 [transcribed as 部光先]; Grand Coordinator of Ningxia and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, formerly Zhu Ji 朱笈 and now Luo Fengxiang 羅鳳翔; Grand Coordinator of Yansui and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Zhang Shouzhong 張守中; Grand Coordinator of Gansu and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Liao Fengjie 廖逢節; and Grand Coordinator (fuzhi) of Yunyang and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Tang Bin 湯賓 pacified the territory and promulgated state policies, all promoting literary and moral education. Regional Inspecting Censors (xun'an jiancha yushi) Zhao Huan 趙煥 for the Tea-and-Horse Trade (chama), Li … for Troop Purification (qingjun) …

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
〔采非〕許〔乾〕河東鹽法張〔道〕秉
憲肅紀丕振士風若奉
命有事茲土則尚寶司少卿石〔星〕
刑科都給事中烏〔昇〕戶部郎
中張〔體乾〕崔〔行可〕兵部主事
劉〔堯成〕協恭綜理於外則左
叅政朱〔卿〕徐〔節〕左叅議劉〔伯〕
===
〔燮〕梅〔友松〕右叅議胡〔定〕姚〔繼〕
〔可〕副使程〔鳴伊〕呂〔鳴珂〕張〔夢〕
〔鯉〕蔡〔可教〕孫〔坤〕王〔惟善〕楊〔起〕
〔元〕晉〔應槐〕平〔康裕〕李〔承式〕陳
〔廷芝〕僉事侯〔居坤〕劉〔之蒙〕翟
〔繡裳〕原〔森〕行太僕寺卿陳〔耀〕
〔文〕祁〔天敘〕少卿袁〔貞吉〕賀〔賁〕
punctuated: 〔采非〕、許〔乾〕，河東鹽法張〔道〕，秉憲肅紀，丕振士風。若奉命有事茲土，則尚寶司少卿石〔星〕，刑科都給事中烏〔昇〕，戶部郎中張〔體乾〕、崔〔行可〕，兵部主事劉〔堯成〕。協恭綜理於外，則左叅政朱〔卿〕、徐〔節〕，左叅議劉〔伯燮〕、梅〔友松〕，右叅議胡〔定〕、姚〔繼可〕，副使程〔鳴伊〕、呂〔鳴珂〕、張〔夢鯉〕、蔡〔可教〕、孫〔坤〕、王〔惟善〕、楊〔起元〕、晉〔應槐〕、平〔康裕〕、李〔承式〕、陳〔廷芝〕，僉事侯〔居坤〕、劉〔之蒙〕、翟〔繡裳〕、原〔森〕，行太僕寺卿陳〔耀文〕、祁〔天敘〕，少卿袁〔貞吉〕、賀〔賁〕、
translation_en: … [Li] Caifei 〔采非〕 and Xu Qian 許〔乾〕, and that for the Hedong Salt Monopoly, Zhang Dao 張〔道〕, upheld the laws and enforced discipline, greatly invigorating the ethos of the literati. As for those who received the imperial command to attend to affairs in this territory, there were Vice Director of the Seal Office Shi Xing 石〔星〕; Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Justice Wu Sheng 烏〔昇〕; Directors in the Ministry of Revenue Zhang Tiqian 張〔體乾〕 and Cui Xingke 崔〔行可〕; and Secretary in the Ministry of War Liu Yaocheng 劉〔堯成〕. Those who collaborated with reverence in the overall administration in the provinces included Left Administration Vice Commissioners Zhu Qing 朱〔卿〕 and Xu Jie 徐〔節〕; Left Assistant Administration Commissioners Liu Boxie 劉〔伯燮〕 and Mei Yousong 梅〔友松〕; Right Assistant Administration Commissioners Hu Ding 胡〔定〕 and Yao Jike 姚〔繼可〕; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Cheng Mingyi 程〔鳴伊〕, Lü Mingke 呂〔鳴珂〕, Zhang Mengli 張〔夢鯉〕, Cai Kejiao 蔡〔可教〕, Sun Kun 孫〔坤〕, Wang Weishan 王〔惟善〕, Yang Qiyuan 楊〔起元〕, Jin Yinghuai 晉〔應槐〕, Ping Kangyu 平〔康裕〕, Li Chengshi 李〔承式〕, and Chen Tingzhi 陳〔廷芝〕; Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Hou Jukun 侯〔居坤〕, Liu Zhimeng 劉〔之蒙〕, Zhai Xiushang 翟〔繡裳〕, and Yuan Sen 原〔森〕; Chief Ministers of the Branch Court of the Imperial Stud Chen Yaowen 陳〔耀文〕 and Qi Tianxu 祁〔天敘〕; and Vice Ministers Yuan Zhenji 袁〔貞吉〕, He Ben 賀〔賁〕, …

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
胡〔維新〕苑馬寺卿馬〔出圖〕少
卿馬〔文健〕孫〔光祖〕先期入
賀則右叅政楊〔旂〕副使郝〔杰〕署
都指揮使李〔學詩〕而署都指
揮僉事梁〔文〕毛〔斐然〕與有防
範之勞例得備書焉
湖廣常德府儒學教授劉〔太〕
和〕謹序
punctuated:
胡〔維新〕，苑馬寺卿馬〔出圖〕、少卿馬〔文健〕、孫〔光祖〕。先期入賀，則右叅政楊〔旂〕、副使郝〔杰〕、署都指揮使李〔學詩〕；而署都指揮僉事梁〔文〕、毛〔斐然〕，與有防範之勞，例得備書焉。
湖廣常德府儒學教授劉〔太和〕謹序。
translation_en:
…Hu Weixin 胡維新; Chief Minister of the Pasturage Office Ma Chutu 馬出圖, and Vice Ministers Ma Wenjian 馬文健 and Sun Guangzu 孫光祖. As for those who departed ahead of time to present congratulations at court, they were Right Administration Vice Commissioner Yang Qi 楊旂, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Hao Jie 郝杰, and Acting Regional Military Commissioner Li Xueshi 李學詩; while Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Liang Wen 梁文 and Mao Feiran 毛斐然 shared in the labor of security precautions, and by precedent merit being recorded in full.
Respectfully prefaced by Liu Taihe 劉太和, Confucian School Instructor of Changde Prefecture in Huguang.

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
夫子焉不學而亦何常師之有
見而民莫不敬言而民莫不信行而民莫
不說是以聲名洋溢乎中國施及蠻貊
孟子曰仁言不如仁聲之入人深也善政
不如善教之得民也善政民畏之善教
民愛之善政得民財善教得民心
易
===
大君之宜行中之謂也
用見大人勿恤有慶也南征吉志行也
六爻之動三極之道也是故君子所居而
安者易之序也所樂而玩者爻之辭也
是故君子居則觀其象而玩其辭動則
觀其變而玩其占是以自天祐之吉无
不利
齊也者言萬物之潔齊也
書
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
夫子焉不學？而亦何常師之有？
見而民莫不敬，言而民莫不信，行而民莫不說。是以聲名洋溢乎中國，施及蠻貊。
孟子曰：「仁言不如仁聲之入人深也，善政不如善教之得民也。善政，民畏之；善教，民愛之。善政得民財，善教得民心。」

易
大君之宜，行中之謂也。
用見大人，勿恤，有慶也；南征吉，志行也。
六爻之動，三極之道也。是故君子所居而安者，易之序也；所樂而玩者，爻之辭也。是故君子居則觀其象而玩其辭，動則觀其變而玩其占，是以「自天祐之，吉无不利」。
齊也者，言萬物之潔齊也。

書
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
1. "Where does our Master not learn? And yet what regular teacher does he have?" (Analects 19.22)
2. "Therefore, when he appears, none of the common people fail to respect him; when he speaks, none of the common people fail to believe him; when he acts, none of the common people fail to be pleased with him. Thus his fame and renown overflow the Central States and extend to the Man and Mo tribes." (Doctrine of the Mean 31)
3. Mencius said, "Benevolent words do not penetrate people as deeply as a reputation for benevolence; good government does not win the people as well as good instruction. Good government makes the people fear it; good instruction makes the people love it. Good government wins the people's wealth; good instruction wins the people's hearts." (Mencius 7A.14)

Classic of Changes (Yi)
1. "'What is fitting for the great ruler': this means walking the path of the mean." (Hexagram 16, Lin, commentary on the lines, six in the fifth place)
2. "'Employing this to see the great man, do not worry': there will be cause for celebration. 'Advancing southward brings good fortune': one's will is carried out." (Hexagram 46, Sheng, commentary on the judgment)
3. "The movements of the six lines contain the Way of the Three Ultimates. Therefore, what the noble man abides in and finds peace in is the sequence of the Changes; what he delights in and ponders is the statements on the lines. Therefore, when at rest, the noble man observes the images and ponders the statements; when in action, he observes the transformations and ponders the prognostications. Thus 'help comes to him from Heaven; there is good fortune and nothing that is not beneficial.'" (Appended Statements, Part I, Chapter 2)
4. "'Ordering' (Zhai, corresponding to the trigram Xun) means that the myriad things are made pure and orderly." (Discussion of the Trigrams, Chapter 5)

Classic of Documents (Shu)

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
彰厥有常吉哉日宣三德夙夜浚明有家
日嚴祗敬六德亮采有邦
念終始典于學厥德修罔覺
三八政一曰食二曰貨三曰祀四曰司空
五曰司徒六曰司寇七曰賓八曰師四
五紀一曰歲二曰月三曰日四曰星辰
五曰曆數
亦越成湯陟丕釐上帝之耿命
詩
===
星言夙駕說于桑田
夜如何其夜未央庭燎之光君子至止鸞
聲將將夜如何其夜未艾庭燎晣晣君
子至止鸞聲噦噦夜如何其夜鄉晨庭
燎有煇君子至止言觀其旂
脩爾車馬弓矢戎兵用戒戎作用逷蠻方
受小球大球爲下國綴旒何天之休
春秋
秋八月壬午大閱〔桓公六年〕
punctuated:
彰厥有常，吉哉！日宣三德，夙夜浚明有家；日嚴祗敬六德，亮采有邦。
念終始典于學，厥德修罔覺。
三、八政：一曰食，二曰貨，三曰祀，四曰司空，五曰司徒，六曰司寇，七曰賓，八曰師。四、五紀：一曰歲，二曰月，三曰日，四曰星辰，五曰曆數。
亦越成湯陟，丕釐上帝之耿命。
《詩》
星言夙駕，說于桑田。
夜如何其？夜未央，庭燎之光。君子至止，鸞聲將將。夜如何其？夜未艾，庭燎晣晣。君子至止，鸞聲噦噦。夜如何其？夜鄉晨，庭燎有煇。君子至止，言觀其旂。
脩爾車馬，弓矢戎兵，用戒戎作，用逷蠻方。
受小球大球，爲下國綴旒，何天之休。
《春秋》
秋，八月，壬午，大閱。〔桓公六年〕
translation_en:
"Manifesting his constancy: how auspicious! Daily displaying three of the virtues, and early and late being earnest and enlightened among those who possess families; daily being strict and reverently honoring the six virtues, and assisting in the affairs of those who possess states."

"Focus from beginning to end constantly on learning, and your virtue will be cultivated without your being conscious of it."

"Third, the eight objects of government: the first is called food; the second is called commodities; the third is called sacrifices; the fourth is called the Minister of Works (sikong); the fifth is called the Minister of Education (situ); the sixth is called the Minister of Justice (sikou); the seventh is called guests; the eighth is called the army. Fourth, the five arrangers of time: the first is called the year; the second is called the month; the third is called the day; the fourth is called the stars and zodiacal spaces; the fifth is called the calendrical calculations."

"And when it came to Tang the Successful ascending the throne, he grandly administered the bright mandate of the Lord on High."

Book of Odes (Shi)

"By starlight he yokes his carriage early, and halts in the mulberry fields."

"How goes the night? The night is not yet ended; the courtyard torches blaze. The lord is arriving; the bells on his horses chime clang-clang. How goes the night? The night is not yet spent; the courtyard torches shine brightly. The lord is arriving; the bells on his horses tinkle harmoniously. How goes the night? The night approaches dawn; the courtyard torches gleam amidst the smoke. The lord is arriving; now we see his banners."

"Make ready your chariots and horses, your bows and arrows and weapons of war, to guard against the outbreak of hostilities, to keep at a distance the southern tribes (Man)."

"He received the small jade token and the large jade token, acting as the pendant-streamers for the subordinate states; he bore the blessings of Heaven."

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

"In autumn, in the eighth month, on the day renwu, there was a grand military review." [Sixth year of Duke Huan]

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
第五道
問先儒有言明君以務學爲急聖學以正
心爲要是心學之懋固治業之所由基
也粤自虞庭肇精一之傳而危微之幾
始判孔門衍誠正之旨而慎獨之義斯
昭淵乎聖學宗旨矣漢唐而下英君誼
辟代有作者其功業非不有卓然可觀
也而正心之學亦有庶幾者歟洪惟我
太祖開天立極究心經史評論最爲精確
===
成祖繼天纘緒博極羣書又頒布以廣其傳于
其燦然者觀之洋洋乎皆丕顯之謨也
而本之淵微著之
綸綍以諭宋濂解縉諸臣者卽心學之根極要
領也亦可得而殫述之歟暨我
世宗運際
中興資兼
神聖功業極巍煥之盛制作炳經緯之章夷考
其
punctuated:
第五道

問：先儒有言：「明君以務學爲急，聖學以正心爲要。」是心學之懋，固治業之所由基也。粤自虞庭肇「精一」之傳，而危微之幾始判；孔門衍「誠正」之旨，而慎獨之義斯昭。淵乎聖學宗旨矣！漢、唐而下，英君誼辟代有作者，其功業非不有卓然可觀也，而正心之學亦有庶幾者歟？洪惟我太祖開天立極，究心經史，評論最爲精確；成祖繼天纘緒，博極羣書，又頒布以廣其傳。于其燦然者觀之，洋洋乎皆丕顯之謨也；而本之淵微，著之綸綍，以諭宋濂、解縉諸臣者，卽心學之根極要領也，亦可得而殫述之歟？暨我世宗運際中興，資兼神聖，功業極巍煥之盛，制作炳經緯之章。夷考其
translation_en:
Question Five

Question: A former Confucian scholar once said, "An enlightened ruler takes devoting himself to learning as his urgent priority, and sage learning takes rectifying the mind as its essential point." Thus, the flourishing of the learning of the mind (xinxue) is truly the foundation upon which the enterprise of governance rests. Ever since the court of Yu initiated the transmission of "refinement and singleness" (jingyi), the subtle incipient tendencies of the precarious human mind and the abstruse moral mind were first distinguished; when the school of Confucius elaborated the purport of "making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind" (chengzheng), the meaning of vigilance in solitude (shendu) was thereby made manifest. How profound is the fundamental doctrine of sage learning! From the Han and Tang dynasties onward, heroic rulers and righteous sovereigns arose in every generation. It is not that their achievements and enterprises lacked anything outstanding and worthy of admiration, yet in the learning of rectifying the mind, were there any who came close?

We humbly reflect upon how our Grand Progenitor (Taizu) opened the heavens and established the supreme standard, applying his mind thoroughly to the Classics and Histories, on which his critical assessments were most precise and accurate; and how the Accomplished Progenitor (Chengzu) succeeded to Heaven's mandate and continued the imperial line, reading exhaustively through the multitude of books and furthermore promulgating them to broaden their transmission. Viewed from what is resplendent in them, how vast and magnificent—all are grandly illustrious counsels! Yet as for what is rooted in profound subtlety and set forth in imperial decrees to instruct such ministers as Song Lian 宋濂 and Xie Jin 解縉—these are indeed the fundamental ultimate and essential mainstays of the learning of the mind. Can they also be exhaustively recounted? Coming down to our Epochal Ancestor (Shizong), whose destiny met with dynastic restoration and whose natural endowments combined the divine and the sagely, his achievements and enterprises reached the utmost flourishing of towering brilliance, and his institutions shone with the splendor of warp and woof. If we examine his…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
箴註所謂相授守一道者可備舉而揚厲之
歟其與聖學所以傳心者亦均有合歟
我
皇上英資天縱盛德日新
經筵日講亟懋緝熙
宸翰召詢時勤
眷諭典學之心固烝烝然日之方升也而所以
紹休
祖宗繼統帝王者信在茲歟抑當有進於此者
歟昔漢儒召對三策首正心之條宋儒
告君四字盡平生之學諸士固欲等而
上之也行將効用
===
明時其何所獻以爲
聖學之助乎願敬陳之毋隱
問聖帝明王必登崇儒雋以恢弘化理所
從來遠矣古昔盛時九德咸事士生其
際者類皆瓌偉卓犖而未嘗以儒自命
及考其德業後世卒莫及焉所謂崇本
punctuated:
箴註所謂「相授守一道」者，可備舉而揚厲之歟？其與聖學所以傳心者，亦均有合歟？我皇上英資天縱，盛德日新，經筵日講，亟懋緝熙，宸翰召詢，時勤眷諭，典學之心，固烝烝然日之方升也。而所以紹休祖宗、繼統帝王者，信在茲歟？抑當有進於此者歟？昔漢儒召對三策，首正心之條；宋儒告君四字，盡平生之學。諸士固欲等而上之也，行將効用明時，其何所獻以爲聖學之助乎？願敬陳之，毋隱。

問：聖帝明王必登崇儒雋，以恢弘化理，所從來遠矣。古昔盛時，九德咸事，士生其際者，類皆瓌偉卓犖，而未嘗以儒自命；及考其德業，後世卒莫及焉。所謂崇本
translation_en:
…admonitions and commentaries, where he spoke of “transmitting and guarding one and the same Way”—can these be fully recounted and extolled? And do they all accord equally with that whereby the learning of the sages transmits the mind? Our august Sovereign is endowed by Heaven with heroic talent, and his illustrious virtue is daily renewed. In the Classics Colloquia and Daily Lectures, he earnestly exerts himself in continuous illumination; through imperial brush-notes and summoned inquiries, he is ever diligent in his solicitous instructions. His heart, devoted to constant learning, indeed rises steadily like the ascending sun. Does the means to carry forward the blessings of the Imperial Ancestors and succeed to the lineage of the Emperors and Kings truly lie herein? Or is there something that should advance even beyond this? In former times, when a Han Confucian [Dong Zhongshu] was summoned to reply with three policy essays, he placed the item of rectifying the mind first; when a Song Confucian [Cheng Yi or Zhu Xi / Lu Jiuyuan] counselled his ruler, four characters summed up the learning of his entire life. You gentlemen surely wish to ascend to an even higher plane. As you are soon to render service in this enlightened era, what will you offer up as an aid to the Imperial Sage’s learning? Pray set it forth respectfully, holding nothing back.

Question: That sage emperors and enlightened kings inevitably advance and honor eminent Confucians in order to broaden and magnify transformative governance is a practice of long standing. In the flourishing eras of antiquity, men of the Nine Virtues all served in office. Scholars born in those times were generally extraordinary and preeminent, yet they never styled themselves “Confucians” (ru); when one examines their virtue and achievements, however, later ages ultimately could never match them. What is called “honoring the fundamental…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
之學不假聲稱者非耶周官以九兩繫
萬民儒居其一至與牧長主吏並稱儒
何重也及班氏著九家論乃以儒者與
陰陽墨道槩列又何其泛濫而不經歟
儒行不同仲尼之告魯君者甚悉儒效
至大楊子之述法言者甚詳然其事果
何在而其人果何指歟漢立儒林傳潛
心大業者何以不與唐立儒學傳語本
六經者何以見遺至宋史於儒林之外
===
別爲道學一傳豈儒與道果有二歟得
中原文獻之傳謹屋漏夢寐之際亦一
代碩儒也顧不獲與濂洛關閩諸賢爲
伍何歟我
國家稽古右文名儒輩出其可以範今而傳
後者抑有其人歟邇者文勝質漓名實
易眩儒之以似爲眞者或不能盡無也
諸生潛心儒業其從違固有定向矣幸
詳言之以觀辯志之學
punctuated: 之學，不假聲稱者非耶？《周官》以九兩繫萬民，儒居其一，至與牧、長、主、吏並稱，儒何重也！及班氏著九家論，乃以儒者與陰陽、墨、道槩列，又何其泛濫而不經歟？儒行不同，仲尼之告魯君者甚悉；儒效至大，楊子之述《法言》者甚詳。然其事果何在，而其人果何指歟？漢立《儒林傳》，潛心大業者何以不與？唐立《儒學傳》，語本六經者何以見遺？至《宋史》，於《儒林》之外，別爲《道學》一傳，豈儒與道果有二歟？得中原文獻之傳，謹屋漏夢寐之際，亦一代碩儒也，顧不獲與濂、洛、關、閩諸賢爲伍，何歟？我國家稽古右文，名儒輩出，其可以範今而傳後者，抑有其人歟？邇者文勝質漓，名實易眩，儒之以似爲眞者，或不能盡無也。諸生潛心儒業，其從違固有定向矣，幸詳言之，以觀辯志之學。
translation_en: … learning that values the fundamental does not rely on outward reputation? In the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), "nine bonds" are used to bind the myriad people together, and the Ru (Confucian scholar) occupies one of them, even being named alongside pasturers, chiefs, masters, and officials—how weighty was the Ru! Yet when Ban [Gu] composed his discourse on the Nine Schools, he grouped the Ru indiscriminately alongside the Yin-Yang, Mohist, and Daoist schools—how sweeping and uncanonical was that? The conduct of the Ru varies, as Zhongni [Confucius] explained in great detail to the ruler of Lu; the efficacy of the Ru is supremely great, as Master Yang [Xiong] recounted at length in his Model Sayings (Fayan). Yet wherein do such deeds truly lie, and to whom do such persons actually refer? The Han histories established the "Biographies of Confucian Scholars" (Rulin zhuan), yet why was one who immersed his mind in the Great Enterprise not included? The Tang histories established the "Biographies of Confucian Learning" (Ruxue zhuan), yet why was one whose words were rooted in the Six Classics left out? Coming to the History of the Song (Songshi), apart from the "Confucian Scholars" (Rulin), it created a separate biography for the "Learning of the Way" (Daoxue)—could it be that the Ru and the Way are truly two different things? Those who received the transmission of the cultural heritage of the Central Plains, and those who maintained reverence even in the privacy of their chambers and in their dreams, were also eminent Ru of their generations; why, then, were they not permitted to be ranked alongside the worthies of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min? Our State examines antiquity and esteems civil culture, and renowned Ru have emerged in succession; are there among them individuals who can serve as models for the present and be transmitted to posterity? In recent times, outward refinement has prevailed while substantive quality has grown thin, and name and reality are easily confused; among the Ru, those who mistake the semblance for the real are perhaps not entirely absent. You students have immersed your minds in the Confucian calling, and your choices of what to follow and what to reject surely have a fixed direction. Please speak of this in detail, so that we may observe your learning in discerning ambitions.

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
問書曰監于先王成憲其永無愆言法之
當守也易曰易窮則變變則通言更化
之宜民也蒼姬以前凡家天下者所守
所變載之紀籍班班然可考矣繼是若
漢若唐若宋其始之制作貽謀未必盡
還三代之舊也然傳之後嗣亦有不可
以少變焉者是故三章之法租庸之制
與夫忠厚立國之規其繼體之君循之
者安違之者敝既敝矣即捄以昭宣之
===
君大中元祐之政而皆不能善其後何
歟當其時獻納之臣如賈誼董仲舒李
翺劉蕡余靖宋綬之徒爭上更化善治
之請而霍光魏相陸贄李泌司馬光呂
公著諸賢則皆以成法為當遵此又何
居果先世之所貽本有可繼之道無待
於紛更歟抑易轍改弦勢所必至而召
敝階亂或不善變者之過也我
國家創制立法酌古準今宏綱細目靡不具
punctuated: 問：《書》曰：「監于先王成憲，其永無愆。」言法之當守也。《易》曰：「易窮則變，變則通。」言更化之宜民也。蒼姬以前，凡家天下者，所守所變，載之紀籍，班班然可考矣。繼是若漢、若唐、若宋，其始之制作貽謀，未必盡還三代之舊也，然傳之後嗣，亦有不可以少變焉者。是故三章之法、租庸之制，與夫忠厚立國之規，其繼體之君，循之者安，違之者敝。既敝矣，即捄以昭、宣之君，大中、元祐之政，而皆不能善其後，何歟？當其時，獻納之臣，如賈誼、董仲舒、李翺、劉蕡、余靖、宋綬之徒，爭上更化善治之請；而霍光、魏相、陸贄、李泌、司馬光、呂公著諸賢，則皆以成法為當遵，此又何居？果先世之所貽，本有可繼之道，無待於紛更歟？抑易轍改弦，勢所必至，而召敝階亂，或不善變者之過也？我國家創制立法，酌古準今，宏綱細目，靡不具
translation_en: Question: The Document Classic (Shu) says: "Take as your mirror the established statutes of the former kings, and you will Forever be free from fault"—speaking of how laws ought to be preserved. The Classic of Changes (Yi) says: "When the Changes run their course, there is transformation; through transformation, there is continuity"—speaking of how reforming governance is fitting for the people. Prior to the house of Zhou, for all who ruled the realm as a family patrimony, what they preserved and what they changed are recorded in historical documents and can be clearly examined. Following them, in dynasties such as the Han, the Tang, and the Song, their initial institutions and the counsels handed down to posterity did not necessarily return completely to the old ways of the Three Dynasties; yet when passed down to later heirs, there were also aspects that could not be altered even slightly. Therefore, with the Three-Article Code of the Han, the tax-and-corvée system (zuyong) of the Tang, and the foundational principle of establishing the state upon loyalty and generosity in the Song, when succeeding sovereigns followed them there was stability, and when they departed from them there was decline. Once decline had set in, even when remedied by rulers such as Emperors Zhao and Xuan of the Han, or by the administrations of the Dazhong era in the Tang and the Yuanyou era in the Song, none of them were able to secure a good outcome afterward—why is this? During those times, ministers who offered counsel—such as Jia Yi, Dong Zhongshu, Li Ao, Liu Fen, Yu Jing, and Song Shou—vied in submitting requests to reform and improve governance; whereas worthies such as Huo Guang, Wei Xiang, Lu Zhi, Li Bi, Sima Guang, and Lü Gongzhu all held that the established laws ought to be observed. Why was this so? Was it indeed that what the former generations handed down inherently possessed a Way that could be continued, having no need for tumultuous alterations? Or was it that changing the tracks and restringing the bow was an inevitable trend of circumstances, and that inviting decline and giving rise to disorder was perhaps the fault of those who were not skillful at carrying out change? Our Dynasty, in founding its institutions and establishing its laws, has weighed antiquity and measured the present; of grand principles and fine details, there is nothing not fully…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
備誠軼漢唐宋而過之也二百年來治
久弊乗容有少異其初者而建議之臣
思爲捄偏補敝之策廼稍起而更新之
此其所規畫者甚詳而爲慮至深遠也
顧議論日繁收效則鮮豈奉法者之未
得其人歟抑議法者尚有遺慮歟玆欲
捄今時之弊以復
典章之舊必何如而後可諸士究心世務必
有所槩於中者願明以告我毋徒勦說
===
爲也
問關中古稱百二之國井張炳曜河嶽秘
英其清淑萃之於人是生文武全材之
士若躬耕莘野而一德陳謨垂釣磻溪
而鷹揚爲烈文經武緯猗歟盛矣嗣是
而後有抱文學於西河而人以聖人目
之者有作史記於西京而人以良史稱
之者有爲漢書而討前史之失者有上
書切諫而補時政之缺者有著經傳集
punctuated:
備，誠軼漢、唐、宋而過之也。二百年來，治久弊乗，容有少異其初者，而建議之臣思爲捄偏補敝之策，廼稍起而更新之。此其所規畫者甚詳，而爲慮至深遠也。顧議論日繁，收效則鮮，豈奉法者之未得其人歟？抑議法者尚有遺慮歟？玆欲捄今時之弊，以復典章之舊，必何如而後可？諸士究心世務，必有所槩於中者，願明以告我，毋徒勦說爲也。
問：關中古稱「百二之國」，井、張炳曜，河、嶽秘英，其清淑萃之於人，是生文武全材之士。若躬耕莘野而一德陳謨，垂釣磻溪而鷹揚爲烈，文經武緯，猗歟盛矣！嗣是而後，有抱文學於西河，而人以聖人目之者；有作《史記》於西京，而人以良史稱之者；有爲《漢書》而討前史之失者；有上書切諫而補時政之缺者；有著《經傳集
translation_en:
… complete, truly surpassing and exceeding those of the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties. Over the past two hundred years, as peace has lasted long and abuses have crept in, things have perhaps come to differ slightly from how they were in the beginning; thus, officials offering proposals, thinking to devise measures to rectify imbalances and mend defects, have gradually risen to renew and reform them. What they have planned is very detailed, and their considerations are most deep and far-reaching. Yet discussions grow daily more numerous while results achieved are few. Is it that the right men have not been found to implement the laws? Or is it that those who deliberate on the laws still have oversights in their considerations? If we now wish to remedy the abuses of the present time so as to restore the old state of our foundational institutions and statutes, how must we proceed before this can be achieved? You scholars have devoted your minds to the affairs of the world and must have convictions formed within yourselves; I wish you to tell me clearly, and not merely offer plagiarized clichés.

Question: Guanzhong was in antiquity called the "country where two can match a hundred." The constellations Jing and Zhang shine brightly above it, and the Yellow River and Mount Hua hold secret essence within it; their pure and auspicious ether gathers in people, thereby giving birth to gentlemen of complete civil and military talent. Such were he who plowed in person in the wilds of Shen and set forth counsels on "pure virtue," and he who dangled a fishing line at the Pan Stream and achieved grand exploits like a soaring hawk—forming the civil warp and military woof, how flourishing indeed! Thereafter, there was one who embraced literary learning in Xihe and was regarded by people as a sage; there was one who composed the Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji) in the Western Capital and was praised by people as a good historian; there was one who wrote the History of the Han (Hanshu) and examined the failings of prior histories; there was one who submitted memorials of earnest remonstrance to remedy the deficiencies of current governance; there was one who authored the Collected…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
解而稱爲武庫者有作玄晏春秋而號
爲書窪者有賦月秘書而後主謂謝莊
不得獨美於前者有詠詩杜陵而元稹
謂詩人以來所未有者此皆飛翰茹精
彪炳藝苑以文而鳴當世者也有節儆
雪霜圖形麒麟者有威寒沙漠立功西
域者有輕兵掠敵足澡渭水之恥者有
單騎入壘卒下回紇之拜者有示虜目
中而矍鑠以收交趾之蹟者有運籌幄
===
内而談笑以却澶淵之師者有挺戈擒
敵上書忠勇之旗以褒嘉者有乗電擊
營人望順昌之幟而奔潰者此皆樹節
輸忠鐫銘彝鼎以武而鳴當世者也其
人可悉數歟槩其人而論之亦有高下
之可言歟而其所謂文武者視商周之
佐亦可若是班歟諸士產於是鄉皆儲
文武之材以需
國用者景仰前脩將誰取衷乎顧究言之毋
punctuated: 解》而稱爲「武庫」者，有作《玄晏春秋》而號爲「書淫」者，有賦月秘書而後主謂謝莊不得獨美於前者，有詠詩杜陵而元稹謂詩人以來所未有者，此皆飛翰茹精、彪炳藝苑，以文而鳴當世者也。有節傲雪霜、圖形麒麟者，有威寒沙漠、立功西域者，有輕兵掠敵、足澡渭水之恥者，有單騎入壘、卒下回紇之拜者，有示虜目中、而矍鑠以收交趾之蹟者，有運籌幄内、而談笑以却澶淵之師者，有挺戈擒敵、上書「忠勇」之旗以褒嘉者，有乗電擊營、人望順昌之幟而奔潰者，此皆樹節輸忠、鐫銘彝鼎，以武而鳴當世者也。其人可悉數歟？槩其人而論之，亦有高下之可言歟？而其所謂文武者，視商、周之佐，亦可若是班歟？諸士產於是鄉，皆儲文武之材以需國用者，景仰前脩，將誰取衷乎？顧究言之，毋…
translation_en:
… Collected Explanations (Jingzhuan jijie) and was acclaimed as an "armory" of learning; there was one who wrote the Spring and Autumn Annals of Master Xuanyan (Xuanyan chunqiu) and was dubbed a "book-obsessive" [reading 窪 as 淫]; there was one who composed a rhapsody on the moon in the Palace Library, of whom the Last Ruler (Houzhu) said that Xie Zhuang 謝莊 could no longer claim sole beauty before him; and there was one who chanted poetry in Duling, of whom Yuan Zhen 元稹 said his like had never existed since poets began. All of these plied their brushes and imbibed the essence of learning, shining brightly in the garden of letters and making their mark upon their age through civil letters.

There was one whose integrity defied snow and frost [reading 儆 as 傲], and whose portrait was painted in the Qilin Pavilion; there was one whose might chilled the desert sands and who established merit in the Western Regions; there was one who raided the enemy with light troops, sufficing to wash away the humiliation at the Wei River; there was one who rode alone into the enemy ramparts and ultimately brought the Uighurs to bow in submission; there was one who kept the barbarians within his sights and in hale old age achieved the feat of pacifying Jiaozhi; there was one who devised strategies within the command tent and repelled the enemy host at Chanyuan amid casual talk and laughter; there was one who brandished his spear to capture the foe, upon whose banner the Emperor inscribed "Loyal and Brave" in praise; and there was one who struck the enemy camp like lightning, at the sight of whose banners at Shunchang the enemy routed and fled. All of these upheld integrity and offered up their loyalty, having their names inscribed on sacrificial bronzes and tripods and making their mark upon their age through martial prowess.

Can all of these men be enumerated in full? If we evaluate them as a whole, can distinctions of higher and lower merit be drawn among them? And as for what are here called their civil and martial achievements, how can they be ranked on the same level as those of the great ministers who assisted the Shang and Zhou dynasties? You gentlemen were born in this region and have all cultivated talents both civil and martial to await the state's employment. In looking up to the worthy predecessors of antiquity, whom among them will you take as your standard? Pray set this forth thoroughly, and do not…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
曰方人則不暇也
問書曰惟事事乃其有備有備無患蓋言
豫也昔人謂救荒無奇策固矣然荒匪
救之難而惟豫之貴是故堯之久溢湯
之恒暘當其時未聞有捐瘠之民夫豈
無其道耶至於周代荒政尤詳大司徒
之聚萬民司救之以王命施惠此特救
之有事之日者也而其所以先事爲之
備者如遺人廩人鄉師之所掌又多散
===
見於六屬之中備之豫也如此王制又
謂三年耕必有一年之食九年耕必有
三年之食以三十年之通雖有凶旱水
溢民無菜色夫救荒如周可謂得策矣
但其所謂一年三年之積果何以爲制
置之法而使凶旱水溢之無患耶後之
言荒政者有平糴常平義倉社倉之法
以爲之備而移粟如梁就食如漢助貸
及於相臣廩給徧於郡國降度牒發封
punctuated:
曰「方人則不暇」也。
問：《書》曰：「惟事事，乃其有備，有備無患。」蓋言豫也。昔人謂救荒無奇策，固矣。然荒匪救之難，而惟豫之貴。是故堯之久溢、湯之恒暘，當其時未聞有捐瘠之民，夫豈無其道耶？至於周代，荒政尤詳。大司徒之聚萬民，司救之以王命施惠，此特救之有事之日者也；而其所以先事爲之備者，如遺人、廩人、鄉師之所掌，又多散見於六屬之中，備之豫也如此。《王制》又謂：「三年耕，必有一年之食；九年耕，必有三年之食。以三十年之通，雖有凶旱水溢，民無菜色。」夫救荒如周，可謂得策矣。但其所謂一年、三年之積，果何以爲制置之法，而使凶旱水溢之無患耶？後之言荒政者，有平糴、常平、義倉、社倉之法以爲之備；而移粟如梁，就食如漢，助貸及於相臣，廩給徧於郡國，降度牒、發封
translation_en:
… say, "As for comparing people, I have no leisure for that."

Question: The Book of Documents (Shu) says, "Only by attending to every matter will there be preparation; with preparation, there is no calamity." This speaks of precautions taken in advance. Men of the past said that for famine relief there is no miraculous policy—this is certainly true. Yet with famine, it is not relieving it that is difficult, but rather advance preparation that is valuable. Therefore, during the prolonged floods under Yao and the persistent droughts under Tang, at those times one never heard of people being abandoned or emaciated; how could this have been without a proper method? Coming to the Zhou dynasty, famine relief administration was especially detailed. The Grand Minister of Education (da situ) gathering the myriad people, and the Corrector of Public Evil (sijiu) bestowing relief by royal command—these were merely measures for providing relief on the day an emergency occurred. Yet the means by which they made preparations beforehand—such as the duties under the charge of the Granary Provisioner (weiren), the Storekeeper (linren), and the Township Preceptor (xiangshi)—furthermore appear scattered throughout the six ministries; such was the thoroughness of their advance preparation! The Royal Regulations (Wangzhi) also states: "With three years of plowing, there must be one year's food saved; with nine years of plowing, there must be three years' food saved. Taking the average of a thirty-year period, even if there are disastrous droughts or floods, the people will not have the famished complexion of those eating only wild greens." Now, famine relief such as that of the Zhou can indeed be called having obtained the right policy. However, regarding what it calls the surpluses of one year and three years, by what method of institutional arrangement were these actually achieved so as to ensure that disastrous droughts and floods caused no calamity? Among those in later times who discussed famine relief administration, there were the methods of equitable grain purchasing (pingdi), ever-normal granaries (changping), charitable granaries (yicang), and community granaries (shecang) to serve as preparations; and there were also measures such as transferring grain as in the state of Liang, moving the population to where food was available as in the Han dynasty, calling upon chief ministers for aid and loans, distributing grain rations throughout the commanderies and principalities, issuing ordination certificates, and opening the reserved treasuries (feng…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
椿諸所設施視周窔若而行之當時亦
不知實有益於濟荒否也邇者臺臣上
言司農覆奏欲脩舉
國初建倉之制而責成守令量里積穀其於
古昔預備之法同與否與備荒之政邦
國首務誠不可諉之無策者諸生挾策
而來願以其素所講求者而著之於篇
punctuated: 椿，諸所設施，視周窔若？而行之當時，亦不知實有益於濟荒否也。邇者臺臣上言，司農覆奏，欲脩舉國初建倉之制，而責成守令，量里積穀，其於古昔預備之法，同與否與？備荒之政，邦國首務，誠不可諉之無策者。諸生挾策而來，願以其素所講求者，而著之於篇。
translation_en:
… reserved treasury funds [fengzhuang; here written 椿 for 樁]—how do all these measures compare with those of the Zhou [note: 窔 appears to be a graphic error for 奚, "how"]? Moreover, when they were put into practice in their own times, one does not know whether they were truly of benefit in relieving famine or not.

Recently, censorial officials submitted a memorial and the Ministry of Revenue responded in a follow-up memorial, wishing to revive and implement the system of establishing granaries from the founding of our Dynasty, and to hold prefects and magistrates responsible for storing grain in proportion to the size of the rural communities (li). Is this identical to or different from the methods of advance preparation in antiquity? The administration of famine preparedness is the foremost task of the state, and truly one cannot shirk it by claiming there is no strategy. You students have come bearing your texts; I hope you will set forth in your essays what you have long studied and investigated.

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
夫子焉不學而亦何常師之有
趙爾守
同考試官教諭阮　批〔子貢形容聖人學無常師語意〕
〔極爲圓活此作體認精到而詞亦足以發之是可式矣〕
同考試官教諭何　批〔發聖人無學無不學無師無不〕
〔師處詞不費而理自躍如是善作者〕
考試官學正宋　批〔精邃雅馴錄之〕
===
考試官教授劉　批〔詞旨渾融〕
聖人不專於學而亦不專於師也葢聖人之所
學者道也道無不在而學因之矣又何泥於師
哉子貢之曉公孫朝也意曰斯道隨寓而各足
聖心體道而不遺夫子之學得統於文武者也
子疑其焉學將謂其有專師矣豈知其天縱之
資雖不假於學習而斯道之未墜者莫非憲章
之所稽生知之質雖不藉於見聞而文獻之足
徵者要皆敏求之所及道有識其大者焉則於

「夫子焉不學，而亦何常師之有？」

趙爾守

同考試官教諭阮批：〔子貢形容聖人學無常師，語意極爲圓活。此作體認精到，而詞亦足以發之，是可式矣。〕

同考試官教諭何批：〔發聖人無學無不學、無師無不師處，詞不費而理自躍如，是善作者。〕

考試官學正宋批：〔精邃雅馴，錄之。〕

考試官教授劉批：〔詞旨渾融。〕

聖人不專於學，而亦不專於師也。葢聖人之所學者，道也；道無不在，而學因之矣，又何泥於師哉？子貢之曉公孫朝也，意曰：斯道隨寓而各足，聖心體道而不遺。夫子之學，得統於文、武者也。子疑其焉學，將謂其有專師矣。豈知其天縱之資，雖不假於學習，而斯道之未墜者，莫非憲章之所稽；生知之質，雖不藉於見聞，而文獻之足徵者，要皆敏求之所及。道有識其大者焉，則於
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

"Where does our Master not learn? And yet what regular teacher does he have?"

Zhao Ershou 趙爾守

Associate Examiner and Instructor Ruan 阮 comments: [Zigong 子貢 describes the Sage as learning without having a regular teacher; the sense of his words is exceedingly rounded and lively. This composition grasps the point with precision and depth, and its phrasing is fully equal to bringing it out—it may serve as a model.]

Associate Examiner and Instructor He 何 comments: [In bringing out how the Sage has nothing to learn and yet nothing from which he does not learn, no teacher and yet no one who is not his teacher, the wording is not wasteful while the principle leaps vividly into view. This is a skillful writer.]

Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Song 宋 comments: [Refined, profound, elegant, and well-ordered; record it for printing.]

Examiner and Prefectural Instructor Liu 劉 comments: [The diction and purport are harmoniously blended.]

The Sage does not confine himself to any one object of learning, nor does he confine himself to any one teacher. For what the Sage learns is the Way; the Way is present everywhere, and his learning follows accordingly—how then could he be bound to any particular teacher? When Zigong enlightened Gongsun Chao 公孫朝, his meaning was this: This Way is complete in itself wherever it resides, and the Sage's mind embodies the Way without omitting anything. Our Master's learning received the line of transmission from Kings Wen 文 and Wu 武. When you ask from whom he learned, you suppose that he had a single, dedicated teacher. How could you know that, although with his Heaven-endowed gifts he has no need to rely on study and practice, yet so long as this Way has not fallen to the ground, all of it is what he investigates in modeling himself upon the ancients; and although with his innate knowledge he does not depend on what is seen and heard, yet wherever documents and worthy men suffice for verification, all of them are reached by his earnest seeking? Where the great principles of the Way are remembered, then from…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
賢者學之矣而散殊之用亦博觀以究其極學
固不專於賢也道有識其小者焉則於不賢者
學之矣而統體之大又多識以會其全亦不專
於不賢也是其虛受以爲心凡道之所在卽學
也孰得其淵源之所自樂取以爲善凡學之所
在皆師也孰知其統緒之攸傳道之屬於人也
無窮而兼體之志亦無窮師其道不泥其迹則
或大或小皆聖學之相承也亦何嘗有專承乎
哉人之寄乎道也無常而主善之師亦無常惟
===
其道不惟其人則賢與不賢皆聖心之翕受也
亦何嘗有專受乎哉要之夫子未嘗不學而亦
未始有定學也故夫子雖無所不師而實未嘗
有所師也焉學之疑淺之乎其觀聖人者矣嘗
謂千聖一心萬古一道文武之統紹自禹湯而
亦臨亦保不泄不忘則固以心爲師者也豈假
於人哉孔子曰文不在玆乎蓋其道固文武之
道則其心亦文武之心此之謂能自得師也善
學聖人者卽是求之有餘師矣
punctuated: 賢者學之矣，而散殊之用亦博觀以究其極，學固不專於賢也。道有識其小者焉，則於不賢者學之矣，而統體之大又多識以會其全，亦不專於不賢也。是其虛受以爲心，凡道之所在，卽學也，孰得其淵源之所自？樂取以爲善，凡學之所在，皆師也，孰知其統緒之攸傳？道之屬於人也無窮，而兼體之志亦無窮。師其道，不泥其迹，則或大或小，皆聖學之相承也，亦何嘗有專承乎哉？人之寄乎道也無常，而主善之師亦無常。惟其道，不惟其人，則賢與不賢，皆聖心之翕受也，亦何嘗有專受乎哉？要之，夫子未嘗不學，而亦未始有定學也。故夫子雖無所不師，而實未嘗有所師也。「焉學」之疑，淺之乎其觀聖人者矣！嘗謂千聖一心，萬古一道。文、武之統紹自禹、湯，而亦臨亦保，不泄不忘，則固以心爲師者也，豈假於人哉？孔子曰：「文不在玆乎？」蓋其道固文、武之道，則其心亦文、武之心，此之謂能自得師也。善學聖人者，卽是求之，有餘師矣。
translation_en:
… he learns it from the worthy; yet as for its dispersed and varied applications, he also observes them broadly so as to exhaust their utmost limits—so his learning certainly is not confined exclusively to the worthy. As for the Way having those who remember its lesser principles, he learns it from the unworthy; yet as for the greatness of its overarching whole, he also remembers much so as to synthesize its entirety—so it is not confined exclusively to the unworthy either.

Thus, making open-minded receptivity his mind, wherever the Way resides is his learning; who can fathom the source from which it originates? Delighting in adopting from others in order to do good, wherever learning resides is his teacher; who can know how its lineage is transmitted? The lodging of the Way among men is inexhaustible, and the resolve to embody it comprehensively is likewise inexhaustible. Taking the Way as one's teacher without clinging to its outward traces, whether great or small, all are the continuous inheritance of sagely learning—how could there ever be an exclusive succession? The manner in which men lodge themselves in the Way is inconstant, and the teacher who makes goodness his master is likewise inconstant. Looking only to the Way and not to the person, both the worthy and the unworthy are gathered and received into the sage's mind—how could there ever be an exclusive reception?

In sum, the Master never fails to learn, yet he has never had a fixed object of learning. Therefore, although there is nothing the Master does not take as his teacher, in reality he has no specific teacher. How shallow in observing the sage was the doubt asking, "Where did he learn?"

It has been said that a thousand sages share a single mind, and ten thousand ages share a single Way. The succession of Kings Wen and Wu was continued from Yu and Tang; ever watchful as if Approaching, ever preserving, neither neglecting nor forgetting, they certainly took their own minds as their teacher—how could they need to borrow from others? Confucius said, "Is not the culture (wen) lodged here in me?" Indeed, since his Way is certainly the Way of Kings Wen and Wu, his mind is likewise the mind of Kings Wen and Wu. This is what is meant by being able to find a teacher in oneself. For those who are good at learning from the sage, if they simply seek it right here, they will find more than enough teachers.

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
見而民莫不敬言而民莫不信行而民莫
不說是以聲名洋溢乎中國施及蠻貊
馮祥
同考試官教諭唐　批〔中庸義不難於騁詞而難於說理此篇甚有體貼而過接處識見筆力俱到必學有本源者錄之〕
同考試官教諭賓　批〔聖德時出感民而聲名之達因之非有二理是作最爲得旨且結出聖人神化配天尤有獨見〕
考試官學正宋　批〔氣格昌大詞理精純〕
考試官教授劉　批〔典麗有雋味〕
===
聖德各當乎民心而譽自達於中外焉甚矣譽
之因於民心也聖德之發見者當其心矣而譽
之隆也固宜中庸之言天道也蓋曰至聖以生
知而備四德其充積者既極夫天淵之盛矣而
發見之妙何如哉是故時出之而爲見一德輝
之動也而瞻大觀之度者咸起夫欽崇之念民
孰有不敬者乎時出之而爲言一德音之昭也
而仰巽命之申者咸致夫尊從之願民孰有不
信者乎時出之而爲行一德行之敷也而覩藝
punctuated:
「見而民莫不敬，言而民莫不信，行而民莫不說。是以聲名洋溢乎中國，施及蠻貊。」
馮祥
同考試官教諭唐　批：〔《中庸》義不難於騁詞，而難於說理。此篇甚有體貼，而過接處識見、筆力俱到，必學有本源者，錄之。〕
同考試官教諭賓　批：〔聖德時出感民，而聲名之達因之，非有二理。是作最爲得旨，且結出聖人神化配天，尤有獨見。〕
考試官學正宋　批：〔氣格昌大，詞理精純。〕
考試官教授劉　批：〔典麗有雋味。〕

聖德各當乎民心，而譽自達於中外焉。甚矣，譽之因於民心也！聖德之發見者當其心矣，而譽之隆也固宜。《中庸》之言天道也，蓋曰：至聖以生知而備四德，其充積者既極夫天淵之盛矣，而發見之妙何如哉？是故時出之而爲見，一德輝之動也，而瞻大觀之度者，咸起夫欽崇之念，民孰有不敬者乎？時出之而爲言，一德音之昭也，而仰巽命之申者，咸致夫尊從之願，民孰有不信者乎？時出之而爲行，一德行之敷也，而覩藝
translation_en:
"Therefore, whenever he appears, the people all revere him; whenever he speaks, the people all believe him; whenever he acts, the people are all pleased with him. Thus his fame and name overflow the Middle Kingdom and extend to the southern and northern barbarians."

Feng Xiang 馮祥

Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Tang 唐 comments: [In essays on the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), the difficulty lies not in giving rein to rhetoric, but in explaining moral principle. This piece shows deep empathy with the text, and at the transitions both insight and brushwork fully hit the mark. He must be someone whose learning has a true source; I select it for inclusion.]
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Bin 賓 comments: [The sage's virtue comes forth at the right time to move the people, and the spread of his fame and name follows from this—there are no two separate principles. This composition best grasps the main purport, and in concluding by bringing out how the sage's marvelous transformation matches Heaven, it shows especially original insight.]
Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Song 宋 comments: [Its spirit and structure are grand and flourishing; its diction and reasoning are refined and pure.]
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Liu 劉 comments: [Classically elegant, with a lingering, rich flavor.]

When the sage's virtues each accord with the minds of the people, his renown naturally reaches both within and without. How profound it is that renown arises from the minds of the people! Once the manifestations of the sage's virtue accord with their minds, it is only fitting that his renown should be so exalted. In speaking of the Way of Heaven, the Doctrine of the Mean says, in effect: The supreme sage, through innate knowledge, is endowed with the four virtues. What is stored up within him has already reached the utmost fullness of the heavens and the abyss; how marvelous, then, is its manifestation! Therefore, when he brings it forth at the proper time and appears before them, it is wholly the movement of his virtuous radiance; and all who gaze upon the bearing of his great presence are stirred with thoughts of reverence and veneration—who among the people would not revere him? When he brings it forth at the proper time in speech, it is wholly the shining forth of his virtuous voice; and all who look up to the proclamation of his gentle commands render their wish to honor and obey—who among the people would not believe him? When he brings it forth at the proper time in action, it is wholly the spreading abroad of his virtuous conduct; and all who behold the setting forth of his…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
極之陳者咸興夫媢嫉之忱又孰有不說者乎
斯則聖德之覃敷皆人心也人心之協應皆聲
名也是以衆志潛孚於無間而聲聞具達自妙
乎風動之神羣情允洽於大同而名譽孔彰自
昭夫暨及之化內而中國則洋溢焉被德既深
而誦德益切即其敬信說之情莫不曰此其明
明之天子乎而順治者有同心矣外而蠻貊亦
施及焉去聖雖遠而慕聖則同聞其敬信說之
風莫不曰此其中國之聖人乎而望治者爲無
===
外矣是其發見之當可也既以昭充積之盛而
其聲名之遠被也益以驗發見之時所謂配天
者亦在是矣非至聖其孰能之雖然至聖固有
同於天矣然維天之命於穆不已而至聖之聲
名此又何以稱歟要之可得而名者化天之道
也不可得而名者神天之德也昔夫子贊堯之
無能名也而可見者惟巍然煥然焉然則發見
之時聲名之著無亦成功文章之盛乎此堯之
所以則天而爲聖之至者歟
punctuated: 極之陳者，咸興夫媢嫉之忱，又孰有不說者乎？斯則聖德之覃敷，皆人心也；人心之協應，皆聲名也。是以衆志潛孚於無間，而聲聞具達，自妙乎風動之神；羣情允洽於大同，而名譽孔彰，自昭夫暨及之化。內而中國，則洋溢焉；被德既深，而誦德益切，即其敬信說之情，莫不曰：「此其明明之天子乎！」而順治者有同心矣。外而蠻貊，亦施及焉；去聖雖遠，而慕聖則同，聞其敬信說之風，莫不曰：「此其中國之聖人乎！」而望治者爲無外矣。是其發見之當可也，既以昭充積之盛；而其聲名之遠被也，益以驗發見之時。所謂「配天」者，亦在是矣。非至聖，其孰能之？雖然，至聖固有同於天矣；然「維天之命，於穆不已」，而至聖之聲名，此又何以稱歟？要之，可得而名者，化天之道也；不可得而名者，神天之德也。昔夫子贊堯之無能名也，而可見者，惟巍然、煥然焉。然則發見之時，聲名之著，無亦成功文章之盛乎？此堯之所以則天，而爲聖之至者歟！
translation_en: … the setting forth of the standard and norm are all stirred with feelings of affectionate devotion [reading 媚茲 for 媢嫉][?]; and who among them would not rejoice? Thus, wherever the sage's virtue spreads widely, it reaches the hearts of the people; and wherever the hearts of the people respond in harmony, it becomes his fame and renown. Therefore, the minds of the multitude are silently won over without a gap, and as his reputation reaches everywhere, it naturally manifests the marvelous power of moving like the wind; the feelings of the masses are truly harmonized in great unity, and as his renown becomes brightly evident, it naturally illuminates a transforming influence that extends to all. Within, it overflows throughout the Central Kingdom: having received his virtue deeply, they praise his virtue all the more earnestly, and from their feelings of reverence, trust, and joy, there is none who does not say, "Is this not our sagely and illustrious Son of Heaven?"—and those who submit to his rule are of one mind. Without, it extends even to the Man and Mo tribes: though far removed from the sage, they are the same in longing for him, and hearing the wind of that reverence, trust, and joy, there is none who does not say, "Is this not the Sage of the Central Kingdom?"—and among those who look for good governance, none is left outside. Thus, the timeliness of his manifestation already reveals the fullness of his inner accumulation, while the far-reaching spread of his fame further verifies the timeliness of his manifestation. What is called "matching Heaven" also lies precisely in this. Who other than the Supreme Sage could be capable of it? Even so, the Supreme Sage is indeed one with Heaven; yet "the Ordinance of Heaven, how profound is its unceasingness!"—how then is the fame and name of the Supreme Sage to be spoken of here? In sum, what can be named is the Way of transforming like Heaven; what cannot be named is the Virtue of being unfathomable like Heaven. Of old, when the Master praised Yao as being beyond all naming, what could be seen was only his towering grandeur in achievements and his brilliant splendor in cultural patterns. Then is not the prominence of fame at the time of manifestation simply the flourishing of his achievements and cultural patterns? Is this not whereby Yao modeled himself on Heaven and became the ultimate of sages?

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
孟子曰仁言不如仁聲之入人深也善政
不如善敎之得民也善政民畏之善敎
民愛之善政得民財善敎得民心
趙完
同考試官教諭何　批〔兩不如處最難發揮善政下四句尤易纏擾思精理瑩爽健數語而義旨淵涵者僅見此篇〕
同考試官教諭賓　批〔峻整中有溫潤簡勁中寓華藻〕
考試官學正宋　批〔婉悉得旨一結尤見言外之意時義之不多得者〕
考試官教授劉　批〔雅練之文〕
===
治道之感人者不同而其應因之矣甚矣民情
係於所感也觀於聲教而其得民者深矣豈言
與政所可及哉孟子之意蓋曰王道貴於得民
人心徵於類應爲治者盍亦愼所以感之者乎
彼人君以仁育天下則仁言仁聲均之足以入
人也然感人以言者僅足以動乎其聽而未必
能洽乎其衷空言之徒施固不若實德之下究
矣而孰與夫仁聲之入人深也人君以善養天
punctuated:
孟子曰：「仁言不如仁聲之入人深也，善政不如善敎之得民也。善政，民畏之；善敎，民愛之。善政得民財，善敎得民心。」
趙完
同考試官教諭何　批〔兩「不如」處最難發揮，「善政」下四句尤易纏擾。思精理瑩，爽健數語而義旨淵涵者，僅見此篇。〕
同考試官教諭賓　批〔峻整中有溫潤，簡勁中寓華藻。〕
考試官學正宋　批〔婉悉得旨，一結尤見言外之意，時義之不多得者。〕
考試官教授劉　批〔雅練之文。〕
治道之感人者不同，而其應因之矣。甚矣，民情係於所感也！觀於聲、教，而其得民者深矣，豈言與政所可及哉？孟子之意，蓋曰：王道貴於得民，人心徵於類應，爲治者盍亦愼所以感之者乎？彼人君以仁育天下，則仁言、仁聲均之足以入人也。然感人以言者，僅足以動乎其聽，而未必能洽乎其衷；空言之徒施，固不若實德之下究矣，而孰與夫仁聲之入人深也？人君以善養天
translation_en:
Mencius said: "Benevolent words do not penetrate people as deeply as a reputation for benevolence. Good governance does not win the people as well as good instruction. Good governance makes the people fear it; good instruction makes the people love it. Good governance wins the people's wealth; good instruction wins the people's hearts."

Zhao Wan 趙完

Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies He 何 comments: [The two "not as good as" comparisons are the most difficult to elaborate upon, and the four clauses beginning with "Good governance" are especially easy to get tangled up in. Only in this essay does one see such precise thought and pellucid principle, conveying deep and rich meaning within a few brisk, vigorous sentences.]

Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Bin 賓 comments: [Within its austere structure there is warmth and grace; within its concise vigor there resides ornate elegance.]

Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Song 宋 comments: [Nuanced and thorough in grasping the main purport. The conclusion especially reveals implications beyond the words themselves—a rare achievement among contemporary expository essays.]

Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Liu 劉 comments: [A refined and polished essay.]

The ways by which modes of governance move people differ, and the responses they elicit follow accordingly. Profound indeed is the degree to which the sentiments of the people depend upon what moves them! When we observe reputation for benevolence and good instruction, how deeply they win over the people—how could mere words and governance ever match them? Mencius's meaning is roughly this: The Kingly Way prizes winning the people, and human hearts are verified by how they respond in kind; why, then, do those who govern not take care in the means by which they move them?

When a ruler nurtures the world with benevolence, both benevolent words and a reputation for benevolence are alike sufficient to reach into people. Yet moving people through words is only enough to stir their hearing, and cannot necessarily permeate their innermost hearts. The mere dispensation of empty words is certainly no match for substantial virtue reaching down to the lowest levels—how can it compare to a reputation for benevolence penetrating people so deeply? When a ruler nourishes the world with goodness…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
下則善政善敎均之可以得民也然道民以政
者能率於法之所及而不能率於法之所不及
外以嚴其防固不若内以一其志矣而孰與夫
善敎之得民也然政之所以不如敎者何哉蓋
政所以彰紀法也法立而民不犯不過致其畏
焉耳至於善敎則惠德所孚民情其大順焉孔
邇以致其懷固有愛之而不忍離者矣而奚止
於畏也哉政所以定經制也制定而用不匱不
過得民財焉耳至於善敎則道化所洽民志其
===
允孚焉好義以終其事固有維之而不可解者
矣而奚止於得財也哉夫使民之畏也不若使
民之愛况愛之而未有不畏者乎得民之財也
不若得民之心况民聚而財未有不聚者乎信
乎善政之不如善敎而仁言仁聲可例見矣雖
然人君一心萬化從出心苟純矣則皇極敷言
德惟善政其所以感民者與聲敎奚異哉不然
卽仁聞具達庠序弦歌亦驩虞粉飾之具耳於
治化又何裨也故曰王道本於誠意君人者尚
punctuated: 下，則善政、善敎均之可以得民也。然道民以政者，能率於法之所及，而不能率於法之所不及；外以嚴其防，固不若内以一其志矣，而孰與夫善敎之得民也？然政之所以不如敎者，何哉？蓋政所以彰紀法也，法立而民不犯，不過致其畏焉耳。至於善敎，則惠德所孚，民情其大順焉；孔邇以致其懷，固有愛之而不忍離者矣，而奚止於畏也哉？政所以定經制也，制定而用不匱，不過得民財焉耳。至於善敎，則道化所洽，民志其允孚焉；好義以終其事，固有維之而不可解者矣，而奚止於得財也哉？夫使民之畏也，不若使民之愛，况愛之而未有不畏者乎？得民之財也，不若得民之心，况民聚而財未有不聚者乎？信乎善政之不如善敎，而仁言、仁聲可例見矣。雖然，人君一心，萬化從出。心苟純矣，則皇極敷言，德惟善政，其所以感民者，與聲敎奚異哉？不然，卽仁聞具達，庠序弦歌，亦驩虞粉飾之具耳，於治化又何裨也？故曰：王道本於誠意。君人者，尚…
translation_en:
… [When a ruler nourishes All-under-]Heaven [with goodness], then both good government and good instruction are equally capable of winning the people. Yet guiding the people with government can make them comply where the law reaches, but cannot make them comply where the law does not reach; strictly enforcing restraints on the outside is certainly not as good as unifying their wills on the inside—how can it compare with good instruction in winning the people?

Yet why is it that government is not as good as instruction? It is because government is that by which discipline and laws are made manifest; when laws are established and the people do not violate them, it merely brings about their fear and nothing more. As for good instruction, where benevolent virtue inspires trust, the feelings of the people become greatly compliant; feeling the ruler's nearness and cherishing him, they truly love him and cannot bear to leave him—how could it stop merely at fear? Government is that by which regular institutions are settled; when institutions are settled and resources are not lacking, it merely obtains the people's wealth and nothing more. As for good instruction, where moral transformation imbues them, the wills of the people are genuinely won over; delighting in righteousness so as to bring their affairs to completion, they are bound by ties that cannot be undone—how could it stop merely at obtaining wealth?

Now, making the people fear is not as good as making the people love—how much more so when there has never been a case of loving without also fearing! Obtaining the people's wealth is not as good as obtaining the people's hearts—how much more so when the people gather and there has never been a case of wealth not also gathering! Truly, good government is not as good as good instruction, and the case of benevolent words and a reputation for benevolence can be seen by analogy.

Even so, the ruler's one mind is the source from which all transformations issue. If his mind is pure, then the August Ultimate spreads forth its words and virtue is manifested in good government—how would the way these move the people differ at all from a reputation for benevolence and good instruction? Otherwise, even if a reputation for benevolence reaches everywhere and the music of stringed instruments and singing fills the local schools, these are merely the instruments of superficial joy and cosmetic adornment—what benefit are they to governing transformation? Therefore it is said: The Kingly Way is rooted in making the intentions sincere. May he who rules over men…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
亦求端於心哉
易
大君之宜行中之謂也
雷大道

考試官學正宋　批〔意精詞雅〕
考試官教授劉　批〔深純得旨〕
===
論人君之當務惟在於任賢而已蓋中道莫要
於任賢也以是行之之謂非大君之當務者哉且
夫人君之臨天下得其道則用天下而有餘不
得其道則爲天下用而不足茲周公繫六五之
辭曰大君之宜者豈徒以崇高富貴足以宰制
天下而已乎亦豈以才術智力足以服役斯民
而已乎必其執簡以御煩能先乎識體之治守
約以該博適得乎當務之圖者而果何在哉亦
punctuated:
亦求端於心哉！

易
《大君之宜，行中之謂也。》
雷大道

同考試官教諭唐　批〔行中義於任賢見之，場中作者率語涉迂泛，此篇體認真切，可以式矣。〕

論人君之當務，惟在於任賢而已。蓋中道莫要於任賢也，以是行之之謂，非大君之當務者哉？且夫人君之臨天下，得其道則用天下而有餘，不得其道則爲天下用而不足。茲周公繫六五之辭曰「大君之宜」者，豈徒以崇高富貴足以宰制天下而已乎？亦豈以才術智力足以服役斯民而已乎？必其執簡以御煩，能先乎識體之治；守約以該博，適得乎當務之圖者，而果何在哉？亦
translation_en:
… likewise seek the starting point in his own mind!

Book of Changes (Yi)
"What is fitting for the great ruler is what is meant by practicing the mean."
Lei Dadao 雷大道

Associate Examiner, County Director of Studies Tang 唐 comments: [The meaning of "practicing the mean" is seen in employing the worthy. Writers in the examination hall generally used roundabout and vague language, whereas this essay shows genuine and earnest comprehension and can serve as a model.]
Associate Examiner, County Director of Studies Ruan 阮 comments: [This topic reveals the mean through employing the worthy, and reveals what is fitting through practicing the mean; it is most difficult to elaborate upon. This composition goes straight to the crux of the matter, and its diction is moreover lucid and fluent. Selected for inclusion.]
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Song 宋 comments: [The ideas are refined and the diction is elegant.]
Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Liu 劉 comments: [Profound, pure, and grasping the essential purport.]

In discussing the proper duty of a ruler of men, it lies solely in employing the worthy and nothing more. Indeed, in the Way of the Mean nothing is more essential than employing the worthy; is not practicing it in this manner what is meant by the proper duty of a great ruler? Moreover, when a ruler of men presides over All under Heaven, if he grasps the proper Way, he utilizes All under Heaven with capacity to spare; if he fails to grasp the proper Way, he is utilized by All under Heaven and falls short. Now, when the Duke of Zhou appended the judgment to the Six in the Fifth place saying, "What is fitting for the great ruler," was it merely that exalted rank and wealth and honor suffice to govern All under Heaven? Or was it merely that talent, statecraft, wisdom, and strength suffice to command the service of these people? Surely it means holding to simplicity in order to govern complexity, being able to put first the governance that understands fundamental principles; and cleaving to what is essential in order to encompass what is broad, thereby hitting upon the plan for what is most urgent. title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
曰行中之謂耳蓋道之所貴者中之所貴者
任賢也自用則小旣溺於所私而偏聽則蔽又
不知所擇謂之行中則未也六五以柔中而應
剛中知虛已來天下之善中之所在也樂取以
大其公而恒持乎勿貳之念謂純心用天下之
賢即所謂中也翕受以弘其度而不參以有我
之私以溥咨保之澤賢者之養道可行也禮隆
於晉接而信之專任之篤養其賢以及於民焉
爲天下而得人君道其有不宜耶以敷敎思之
===
功賢者之敎道可行也敬篤於乎嘉而言必聽
諫必行用其中以達於民焉急親賢以爲務治
道孰大於是耶是其始也以已之中任乎賢而
中之體已立其旣也取人之中達乎治而中之
用以行此六五之知臨而夫子申之非以立君
道之極乎大抵中之爲道也無不該而施之用
賢也爲甚切四岳之舉五臣之任在唐虞獨際
其盛者而其相傳不過曰允執厥中而已中固
所以爲賢也大哉君哉之稱無亦大君之宜歟
punctuated: 曰「行中之謂」耳。蓋道之所貴者，中；之所貴者，任賢也。自用則小，旣溺於所私；而偏聽則蔽，又不知所擇，謂之行中則未也。六五以柔中而應剛中，知虛已來天下之善，中之所在也。樂取以大其公，而恒持乎勿貳之念，謂純心用天下之賢，即所謂中也。翕受以弘其度，而不參以有我之私。以溥咨保之澤，賢者之養道可行也。禮隆於晉接，而信之專、任之篤，養其賢以及於民焉。爲天下而得人，君道其有不宜耶？以敷敎思之功，賢者之敎道可行也。敬篤於乎嘉，而言必聽、諫必行，用其中以達於民焉。急親賢以爲務，治道孰大於是耶？是其始也，以已之中任乎賢，而中之體已立；其旣也，取人之中達乎治，而中之用以行。此六五之「知臨」，而夫子申之，非以立君道之極乎？大抵中之爲道也，無不該，而施之用賢也爲甚切。四岳之舉、五臣之任，在唐虞獨際其盛者，而其相傳不過曰「允執厥中」而已。中固所以爲賢也，「大哉」、「君哉」之稱，無亦「大君之宜」歟？
translation_en: … Simply: “This means practicing the Mean.” For what the Way values is the Mean, and what the Mean [?] values is employing the worthy. If one relies only on oneself, one becomes petty, already mired in selfish partiality; and if one listens only to one side, one becomes deluded, not knowing how to choose—this cannot yet be called practicing the Mean. The Six in the Fifth place, possessing yielding centrality and responding to firm centrality, knows to empty the self in order to attract the goodness of the world; therein lies the Mean. Gladly drawing upon others to enlarge his impartiality, and constantly maintaining an undivided mind—employing the worthies of the world with a pure heart—is precisely what is called the Mean. Broadly receiving others to expand his magnanimity, he does not mix in the selfishness of personal ego. By extending the bounty of consultation and protection, the worthy’s way of nourishing the people can be put into practice. When courtesy is exalted in granting audiences, and when he trusts them exclusively and employs them earnestly, he nourishes the worthy so that the benefit reaches the people. Obtaining the right men for the sake of the world—how could the Way of the Ruler not be fitting? By spreading the achievements of thoughtful instruction, the worthy’s way of educating the people can be put into practice. When respect is earnestly grounded in sincere appreciation [? 孚嘉], so that their words are always heeded and their remonstrances always acted upon, he uses their Mean to reach the people. Making intimacy with the worthy one’s urgent priority—what principle of governance is greater than this? Thus in the beginning, through the Mean within oneself one employs the worthy, and the substance of the Mean is already established; thereafter, one adopts the Mean of others to achieve good governance, and the function of the Mean is thereby carried out. This is the “wise approach” (zhi lin 知臨) of the Six in the Fifth place, and when the Master expounded upon it, was it not to establish the ultimate standard of the Way of the Ruler? Generally speaking, the Mean as a Way encompasses everything, yet when applied to employing the worthy it is most pertinent. The recommendations of the Four Peaks and the appointment of the Five Ministers reached their unique flourishing in the eras of Tang (Yao) and Yu (Shun), yet what they transmitted to one another was nothing more than “Sincerely hold fast the Mean.” The Mean is indeed that whereby one treats the worthy; are not the praises “Great indeed!” and “A true ruler indeed!” also what is meant by “fitting for a great ruler” …

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
周子曰純心要矣用賢急焉欲法堯舜者必知
所從事而後可
六爻之動三極之道也是故君子所居而
安者易之序也所樂而玩者爻之辭也
是故君子居則觀其象而玩其辭動則
觀其變而玩其占是以自天祐之吉无
不利
馮祥

===
同考試官教諭阮　批〔君子成位乎中乃題本旨此作　得之宜錄以式〕
考試官學正宋　批〔體裁簡當〕
考試官教授劉　批〔整潔〕
大傳論易具乎至理因表學易者之得天也夫
易通乎三極而皆天之理也君子盡學易之功
寧不爲天之所祐哉大傳之意蓋以聖人之作
易流通於三極而貫徹於身心者也兼體之者
punctuated:
周子曰：「純心要矣，用賢急焉。」欲法堯、舜者，必知所從事而後可。

「六爻之動，三極之道也。是故君子所居而安者，易之序也；所樂而玩者，爻之辭也。是故君子居則觀其象而玩其辭，動則觀其變而玩其占，是以『自天祐之，吉无不利』。」

馮祥
同考試官教諭唐批：〔三極屬之君子，此心易也，非造其奧者未易語此。此作詞約義該，精藴具見，殆不當以經生槩之矣。〕
同考試官教諭阮批：〔君子成位乎中，乃題本旨。此作得之，宜錄以式。〕
考試官學正宋批：〔體裁簡當。〕
考試官教授劉批：〔整潔。〕

《大傳》論《易》具乎至理，因表學《易》者之得天也。夫《易》通乎三極，而皆天之理也。君子盡學《易》之功，寧不爲天之所祐哉？《大傳》之意，蓋以聖人之作《易》，流通於三極而貫徹於身心者也，兼體之者，
translation_en:
Master Zhou (Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤) said: "Purifying the mind is essential; employing the worthy is urgent." Those who wish to emulate Yao and Shun must first know what to devote themselves to before they can succeed.

"The movements of the six lines are the Way of the Three Ultimates. Therefore, what the noble man abides in with peace is the sequence of the Changes (Yi 易); what he delights in and ponders is the words of the lines. Therefore, when at rest, the noble man observes its images and ponders its words; when in action, he observes its changes and ponders its prognostications. Thus, 'help is given to him from Heaven; there will be good fortune and nothing that is not beneficial.'"

Feng Xiang 馮祥
Associate Examiner, Instructor Tang 唐, comments: [Attributing the Three Ultimates to the noble man—this is the Changes of the mind. None who has not penetrated its depths could easily speak of this. This essay is concise in wording and comprehensive in meaning, fully revealing the subtlest essence; one should hardly measure him by the standard of an ordinary student of the Classics.]
Associate Examiner, Instructor Ruan 阮, comments: [That the noble man establishes his position in the center is the fundamental purport of the theme. This essay has grasped it and ought to be recorded as a model.]
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Song 宋, comments: [The form and structure are concise and fitting.]
Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Liu 劉, comments: [Orderly and pure.]

The Great Commentary (Dazhuan 大傳), in discussing how the Changes embodies the ultimate principle, thereby sets forth how one who studies the Changes receives the favor of Heaven. Now, the Changes penetrates the Three Ultimates, and all of them are the principle of Heaven. When the noble man exhausts the effort of studying the Changes, how could he not be helped by Heaven? The meaning of the Great Commentary is that when the sages created the Changes, it flowed through the Three Ultimates and penetrated both body and mind. As for the one who embodies them all together, …

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
不有望於君子乎彼剛柔變化之極流行於一
卦六爻之間初二之動卽地之剛柔迭用也三
四之動卽人之仁義時出也五上之動卽天之
陰陽迭運也其時成於六位者一三極之散見
焉至著之象孰非至微之理乎而不可典要拘
矣其周流於六虛者一三極之統體焉形下之
器孰非形上之妙乎而不可典常求矣君子固
將成位乎其中者而可無會極之學乎自身之
居安而自得也則在於易之序焉所以立身極
===
者不能外也自心之樂玩而不窮也則在於爻
之辭焉所以立心極者不能外也是以未動之
先則觀其象也玩其辭也而所居所樂於靜者
皆易矣方動之際則觀其變也玩其占也而所
居所樂於動者皆易矣夫易之理卽天也君子
不違乎易焉則靜與天俱動與天游隨在昭眷
德之應思若啓之行若翼之無往非順適之休
一理感通而天心助順不有以統會乎三極耶
吁君子其善於體易也夫嘗聞善言天者曰天
punctuated: 不有望於君子乎？彼剛柔變化之極，流行於一卦六爻之間：初、二之動，卽地之剛柔迭用也；三、四之動，卽人之仁義時出也；五、上之動，卽天之陰陽迭運也。其時成於六位者，一三極之散見焉，至著之象，孰非至微之理乎？而不可典要拘矣。其周流於六虛者，一三極之統體焉，形下之器，孰非形上之妙乎？而不可典常求矣。君子固將成位乎其中者，而可無會極之學乎？自身之居安而自得也，則在於易之序焉，所以立身極者不能外也；自心之樂玩而不窮也，則在於爻之辭焉，所以立心極者不能外也。是以未動之先，則觀其象也，玩其辭也，而所居所樂於靜者，皆易矣；方動之際，則觀其變也，玩其占也，而所居所樂於動者，皆易矣。夫易之理卽天也。君子不違乎易焉，則靜與天俱，動與天游，隨在昭眷德之應，思若啓之，行若翼之，無往非順適之休。一理感通，而天心助順，不有以統會乎三極耶？吁！君子其善於體易也夫！嘗聞善言天者曰：天
translation_en: …is this not what is hoped for in the noble man? Those ultimate principles of the transformation of the firm and the yielding flow through the six lines of each hexagram: the movement of the first and second lines is none other than the alternating operation of the firm and the yielding of Earth; the movement of the third and fourth lines is none other than the timely issuance of humaneness and righteousness in Man; the movement of the fifth and topmost lines is none other than the alternating cycle of yin and yang in Heaven. Their timely completion across the six positions is entirely the dispersed manifestation of the Three Ultimates; among the most manifest images, which is not the most subtle principle? Thus they cannot be constrained by fixed rules. Their circulation through the six vacuous spaces is entirely the unified substance of the Three Ultimates; among the concrete vessels below form, which is not the wondrous mystery above form? Thus they cannot be sought through rigid norms. Since the noble man is destined to establish his position in their midst, how could he be without the learning that converges upon the Ultimate? As for his person dwelling in peace and finding self-possession, this lies in the sequence of the Changes—that by which he establishes the ultimate standard of his person cannot depart from it. As for his mind delighting in and pondering them inexhaustibly, this lies in the words of the lines—that by which he establishes the ultimate standard of his mind cannot depart from it. Therefore, prior to action, he contemplates its images and ponders its words, so that what he dwells in and delights in during stillness is altogether the Changes; at the moment of action, he contemplates its changes and ponders its prognostications, so that what he dwells in and delights in during activity is altogether the Changes. Now, the principle of the Changes is Heaven itself. When the noble man does not deviate from the Changes, in stillness he abides with Heaven, and in activity he roams with Heaven. Everywhere the response of Heaven's favor toward virtue is made manifest; his thoughts are as if inspired by it, his actions as if winged by it, and wherever he goes there is nothing but the blessing of smooth harmony. When the one principle resonates and penetrates, and the mind of Heaven aids compliance, does he not thereby unify and bring together the Three Ultimates? Ah! How well the noble man embodies the Changes! It has been heard from one skilled in speaking of Heaven that: "If Heaven…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
不變則道亦不變易貫三才而變動不居何歟
蓋天之不變以其變也而惟化斯神易之變以
不變也而通則可久此君子學識其變而三極
會於一心也若楊氏之太玄關朗之洞極司馬
氏之潛虛亦爲不善變矣謂得於居樂之妙可
乎
書

日嚴祗敬六德亮采有邦
屈灼

大臣贊恒德之美而因著其宜于用焉夫德者
適用之具也彰而能久則用之家國無不宜矣
非吉士而何臯陶陳謨至此若曰求賢以圖治
者明哲之君也度德而論材者觀人之要也九
punctuated:

… does not change, neither does the Way change." The Book of Changes (Yi) threads through the Three Powers, yet moves and changes without resting—why is that? It is because Heaven's constancy lies in its very change, and only through transformation does it become numinous; the Changes' change lies in its constancy, and when it penetrates through, it can endure. Thus the noble man through learning comprehends its changes, and the Three Ultimates converge within his single mind. As for Yang Xiong's Supreme Mystery (Taixuan), Guan Lang's Penetrating the Ultimate (Dongji), and Sima Guang's Hidden Vacuity (Qianxu), they were truly inept at change! Could they be said to have grasped the subtlety of dwelling at ease and taking joy in it?
