title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
德在人固以不偏爲貴矣吾何以稽之哉彼德
而弗彰則無以徵其美彰而弗久亦何以驗其
成必其具此德也隨事以効其動固顯夫篤實
之華矣而且經德不回非徒襲取于旦夕因行
以露其眞固達夫和順之美矣而且執德不變
爲能實踐于始終則盛德日新而富有之業已
豫允爲邦家之楨也體道恒久而可大之用已
基足當俊乂之選也謂之吉士信非名浮其實
矣而措之邦國又孰有不宜哉故九德而有其
===
三不徒蘊諸身已也緝熙以會其全而至德之
光日益奮焉則三德彰而有常矣以之爲大夫
必能出其宣著者以趨事而夙夜匪懈明作之
功可成也不爲有家之吉士矣乎九德而有其
六不徒備諸身已也嚴翼以愼其防而敬德之
功日益純焉則六德彰而有常矣以之爲諸侯
必能出其祇敬者以旬宣而經緯有章寅亮之
績可熙也不爲有邦之吉士矣乎至是則乃言
采采者爲可徵而亦言有德者非無據人君即
punctuated: 德在人，固以不偏爲貴矣，吾何以稽之哉？彼德而弗彰，則無以徵其美；彰而弗久，亦何以驗其成？必其具此德也，隨事以効其動，固顯夫篤實之華矣；而且經德不回，非徒襲取于旦夕。因行以露其眞，固達夫和順之美矣；而且執德不變，爲能實踐于始終。則盛德日新，而富有之業已豫，允爲邦家之楨也；體道恒久，而可大之用已基，足當俊乂之選也。謂之「吉士」，信非名浮其實矣，而措之邦國，又孰有不宜哉？故九德而有其三，不徒蘊諸身已也，緝熙以會其全，而至德之光日益奮焉，則三德彰而有常矣。以之爲大夫，必能出其宣著者以趨事，而夙夜匪懈，明作之功可成也，不爲有家之吉士矣乎？九德而有其六，不徒備諸身已也，嚴翼以愼其防，而敬德之功日益純焉，則六德彰而有常矣。以之爲諸侯，必能出其祇敬者以旬宣，而經緯有章，寅亮之績可熙也，不爲有邦之吉士矣乎？至是，則「乃言采采」者爲可徵，而「亦言有德」者非無據。人君即…
translation_en:
… virtues reside in a person, it is indeed their freedom from one-sidedness that is prized; yet how am I to examine them? If a virtue is not manifest, there is no way to attest its excellence; if it is manifest yet does not endure, how either can one verify its completion? Only when someone possesses this virtue and applies it in action as affairs arise—thus displaying the splendor of genuine substance—and moreover maintains a constant virtue without deflection, not merely seizing it for a morning or an evening; when through conduct he reveals its truth—thus attaining the beauty of harmony and compliance—and moreover holds fast to virtue without change, able to practice it in earnest from beginning to end: then his abundant virtue is daily renewed and his richly endowed enterprise is already prepared, making him truly a pillar of state and family; embodying the Way with constancy and endurance, the foundation for greatness in application is already laid, making him worthy of selection among the eminent and able. To call him a "worthy gentleman" (jishi) is truly no case of reputation exceeding reality; and when he is placed in service to the state, how could there be anything unsuitable?

Therefore, when a man possesses three of the nine virtues, he does not merely harbor them within his person; through continuous radiance he brings them to wholeness, and as the light of supreme virtue grows ever more vigorous day by day, those three virtues become manifest and constant. Employ such a man as a Grand Master, and he will surely bring forth what he has displayed and made illustrious in order to attend to affairs; never lax morning or night, the achievement of clear and energetic service can be accomplished—is he not a worthy gentleman for a noble house? When a man possesses six of the nine virtues, he does not merely keep them complete within his person; with strictness and reverence he guards his bounds, and as the work of reverent virtue grows ever purer day by day, those six virtues become manifest and constant. Employ such a man as a feudal lord, and he will surely bring forth his respectful reverence to diffuse royal governance throughout his domain; with order and pattern in his administration, the achievements of reverent enlightenment can be made to flourish—is he not a worthy gentleman for a fiefdom?

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
此辨之而知人之道豈外是哉雖然未可以易
言也蓋必君德清明而後鑒觀不眩唐虞之際
衆賢和朝雖其觀德有要亦濬哲克明以豫其
感也苟取人無本而徒于行事者求之則徇迹
遺心邪正難辨其不至于失人者幾希故曰純
心要矣用賢急焉
三八政一曰食二曰貨三曰祀四曰司空
五曰司徒六曰司寇七曰賓八曰師四
五紀一曰歲二曰月三曰日四曰星辰
五曰曆數
趙完
===
同考試官教諭竇　批〔八政五紀最難次敘是篇對待峻整剪裁有法且詞典而粹錄之〕
考試官學正宋　批〔格整義精氣昌詞健〕
考試官教授劉　批〔體認敬天勤民意親切〕
君子演三四之疇而勤民敬天之道備矣蓋人
君奉天以惠民者也八政行而五紀協俯仰其
無愧矣乎箕子演之以告武王也若曰人君建
punctuated:
此辨之，而知人之道豈外是哉？雖然，未可以易言也。蓋必君德清明，而後鑒觀不眩。唐虞之際，衆賢和朝，雖其觀德有要，亦濬哲克明以豫其感也。苟取人無本，而徒于行事者求之，則徇迹遺心，邪正難辨，其不至于失人者幾希。故曰：「純心要矣，用賢急焉。」

三、八政：一曰食，二曰貨，三曰祀，四曰司空，五曰司徒，六曰司寇，七曰賓，八曰師。四、五紀：一曰歲，二曰月，三曰日，四曰星辰，五曰曆數。
趙完

君子演三四之疇，而勤民敬天之道備矣。蓋人君奉天以惠民者也，八政行而五紀協，俯仰其無愧矣乎！箕子演之以告武王也，若曰：人君建
translation_en:
… discern them by this, and how could the way of knowing men lie outside of this? Even so, this cannot be spoken of lightly. Only when the sovereign's virtue is clear and bright will his observation and judgment not be deluded. During the era of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun], a multitude of worthies brought harmony to the court; although there were essentials for observing virtue, it was also because the sovereigns were profoundly wise and able to make bright their virtue, thereby preparing the basis for that responsiveness. If in selecting men one lacks this fundamental root and merely seeks them through their outward actions, then by following traces while neglecting the mind, the crooked and the upright will be hard to distinguish, and few indeed will avoid failing to find the right men. Therefore it is said: "Purifying the mind is essential; employing the worthy is urgent."

"Third, the Eight Objects of Government: the first is called food; the second is called commodities; the third is called sacrifices; the fourth is called the Minister of Works; the fifth is called the Minister of Education; the sixth is called the Minister of Justice; the seventh is called the reception of guests; the eighth is called the army. Fourth, the Five Arrangements of Time: the first is called the year; the second is called the month; the third is called the day; the fourth is called the stars and constellations; the fifth is called the calendrical calculations." [From the "Great Plan" (Hongfan) of the Book of Documents.]

Zhao Wan 趙完

In this essay the parallel treatment is rigorous and well-structured, the tailoring is methodical, and the diction is classical and pure. We record it for publication.]
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Song 宋, comments: [The structure is regular and the meaning precise; the vitality is flourishing and the diction vigorous.]
Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Liu 劉, comments: [It grasps with keen intimacy the meaning of revering Heaven and being diligent toward the people.]

When the noble man expounds the third and fourth categories [of the Great Plan], the way of being diligent toward the people and revering Heaven is made complete. For the sovereign is one who receives the mandate of Heaven in order to bestow favor upon the people. When the Eight Objects of Government are put into practice and the Five Arrangements of Time are brought into harmony, can he not look down upon the earth and up toward Heaven without shame? title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
極以圖治固將一天人而贊化育也洛書之三
四固第以八政五紀矣其目何如彼惟天生民
而人君牧之所以裁成輔相者其責也故因之
有八政之疇以開養道之原食固居其一矣而
貨以利用祀以報本政之列于二三者此焉以
貽奠安之澤司空固居其四矣而司徒以立敎
司寇以明刑政之列于五六者此焉至若天秩
有禮爲之賔以親邦國天討有罪爲之師以平
邦國非政之次于七八者乎隨其分願之各足
===
而因事厚生所謂作君作師法天以經政者至
此其克盡矣惟天垂象而人君則之所以治曆
明時者其責也故列之爲五紀之疇觀陰陽以
盡變歲功于是乎用成矣而晦明之代禪者必
紀其弦望之實故以歲爲首而次以月焉配天
行以貞度日候于此乎不爽矣而經緯之異名
者必紀其次舍之詳故以日居三而次以星辰
焉至若辨敘事而立數以步其常志災祥而錯
綜以占其變又非曆數之次于五者乎因其氣
punctuated: 極以圖治，固將一天人而贊化育也。《洛書》之三、四，固第以八政、五紀矣，其目何如？彼惟天生民而人君牧之，所以裁成輔相者，其責也，故因之有八政之疇。以開養道之原，食固居其一矣；而貨以利用，祀以報本，政之列于二、三者此焉。以貽奠安之澤，司空固居其四矣；而司徒以立敎，司寇以明刑，政之列于五、六者此焉。至若天秩有禮，爲之賔以親邦國；天討有罪，爲之師以平邦國，非政之次于七、八者乎？隨其分願之各足，而因事厚生，所謂作君作師，法天以經政者，至此其克盡矣。惟天垂象而人君則之，所以治曆明時者，其責也，故列之爲五紀之疇。觀陰陽以盡變，歲功于是乎用成矣；而晦明之代禪者，必紀其弦望之實，故以歲爲首而次以月焉。配天行以貞度，日候于此乎不爽矣；而經緯之異名者，必紀其次舍之詳，故以日居三而次以星辰焉。至若辨敘事而立數以步其常，志災祥而錯綜以占其變，又非曆數之次于五者乎？因其氣…
translation_en:
… standard of perfection in order to plan for good governance, he certainly intends to unify Heaven and humanity and assist in the transforming and nourishing processes of nature. The third and fourth divisions of the Luo Writing (Luoshu) are indeed ordered as the Eight Objects of Government (bazheng) and the Five Arrangements of Time (wuji); what are their specific items?

Now, since Heaven gives birth to the people and the sovereign shepherds them, it is his responsibility to regulate and assist the course of nature; therefore, based on this, there is the category of the Eight Objects of Government. To open up the source of the way of nourishment, food (shi) naturally occupies the first place; while commodities (huo) serve to facilitate useful employment and sacrifices (si) serve to repay the origin of things—such are the affairs of government ranked second and third. To bestow the blessing of settled security, the Minister of Works (sikong) naturally occupies the fourth place; while the Minister of Education (situ) establishes instruction and the Minister of Justice (sikou) clarifies punishments—such are the affairs of government ranked fifth and sixth. As for Heaven's ordaining the social ranks with their rites, making guests (bin) of them so as to draw the states into friendly relations; and Heaven's punishing the guilty, raising armies (shi) so as to pacify the states—are these not the affairs of government ordered seventh and eighth? Ensuring that each person's lot and wishes are satisfied, and enriching their livelihood according to circumstances—what is meant by acting as sovereign and acting as teacher, modeling oneself on Heaven to regulate governance, is hereby fulfilled to the utmost.

Since Heaven suspends its celestial signs and the sovereign takes them as his model, it is his responsibility to regulate the calendar and clarify the seasons; therefore, he sets them forth as the category of the Five Arrangements of Time. By observing yin and yang to exhaust their changes, the work of the year (sui) is thereby brought to completion; and as darkness and light succeed one another, one must record the realities of the quarter and full moons, and so the year is placed at the head and followed next by the month (yue). By matching the revolution of Heaven to rectify the degrees of motion, the solar periods of the day (ri) thus never err; and as the longitudinal and latitudinal luminaries bear different names, one must record in detail their stations and mansions, and so the day occupies the third place and is followed next by the stars and zodiacal spaces (xingchen). As for distinguishing the sequence of seasonal affairs and establishing numerical rules to calculate their regularities, or recording calamities and auspicious omens and synthesizing them to divine their anomalies—is this not the calendrical calculations (lishu) ordered in the fifth place? title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
運之推遷而察器觀象所謂先天後天奉時以
不違者至此其無愧矣是則八政行則俯以立
民之命五紀協則仰以憲天之心于此而兼舉
焉彝倫有不敘哉抑有本焉皇極是矣蓋極者
民之性也天之精也君人能愼厥身修則萬物
咸若乾道以清八政五紀皆舉而措之無難者
使身極未端規規焉于政令象數之末亦何以
聯屬天民而成其治哉有志于敘倫者當知所
以崇本矣
===
詩
夜如何其夜未央庭燎之光君子至止鸞
聲將將夜如何其夜未艾庭燎晣晣君
子至止鸞聲噦噦夜如何其夜鄉晨庭
燎有煇君子至止言觀其旂
張問達
同考試官敎諭何　批〔摸寫宣王儆惕之心宛然在目〕
且筆力簡勁更不落俗是深於詩者
考試官學正宋　批〔發周宣勤政之意婉曲殆盡〕
punctuated:
運之推遷，而察器觀象，所謂先天後天、奉時以不違者，至此其無愧矣。是則八政行，則俯以立民之命；五紀協，則仰以憲天之心。于此而兼舉焉，彝倫有不敘哉？抑有本焉，皇極是矣。蓋極者，民之性也，天之精也。君人能愼厥身修，則萬物咸若，乾道以清，八政五紀皆舉而措之無難者。使身極未端，規規焉于政令象數之末，亦何以聯屬天民而成其治哉？有志于敘倫者，當知所以崇本矣。

詩
「夜如何其？夜未央。庭燎之光。君子至止，鸞聲將將。夜如何其？夜未艾。庭燎晣晣。君子至止，鸞聲噦噦。夜如何其？夜鄉晨。庭燎有煇。君子至止，言觀其旂。」
張問達
同考試官敎諭何　批〔摸寫宣王儆惕之心，宛然在目，〕且筆力簡勁，更不落俗，是深於詩者。
考試官學正宋　批〔發周宣勤政之意，婉曲殆盡。〕
translation_en:
… according to the shifting cycles of cosmic pneumas, one inspects the astronomical instruments and observes the celestial phenomena. What is meant by preceding Heaven when Heaven does not act in opposition, and following Heaven by reverently conforming to the cosmic timing—at this point one can truly feel no shame in relation to it. Thus, when the Eight Objects of Government are put into practice, one looks down to establish the livelihood of the people; when the Five Arrangements are harmonized, one looks up to model oneself on the mind of Heaven. When both of these are carried out together here, how could the constant human relationships fail to be set in order? Yet there is a fundamental root to this, namely the August Ultimate. For the Ultimate is the nature of the people and the essence of Heaven. If the ruler of men can be cautious in cultivating his own person, then the myriad things will all be in harmony, the Way of Heaven will be clear, and the Eight Objects of Government and Five Arrangements can all be raised up and implemented without difficulty. If the standard of his own person is not yet upright, and he busies himself petty-mindedly with the superficialities of administrative ordinances and astronomical numbers, how then could he bind together Heaven and the people and bring his governance to completion? Those who aspire to set the human relationships in order must understand how to revere the fundamental root.

Classic of Poetry (Shijing)
"How goes the night? The night is not yet at its height. The courtyard torches are bright. The noblemen arrive; their harness-bells chime jiang-jiang. How goes the night? The night is not yet ended. The courtyard torches gleam softly. The noblemen arrive; their harness-bells chime hui-hui. How goes the night? The night approaches dawn. The courtyard torches give off a smoky glow. The noblemen arrive; now we can see their banners."
By Zhang Wenda 張問達.
Associate Examiner Instructor He 何 comments: [He depicts King Xuan's vigilant and conscientious mind so vividly that it appears right before one's eyes,] and moreover the force of his brush is concise and vigorous, completely free of vulgarity; he is one deeply versed in the Classic of Poetry.
Examiner Associate Instructor Song 宋 comments: [He brings out the meaning of King Xuan of Zhou's diligence in governance with subtle and exhaustive thoroughness.]

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授劉　批〔語雅健有次第〕
周王屢審視朝之期而心益慮其晩也夫視朝
有常期也周王屢致問而心惟恐晩焉不可以
觀無逸之衷乎想其不安于寢而發問若曰君
向明而出治當未明以求衣今夜如何哉夜其
未央乎然夜雖未央而庭燎之設于門內者爛
然其有光矣則凡百君子志急在公而鳴和鸞
以至止者已將將而有聲此其秉時靖共之心
爲甚殷也予獨安于寢焉其如朝會之盈何哉
===
既而又問曰君身日有萬幾當夙興以始事今
夜如何哉夜其未艾乎然夜雖未艾而庭燎之
設于門內者晣然其小明矣則凡百君子敬篤
上交而鳴和鸞以至止者已噦噦而可聞此其
待旦分猷之念爲至勤也予獨安于寢焉其如
朝會之昌何哉終而又問曰君日出而視朝臣
別色而始入今夜如何哉吾意東方欲明而庭
燎將盡見其煙光之相雜矣則凡百君子精白
承休而建淑旂以至止者已物采之可觀此其

The King of Zhou repeatedly inquired about the time for holding court, his mind growing ever more anxious lest he be late. Now, there is a fixed time for holding court; when the King of Zhou repeatedly asked after it, fearing in his heart only that it might be too late, can we not see in this his inner spirit of untiring diligence? One may imagine him restless in his bedchamber and asking the question, as if to say: "A ruler faces the dawn to go forth and govern, and ought to call for his robes before daybreak. How goes the night now? Is the night not yet spent? Yet even though the night is not yet spent, the courtyard torches set up inside the gate are already blazing brightly with light; and all the many lords and officers, their minds urgently bent on public duty, sounding their carriage bells and harness bells as they arrive, are already making a ringing clatter. How deeply earnest is their devotion to seizing the moment and quietly fulfilling their duties! Were I alone to rest at ease in my bedchamber, what would become of the crowded court assembly?"

Presently he asked again: "A ruler in his person faces ten thousand affairs each day, and ought to rise early to begin his business. How goes the night now? Is the night not yet ended? Yet even though the night is not yet ended, the courtyard torches set up inside the gate are already gleaming with a fainter light; and all the many lords and officers, reverently devoted to serving their superior, sounding their carriage bells and harness bells as they arrive, can already be heard chiming in measured rhythm. How utterly diligent is their eagerness to await the dawn and share in the counsels of state! Were I alone to rest at ease in my bedchamber, what would become of the thriving court assembly?"

Finally he asked once more: "The ruler holds court when the sun comes out, and the ministers enter only when colors can be distinguished. How goes the night now? I think the east is about to brighten and the courtyard torches are nearly burned out, so that one sees their smoke mingling with the light; and all the many lords and officers, with pure devotion upholding the royal grace and raising their fine dragon-banners as they arrive, already present a visible display of emblems and colors. title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
宣序民事之願又更切也予尚安于寢焉其如
羣工之望何哉是則由晦而明時以漸而頓異
自聞而見心以漸而益勤周王其賢矣乎抑考
時幾之勑昧爽之規古之明君所以宵衣求理
而不遑寧處者誠有見於宴安之習勝斯治化
之所由隳也宣王之問夜其庶幾路寢聽政潔
粢盛以卽安之風乎則其成車攻復古之治而
爲中興之令主有以也
受小球大球爲下國綴旒何天之休
張永錫
同考試官教諭何　批〔題旨得人得天本由一理此作詞甚融透而氣復博大蓋頌義之精者錄之〕
考試官學正宋　批〔莊重典雅〕
考試官教授劉　批〔健朗〕
大一統以承天眷商王受命之實也蓋人君以
得天下之心爲福也商王有一統之治則所以
承天眷者不在是哉商人祫祭而推及此蓋曰
帝王之凝命本于德而帝王之受命徵于人我
punctuated:
宣序民事之願又更切也。予尚安于寢焉，其如羣工之望何哉？是則由晦而明，時以漸而頓異；自聞而見，心以漸而益勤。周王其賢矣乎！抑考時幾之勑、昧爽之規，古之明君所以宵衣求理而不遑寧處者，誠有見於宴安之習勝，斯治化之所由隳也。宣王之問夜，其庶幾路寢聽政、潔粢盛以卽安之風乎！則其成車攻復古之治，而爲中興之令主，有以也。

受小球大球，爲下國綴旒，何天之休。
張永錫
同考試官教諭何　批〔題旨得人得天本由一理，此作詞甚融透，而氣復博大，蓋頌義之精者，錄之。〕
考試官學正宋　批〔莊重典雅。〕
考試官教授劉　批〔健朗。〕

translation_en:
… desire to proclaim and order the affairs of the people is even more urgent. If I still rest comfortably in my bedchamber, how could I face the expectations of all the officials? Thus, from darkness to dawn, the hour gradually yet markedly shifts; from hearing to seeing, his mind becomes progressively more diligent. How worthy indeed was the King of Zhou! Moreover, if we examine the admonition to be cautious of time and opportunity and the rule of rising before daybreak, the reason the enlightened rulers of antiquity dressed before dawn to seek good governance and had no leisure to rest in comfort was truly because they saw that when habits of ease and comfort prevail, transformative governance is thereby ruined. Does not King Xuan's asking about the night come close to that custom of hearing affairs of state in the state chamber and preparing pure sacrificial millet before taking one's ease? Then there is good reason indeed that he achieved the governance of "Our Chariots Were Strong" (Che gong) that restored antiquity, and became an admirable sovereign of dynastic revival.

"He received the small jade tablet and the large jade tablet, / And became the pendant-streamers for the subordinate states; / He bore the favor of Heaven." (Book of Odes, "Chang fa")
By Zhang Yongxi 張永錫
Associate Examiner Instructor He 何 comments: [The theme of the topic is that winning the people and winning Heaven originally stem from a single principle. The wording of this essay is thoroughly penetrating and its vital breath is moreover broad and grand; it captures the essence of the Sacrificial Odes (Song), so I select it for inclusion.]
Examiner Subprefectural Instructor Song 宋 comments: [Grave and classically elegant.]
Examiner Prefectural Instructor Liu 劉 comments: [Vigorous and clear.]

Unifying the realm on a grand scale so as to receive the favor of Heaven is the substantive reality of the Shang king's receiving the Mandate. Indeed, a ruler takes winning the hearts of the world as his blessing; since the Shang king possessed unified governance, did not that whereby he received the favor of Heaven lie right here? When the people of Shang performed the collective ancestral sacrifice (xia) and traced things to this point, it was as if to say: An emperor's or king's consolidating the Mandate is rooted in virtue, while an emperor's or king's receiving the Mandate is verified by the people. title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
祖以敬德而承式圍之命也試徵之來朝之人
乎誠以九圍之中其國不一其勢若難比也玆
焉仰明王之建極而脩瑞恪職合萬國以攸同
慕商命之維新而執玉來王盡庶邦而畢至以
朝小國則於小球而受之渙者以萃離者以合
而趨向之恐後者若有聯之而不能間也以朝
大國則於大球而受之近無不悅遠無不來而
歸附之爭先者若有繫之而不可解也不爲下
國之綴旒乎而天休之何不外是矣蓋天命主
===
於人心而歸德者旣同斯祗承乎眷德者爲益
至人心莫非天意而助信者無外斯昭受乎助
順者爲益隆羣后之肆朝固上天之示以行事
也人與之卽天與之而所以仰藉乎休徵者胥
此焉在矣百辟之戴見固帝命之顯於不違也
得乎人卽得乎天而所以寵膺乎景福者胥此
焉寓矣吁此有商王業之所由以成也登歌於
祫祭之頃烏容已乎抑此後人之頌湯也而非
湯之所以自待也蓋其制心制事不邇不殖惟
punctuated: 祖以敬德而承式圍之命也，試徵之來朝之人乎？誠以九圍之中，其國不一，其勢若難比也。玆焉仰明王之建極，而脩瑞恪職，合萬國以攸同；慕商命之維新，而執玉來王，盡庶邦而畢至。以朝小國，則於小球而受之，渙者以萃，離者以合，而趨向之恐後者，若有聯之而不能間也。以朝大國，則於大球而受之，近無不悅，遠無不來，而歸附之爭先者，若有繫之而不可解也。不爲下國之綴旒乎？而天休之何，不外是矣。蓋天命主於人心，而歸德者旣同，斯祗承乎眷德者爲益至；人心莫非天意，而助信者無外，斯昭受乎助順者爲益隆。羣后之肆朝，固上天之示以行事也，人與之卽天與之，而所以仰藉乎休徵者，胥此焉在矣。百辟之戴見，固帝命之顯於不違也，得乎人卽得乎天，而所以寵膺乎景福者，胥此焉寓矣。吁！此有商王業之所由以成也，登歌於祫祭之頃，烏容已乎？抑此後人之頌湯也，而非湯之所以自待也。蓋其制心制事，不邇不殖，惟
translation_en:
… ancestor through his reverent virtue received the mandate to serve as the model for the nine regions; let us test and verify this in the people who came to pay court! Indeed, within the nine regions, the states are not uniform, and their circumstances seem difficult to unite. Yet now they look up to the enlightened king's establishment of the supreme standard, preparing theirjade tokens and reverently fulfilling their duties, uniting the myriad states into shared harmony; admiring the renewal of the Mandate of Shang, they hold jade and come to pay homage to the king, all the numerous states arriving in full. When giving audience to the small states, he receives the small jade tablet from them; what was scattered is gathered, what was separated is joined, and those hastening forward in fear of being last are as if linked together so that nothing can come between them. When giving audience to the great states, he receives the great jade tablet from them; none near fail to rejoice, none far fail to come, and those vying to be first in pledging allegiance are as if bound together so that nothing can untie them. Does he not thus serve as the banner-pendants uniting the subordinate states? And how he bears the blessings of Heaven is nothing outside of this!

For the Mandate of Heaven rests upon the hearts of the people; when those who turn to virtue are already united, then one's reverent reception of Heaven's favor toward virtue becomes all the more complete. The hearts of the people are none other than the will of Heaven; when those who aid trustworthiness leave none outside, then one's illustrious reception of Heaven's aid to compliance becomes all the more grand. The assembled rulers presenting themselves at court is truly High Heaven manifesting its workings through deeds; when men grant their support, Heaven grants its support, and that whereby he looks up to rely upon auspicious verifications is wholly found right here. The hundred princes appearing in homage before their sovereign is truly the Supreme Ancestor's mandate shown to be unfailing; to win the people is to win Heaven, and that whereby he enjoys in favor great blessings is wholly lodged right here.

Ah! This is how the kingly enterprise of the house of Shang came to be accomplished; when ascending to sing praises at the moment of the collective ancestral sacrifice (xia), how could they refrain from doing so? Yet this was later men's eulogy of Tang, and not how Tang regarded himself. For he regulated his mind and regulated his affairs, neither indulging in sensory pleasures nor hoarding wealth, only…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
欲純一敬以爲昭格則其荷天休而聯下國固
有不自知其然者後世徒謂以鳴條之師得之
嗚呼是豈知湯之心者哉
春秋
五月癸丑公會晉侯齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭伯
衛子莒子盟于踐土〔僖公二十有八年〕
晉侯伐衛〔文公元年〕秋七月己未同盟
于亳城北〔襄公十有一年〕
馬愷
===

〔中作者不泛則略辭雅嚴正僅見此篇〕

此見晉平之忘本業而忝厥祖也君子遡文襄

文襄悼公之所以尊周者乎故城濮之績成而
punctuated:

…wished only to maintain pure, single-minded reverence so as to reach brightly to Heaven; thus, in receiving Heaven’s blessings and uniting the subordinate states, it occurred naturally without his even being conscious of how it came to be. Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

“In the fifth month, on the day guichou, the Duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Wei, and the Viscount of Ju, and made a covenant at Jiantu.” [Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi] “The Marquis of Jin attacked Wei.” [First year of Duke Wen] “In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day jiwei, they made a joint covenant north of the city of Bo.” [Eleventh year of Duke Xiang]

From this we see how Duke Ping of Jin 晉平公 forgot his fundamental enterprise and disgraced his ancestors. When the gentleman traces back the meritorious deeds of Dukes Wen 晉文公, Xiang 晉襄公, and Dao 晉悼公, how can he not feel deep regret over Duke Ping? title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
踐土之宮作文於是有獻俘之禮焉是雖天王
下勞若屈其居尊之體而叔興授策式昭夫天
命之榮當是時出入三覲稽首對揚不猶爲一
時之盛事哉觀於文而晉之能勤其業者基於
此矣既祥以聲罪而輯旅於南陽襄於是有朝
王之舉焉是雖因伐以行圖免效尤之禍而且
居獻計允協覲王之典當是時于溫一朝諸侯
景從不猶爲叔世之僅見哉觀於襄而晉之能
勤其業者爲可繼矣及晉悼之復霸適鄭人之
===
行成而亳北之信講焉質以司愼司盟監以名
山名川要以先王先公而布之載書曰同奬王
室則三駕之功雖未成而一念之忠不可泯其
視文襄之業不益有光乎吁晉之世勤其業而
功在王室如此使平而能尊周則可以文可以
襄可以悼而霸業其不墜矣柰之何惟杞是城
而不三霸若也其何以宗諸侯而主夏盟哉宜
春秋直書其事而貶之也雖然平固不足責矣
文襄之行譎而不正悼雖有君子之資而荀罃
punctuated: 踐土之宮作，文於是有獻俘之禮焉。是雖天子下勞，若屈其居尊之體，而叔興授策，式昭夫天命之榮。當是時，出入三覲，稽首對揚，不猶爲一時之盛事哉？觀於文，而晉之能勤其業者基於此矣。既祥，以聲罪而輯旅於南陽，襄於是有朝王之舉焉。是雖因伐以行，圖免效尤之禍，而且居獻計，允協覲王之典。當是時，于溫一朝，諸侯景從，不猶爲叔世之僅見哉？觀於襄，而晉之能勤其業者爲可繼矣。及晉悼之復霸，適鄭人之行成，而亳北之信講焉。質以司愼、司盟，監以名山、名川，要以先王、先公，而布之載書曰「同奬王室」，則三駕之功雖未成，而一念之忠不可泯，其視文、襄之業不益有光乎？吁！晉之世勤其業而功在王室如此。使平而能尊周，則可以文、可以襄、可以悼，而霸業其不墜矣。柰之何惟杞是城，而不三霸若也！其何以宗諸侯而主夏盟哉？宜《春秋》直書其事而貶之也。雖然，平固不足責矣，文、襄之行譎而不正，悼雖有君子之資，而荀罃
translation_en: … the palace at Jiantu was built, and thereupon Duke Wen performed the rite of presenting captives of war. Although the Heavenly King descended to reward his toil, seemingly compromising his exalted dignity, Shuxing conferred the royal commission, thereby manifesting the glory of Heaven's Mandate. At that time, coming and going in three audiences, bowing his head to the ground to extol the royal grace—was this not still a grand event of the age? Looking at Duke Wen, we see that Jin's ability to labor diligently at its enterprise was founded upon this. After the first-anniversary mourning sacrifice, having denounced a crime and assembled his troops at Nanyang, Duke Xiang thereupon undertook the act of paying court to the King. Although this was done in the course of a punitive expedition, seeking to avoid the calamity of imitating a bad example, JuJu offered a plan that truly accorded with the canons of royal audiences. At that time, at a single court audience at Wen, the feudal lords followed like shadows—was this not still a rare sight in a declining age? Looking at Duke Xiang, we see that Jin's ability to labor diligently at its enterprise was worthy of continuation. When Duke Dao of Jin restored the霸 (hegemony), it happened that the men of Zheng sued for peace, and the covenant north of Bo was concluded. Calling upon the deities Sishen and Simeng as witnesses, overseen by the famous mountains and great rivers, binding themselves by the former kings and former dukes, they proclaimed in the covenant document: "Together we shall aid and support the Royal House." Thus, although the achievement of the three expeditions was not yet complete, his single-minded loyalty cannot be obliterated; compared to the enterprises of Dukes Wen and Xiang, did it not shine even more brightly? Alas! Such was Jin's hereditary diligence in its enterprise and its meritorious service to the Royal House. Had Duke Ping been able to honor Zhou, he could have matched Wen, he could have matched Xiang, and he could have matched Dao, and the hegemonic enterprise would not have fallen into ruin. Why, then, did he only wall Qi, failing to measure up to the three hegemons? How could he thereby serve as the leader of the feudal lords and preside over the covenants of the Chinese states? Rightly did the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) directly record the event to censure him. Even so, Duke Ping is certainly not worth reproaching; the conduct of Dukes Wen and Xiang was crafty and not upright, and although Duke Dao had the qualities of a gentleman, Xun Ying …

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
諸人鮮格心之學三君功利之在人者淺矣所
以不數世而失諸侯也然則爲國者其尚敦不
息之誠而後可
三月公會劉子晉侯宋公蔡侯衛侯陳子
鄭伯許男曹伯莒子邾子頓子胡子滕
子薛伯杞伯小邾子齊國夏于召陵侵
楚〔定公四年〕
趙爾守
同考試官敎諭阮　批〔題內侵字乃聖人陋晉書法知〕
===
者甚少此作發揮明盡蓋潛心經學而有得者
考試官學正宋　批〔辭義凜然〕
考試官敎授劉　批〔得聖人陋晉之旨〕
霸主奉天討而沮於利春秋陋之也夫霸者之
所以行乎諸侯義也晉定奉命攘楚而顧以利
沮春秋陋之也宜哉昔蔡求釋憾於楚晉人請
命於周上勤元老下合列國同會召陵以討之
焉宜有美詞以揚其事而書侵者何哉蓋霸者
之奉王命將大義是伸而不可以利沮者也以
punctuated:
諸人鮮格心之學，三君功利之在人者淺矣，所以不數世而失諸侯也。然則爲國者，其尚敦不息之誠而後可。
三月，公會劉子、晉侯、宋公、蔡侯、衛侯、陳子、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、莒子、邾子、頓子、胡子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊國夏于召陵，侵楚。〔定公四年〕
趙爾守
同考試官敎諭阮　批〔題內「侵」字，乃聖人陋晉書法，知〕者甚少。此作發揮明盡，蓋潛心經學而有得者。
考試官學正宋　批〔辭義凜然。〕
考試官敎授劉　批〔得聖人陋晉之旨。〕
霸主奉天討而沮於利，《春秋》陋之也。夫霸者之所以行乎諸侯，義也。晉定奉命攘楚，而顧以利沮，《春秋》陋之也宜哉！昔蔡求釋憾於楚，晉人請命於周，上勤元老，下合列國，同會召陵以討之焉，宜有美詞以揚其事，而書「侵」者何哉？蓋霸者之奉王命，將大義是伸，而不可以利沮者也。以
translation_en:
… and the others lacked the learning to rectify the ruler's mind, so the utilitarian achievements of the three rulers left only a shallow impression on people; this is why within a few generations Jin lost the allegiance of the feudal lords. That being so, those who govern a state must cultivate unceasing sincerity before they can succeed.

"In the third month, the Duke met Viscount Liu, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Wei, the Viscount of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Hu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Little Zhu, and Guo Xia of Qi at Shaoling, and made an incursion into Chu." [Fourth year of Duke Ding]

By Zhao Ershou 趙爾守.

Associate Examiner, Instructor Ruan 阮, comments: [The word "incursion" (qin 侵) in the topic is the Sage's historiographical method of disparaging Jin; very few understand] this. This essay expounds it with complete clarity, showing that the author has immersed his mind in classical learning and gained true insight.

Examiner, Director of Studies Song 宋, comments: [The diction and moral principle are awe-inspiring.]

Examiner, Instructor Liu 劉, comments: [He has grasped the Sage's intent in disparaging Jin.]

When a hegemon undertakes a punitive expedition mandated by Heaven yet is deterred by private gain, the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) disparages him. Now, that by which a hegemon exercises leadership among the feudal lords is righteousness. Duke Ding of Jin received the royal command to repel Chu, yet on the contrary was deterred by profit; how fitting it is that the Spring and Autumn Annals disparages him! In the past, when Cai sought to vent its grievance against Chu, the men of Jin requested a mandate from Zhou. Above, they troubled a senior statesman of the royal court; below, they united the various states, assembling together at Shaoling to punish Chu. There ought to have been praising words to extol the undertaking—so why did the text record it merely as an "incursion"? It is because when a hegemon receives the king's command, he is about to extend great righteousness and must not be deterred by profit. Given…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
楚之横而仗義以攘之以蔡之辱而仗義以安
之夫誰曰非王者之師而何可以苟寅之求貨
遂止哉乃師未行於江漢而即有蔡人之辭威
未加於荊楚而遽返諸侯之旅國家本無虞也
而借口於水潦之方降不過以求之未遂而已
攘楚而無及於楚何以懲拘囚之横吾不意行
義而舉者以求利而躓衆也蓋不待召陵之後而
已知楚之重禍于蔡矣諸侯本無貳也而托辭
於中山之不服不過以貨之未得而已救蔡而
===
無補于蔡何以慰沈王之衷吾不意討罪而行
者以無功而返也蓋不待柏舉之戰而已知蔡
之轉望于吳矣噫召陵城濮之役君子嘗以無
命咎桓文矣定之請命宜陋二霸於不足尚者
而顧出其下也是役也不惟無以撫蔡而且重
失諸侯矣其何以爲盟主哉故春秋特書曰侵
若曰天討未明是亦潛師掠境而已所以陋之
者爲何如抑天下不患無時幾之會而患無識
時之俊傑召陵之師正晉霸復興之一機也而
punctuated: 楚之横，而仗義以攘之；以蔡之辱，而仗義以安之，夫誰曰非王者之師？而何可以苟寅之求貨遂止哉？乃師未行於江漢，而即有蔡人之辭；威未加於荊楚，而遽返諸侯之旅。國家本無虞也，而借口於水潦之方降，不過以求之未遂而已。攘楚而無及於楚，何以懲拘囚之横？吾不意行義而舉者，以求利而躓衆也。蓋不待召陵之後，而已知楚之重禍于蔡矣。諸侯本無貳也，而托辭於中山之不服，不過以貨之未得而已。救蔡而無補于蔡，何以慰沈王之衷？吾不意討罪而行者，以無功而返也。蓋不待柏舉之戰，而已知蔡之轉望于吳矣。噫！召陵、城濮之役，君子嘗以無命咎桓、文矣。定之請命，宜陋二霸於不足尚者，而顧出其下也。是役也，不惟無以撫蔡，而且重失諸侯矣，其何以爲盟主哉？故《春秋》特書曰「侵」，若曰天討未明，是亦潛師掠境而已。所以陋之者爲何如！抑天下不患無時幾之會，而患無識時之俊傑。召陵之師，正晉霸復興之一機也，而
translation_en: … because of the arrogance of Chu, they relied on righteousness to repel it; because of the humiliation of Cai, they relied on righteousness to bring it peace. Who then could say this was not the army of a true king? And how could it be abruptly halted merely because Xun Yin [transcribed 苟寅] demanded bribes? Yet before the troops had even marched to the Jiang and Han rivers, excuses were already being made to the people of Cai; before their military might had even been brought to bear upon Jing-Chu, the forces of the feudal lords were hastily turned back. The state in truth faced no domestic peril, yet they used the recent descent of floodwaters as a pretext—this was nothing more than because their demands had not been met. Setting out to repel Chu without ever reaching Chu, how could they punish its tyrannical detention and imprisonment of the marquis? I would never have expected that those who rose up to enact righteousness would cause the multitude to stumble through their pursuit of profit! Indeed, one did not need to wait until after the covenant at Shaoling to know that Chu would inflict grave calamity upon Cai. The feudal lords in truth harbored no duplicity, yet they made an excuse of Zhongshan's insubordination—this was nothing more than because the bribes had not been obtained. Setting out to rescue Cai without bringing any aid to Cai, how could they console the heart of him who sank his jade [in prayer to the river]? I would never have expected that those who marched forth to punish a crime would return without achievement! Indeed, one did not need to wait until the Battle of Boju to know that Cai would turn its hopes toward Wu. Alas! Regarding the campaigns of Shaoling and Chengpu, the gentleman once faulted Dukes Huan and Wen for acting without the king's mandate. Duke Ding, having requested the royal mandate, ought to have made those two hegemons look unworthy of esteem; yet instead he fell even beneath them! In this campaign, not only Did he fail to comfort Cai, he also gravely lost the allegiance of the feudal lords. How then could he serve as lord of the covenant? Therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals specially records it as an "incursion" (qin), as if to say that since Heaven's punitive expedition was not made manifest, this too was nothing more than sneaking troops across a border to raid. How profound is this disparagement! Moreover, the realm does not suffer from a lack of timely opportunities, but rather from a lack of outstanding men who recognize the times. The army at Shaoling was precisely an opportunity for the revival of Jin's hegemony, yet…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
苟寅鄙夫竟以利敗天下之勢去而不可挽者
寅實爲之貨之易于溺人而其弊至於莫捄有
識者可以鑒矣
禮記
天則不言而信神則不怒而威
楊光訓
同考試官教諭唐　批〔格正氣昌意精詞練發明天神之妙殆無餘藴而結處歸本于心尤見體認取之〕
考試官學正宋　批〔充暢古雅究極淵微〕
考試官教授劉　批〔典則可式〕
===
記者極言天神之妙一無所爲而然也甚矣樂
化感人心于無間也信不以言而威不以怒天
神之妙斯其至矣記者推之見君子致樂之極
功也葢謂樂之爲道所以合神明協造化而貫
通乎人心者也君子致樂以治心固馴至于天
神矣其妙果何如哉是故人心本具乎實理苟
德未達諸天信未必其不言也今惟易直子諒
之心妙于天則天在吾心即信在吾心也而推
punctuated:
苟寅鄙夫，竟以利敗。天下之勢，去而不可挽者，寅實爲之。貨之易于溺人，而其弊至於莫捄，有識者可以鑒矣。

《禮記》
「天則不言而信，神則不怒而威。」
楊光訓
同考試官教諭唐　批〔格正氣昌，意精詞練，發明天神之妙，殆無餘藴，而結處歸本于心，尤見體認，取之。〕
考試官學正宋　批〔充暢古雅，究極淵微。〕
考試官教授劉　批〔典則可式。〕

記者極言天神之妙，一無所爲而然也。甚矣，樂化感人心于無間也！信不以言，而威不以怒，天神之妙，斯其至矣。記者推之，見君子致樂之極功也。葢謂樂之爲道，所以合神明、協造化，而貫通乎人心者也。君子致樂以治心，固馴至于天神矣，其妙果何如哉？是故人心本具乎實理，苟德未達諸天，信未必其不言也。今惟易直子諒之心妙于天，則天在吾心，即信在吾心也，而推
translation_en:
… the vulgar fellow荀寅 Xun Yin [read 荀 for 苟] ultimately ruined it out of greed for profit. That the momentum of the realm slipped away and could no longer be recovered was truly Xun Yin's doing. How easily material goods drown a man, and how the resulting harm reaches a point beyond rescue—men of discernment may take this as a mirror!

Record of Rites (Liji)
"Being like Heaven, he is trusted without speaking; being like a spirit, he is awe-inspiring without being angry."
Yang Guangxun
Associate Examiner and Instructor Tang comments: [The structure is upright and the vital breath flourishing; the ideas are refined and the diction polished. In elucidating the wondrousness of Heaven and the spirits, it leaves almost nothing unexpressed, and at the conclusion it traces the root back to the mind, which especially shows personal realization. Selected.]
Examiner and Director of Studies Song comments: [Full, fluent,古典 and elegant, thoroughly probing the profound and subtle.]
Examiner and Instructor Liu comments: [Canonical in standard, worthy of serving as a model.]

The recorder speaks to the utmost of the wondrousness of Heaven and the spirits, which is altogether so without any deliberate effort. Profound indeed is the way the transformative influence of music moves the human mind without the slightest gap! To be trusted without speaking and awe-inspiring without anger—this is the ultimate perfection of the wondrousness of Heaven and the spirits. The recorder extends this idea to show the supreme achievement of the noble man in carrying music to its utmost. For the Way of music is that by which one unites with spiritual illumination, harmonizes with the creative transformations of nature, and penetrates the human mind. When the noble man carries music to its utmost in order to govern his mind, he naturally progresses until he reaches the level of Heaven and the spirits; what, then, is that wondrousness really like? Therefore, the human mind is originally endowed with real principle, yet if one's virtue has not reached up to Heaven, trust will not necessarily come without speaking. Now, only when an easy, straightforward, filial, and sincere mind reaches the wondrousness of Heaven does Heaven reside in my mind, which means trust resides in my mind; and when extending…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
誠于天下皆取足于此心之天焉故不必脩詞
以立誠而無聲之默會一無妄之流通不必寡
言以成信而至靜之淵涵一至誠之貫徹時顯
諸言天眞之發固信也時藏于默精誠之藴亦
信也蓋惟其信不惟其言其諸天道默運而化
機自爲之不爽者乎人心本自有可畏苟德未
入于神威未必其不怒也今惟易直子諒之心
妙于神則神在吾心卽威在吾心也而顯道于
天下皆取足于此心之神焉故神武不假于奮
===
揚而有嚴有翼自儼莊敬于無形神威不假于
震厲而惟玄惟默自顯赫奕于有象怒通諸感
凜然者固可見也怒涵諸寂肅然者亦如在也
蓋惟其威不惟其怒其諸鬼神莫測而百衆自
爲之畏服者乎是知天固不言而信所以成其
信者從天之樂致之也神固不怒而威所以成
其威者率神之樂啓之也樂之功用如此君子
其可須臾離哉雖然天也神也豈吾心所本無
哉蓋心之虛靈卽天也心之通變卽神也能致
punctuated: 誠于天下，皆取足于此心之天焉。故不必脩詞以立誠，而無聲之默會，一無妄之流通；不必寡言以成信，而至靜之淵涵，一至誠之貫徹。時顯諸言，天眞之發固信也；時藏于默，精誠之藴亦信也。蓋惟其信，不惟其言，其諸天道默運，而化機自爲之不爽者乎！人心本自有可畏，苟德未入于神，威未必其不怒也。今惟易直子諒之心妙于神，則神在吾心，卽威在吾心也。而顯道于天下，皆取足于此心之神焉。故神武不假于奮揚，而有嚴有翼，自儼莊敬于無形；神威不假于震厲，而惟玄惟默，自顯赫奕于有象。怒通諸感，凜然者固可見也；怒涵諸寂，肅然者亦如在也。蓋惟其威，不惟其怒，其諸鬼神莫測，而百衆自爲之畏服者乎！是知天固不言而信，所以成其信者，從天之樂致之也；神固不怒而威，所以成其威者，率神之樂啓之也。樂之功用如此，君子其可須臾離哉！雖然，天也，神也，豈吾心所本無哉？蓋心之虛靈卽天也，心之通變卽神也。能致
translation_en: …extending sincerity to all under heaven draws entirely upon the Heaven within this mind. Therefore, one need not polish words to establish sincerity, for silent comprehension without sound is entirely the flow of truth free from falsehood; one need not be sparing of words to achieve trustworthiness, for the deep containment of utmost stillness is entirely the penetration of utmost sincerity. When at times it is manifested in speech, the expression of natural genuineness is certainly trustworthy; when at times it is hidden in silence, the store of pure sincerity is likewise trustworthy. Indeed, it depends solely on trustworthiness and not on words—is this not like the Way of Heaven operating in silence while the mechanisms of transformation are unfailingly fulfilled of their own accord? The human mind inherently possesses that which inspires awe, yet if virtue has not entered the realm of the spiritual, majesty is not necessarily achieved without anger. Now, since the easy, straightforward, filial, and compassionate mind reaches wondrous perfection in the spiritual, the spiritual is within one's own mind, which means majesty is within one's own mind. And making the Way manifest to all under heaven draws entirely upon the spirit within this mind. Therefore, spiritual martial vigor does not rely on fierce display, yet being stern and reverent, it naturally commands solemn respect in the formless; spiritual majesty does not rely on thunderous severity, yet in profound mystery and silence, it naturally reveals glorious splendor in the visible. When anger responds to stimulus, its awesome presence can certainly be seen; when anger is contained in stillness, its solemnity is likewise as if palpably present. Indeed, it depends solely on majesty and not on anger—is this not like ghosts and spirits being unfathomable while the multitude of people naturally submit in awe of their own accord? Thus we know that Heaven is indeed trustworthy without speaking, and that by which its trustworthiness is accomplished is brought about by the music that follows Heaven; the spiritual is indeed majestic without anger, and that by which its majesty is accomplished is opened up by the music that accords with the spiritual. Such is the efficacy of music—how could the gentleman depart from it even for an instant! Even so, are Heaven and the spiritual originally absent from our own mind? For the empty and numinous awareness of the mind is Heaven, and the mind's capacity to penetrate change is the spiritual. If one can fully develop…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
樂以養之則德備而吾心固有之天復義精而
吾心自然之神具矣否則空虛徂伏又何足語
治心之功
孝子之有深愛者必有和氣有和氣者必
有愉色有愉色者必有婉容
王櫕
同考試官教諭唐　批〔和氣愉色婉容最難形容是作〕
冲融溫粹更無痕跡佳士也
考試官學正宋　批〔發揮孝子深愛之形精純瑩徹〕
===
考試官教授劉　批〔婉確細潤〕
人子愛乎親者至斯發于外者順矣蓋孝子愛
親無所不用其極也則夫辭氣容色之形孰非
順德之不容掩者哉見于祭義如此蓋謂人子
之於親孰不有愛也愛而弗深則發于聲徵于
色而動于身者斯難乎其順矣惟孝子也至情
素篤于天性而二人之懷結諸心而無所解天
親不假以人爲而一本之念體其志而不敢違
致愛致慤無物可以易其衷也克敬克孝無時
punctuated:
樂以養之，則德備而吾心固有之天復，義精而吾心自然之神具矣。否則空虛徂伏，又何足語治心之功！

孝子之有深愛者必有和氣，有和氣者必有愉色，有愉色者必有婉容。
王櫕
同考試官教諭唐　批〔和氣、愉色、婉容最難形容，是作〕冲融溫粹，更無痕跡，佳士也。
考試官學正宋　批〔發揮孝子深愛之形，精純瑩徹。〕
考試官教授劉　批〔婉確細潤。〕

人子愛乎親者至，斯發于外者順矣。蓋孝子愛親，無所不用其極也，則夫辭氣容色之形，孰非順德之不容掩者哉？見于《祭義》如此。蓋謂人子之於親，孰不有愛也？愛而弗深，則發于聲、徵于色而動于身者，斯難乎其順矣。惟孝子也，至情素篤于天性，而二人之懷結諸心而無所解；天親不假以人爲，而一本之念體其志而不敢違。致愛致慤，無物可以易其衷也；克敬克孝，無時
translation_en:
…music to nourish it, then virtue will be complete and the Heaven inherent in our mind will be restored; rightness will be refined and the spirit natural to our mind will be fully present. Otherwise, falling into emptiness and passivity, how could it be worth speaking of the work of governing the mind!

"A filial son who has deep love must have a harmonious disposition; he who has a harmonious disposition must have a pleasant countenance; he who has a pleasant countenance must have a compliant demeanor."

Wang Zan 王櫕
Associate Examiner, County Director of Studies Tang 唐 comments: 〔A harmonious disposition, a pleasant countenance, and a compliant demeanor are most difficult to describe; this composition〕 is harmonious, warm, and pure, without a trace of artifice—a fine scholar indeed.
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Song 宋 comments: 〔It elaborates the outward manifestations of a filial son's deep love in a refined, pure, and pellucid manner.〕
Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Liu 劉 comments: 〔Gentle, exact, delicate, and polished.〕

When a son's love for his parents reaches the utmost, what is manifested on the outside is compliant. Indeed, in loving his parents, there is nowhere that a filial son does not exert himself to the utmost; thus, in the outward manifestations of his words, breath, demeanor, and countenance, which of them is not an irrepressible expression of compliant virtue? Such is what appears in the Meaning of Sacrifices (Jiyi). It means to say: in a son's relation to his parents, who does not have love? Yet if that love is not deep, then what issues in his voice, shows in his countenance, and moves in his person will hardly be compliant. Only the filial son, whose utmost affection is ever earnest by heavenly nature, holds the thought of his two parents bound fast in his heart without ever letting go; heavenly kinship does not rely on human artifice, and the mindfulness of his single root embodies their wishes without daring to disobey. Carrying love and sincerity to the utmost, no external thing can alter his inner feelings; able to be reverent and filial, there is no moment…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
可以間其誠也夫是之謂深愛矣而形見于外
豈容以自已哉言乎其氣非有心以求和而心
和則氣和自藹然其可掬焉處之順逆不必同
而出之爲詞殆見其溫而不見其厲矣深愛之
形于和氣有如此言乎其色非有心以求愉而
根心則生色自粹然其可卽焉親之好惡不敢
必而著之于面殆見其悅而不見其戾矣深愛
之形于愉色有如此言乎其容亦未嘗有心以
求婉也然一德極其誠則四體安于化而動容
===
自協于禮焉周旋進退雖不同而彰之于躬殆
見其順而不見其違矣深愛之見于婉容又如
此是知曰氣曰色曰容順德著于外象之皆可
見者也和也愉也婉也順德根于中機之不可
遏者也外盡其禮內盡其誠孝子事親之道無
餘蘊矣雖然人子之事親也亦求盡其心而已
故心苟盡焉王食萬方而夔夔齊栗固孝也菽
食飲水而日盡其歡亦孝也心或未盡則大本
已失雖日用三牲奚益哉噫此曾參之養志閔
punctuated: 可以間其誠也，夫是之謂深愛矣。而形見于外，豈容以自已哉？言乎其氣，非有心以求和，而心和則氣和，自藹然其可掬焉；處之順逆不必同，而出之爲詞，殆見其溫而不見其厲矣，深愛之形于和氣有如此。言乎其色，非有心以求愉，而根心則生色，自粹然其可卽焉；親之好惡不敢必，而著之于面，殆見其悅而不見其戾矣，深愛之形于愉色有如此。言乎其容，亦未嘗有心以求婉也，然一德極其誠，則四體安于化，而動容自協于禮焉；周旋進退雖不同，而彰之于躬，殆見其順而不見其違矣，深愛之見于婉容又如此。是知曰氣、曰色、曰容，順德著于外，象之皆可見者也；和也、愉也、婉也，順德根于中，機之不可遏者也。外盡其禮，內盡其誠，孝子事親之道無餘蘊矣。雖然，人子之事親也，亦求盡其心而已。故心苟盡焉，王食萬方而夔夔齊栗，固孝也；菽食飲水而日盡其歡，亦孝也。心或未盡，則大本已失，雖日用三牲，奚益哉？噫！此曾參之養志、閔…
translation_en:
…can interrupt his sincerity. Now this is what is called deep love. And when it manifests externally, how could it be restrained by oneself? Speaking of his demeanor, he does not intentionally seek to be harmonious, yet because his heart is harmonious, his demeanor is harmonious, naturally so gentle and genial that it seems tangible. Whether the circumstances he faces are favorable or adverse need not be the same, yet when expressed in words, one sees only his warmth and never harshness. Such is how deep love takes form in a harmonious demeanor. Speaking of his countenance, he does not intentionally seek to be cheerful, yet because it is rooted in the heart, it produces a countenance naturally so pure and mild that he is approachable. He dares not take his parents' likes and dislikes for granted, yet as shown on his face, one sees only his pleasure and never perversity. Such is how deep love takes form in a cheerful countenance. Speaking of his bearing, neither has he ever intentionally sought to be compliant; yet when his single-minded virtue reaches the utmost sincerity, his four limbs rest naturally in transformation, and his movements spontaneously accord with ritual propriety. Though his turning, advancing, and retiring vary with the occasion, as displayed in his person, one sees only his compliance and never defiance. Such again is how deep love is seen in a compliant bearing.

From this we know that what are called demeanor, countenance, and bearing are compliant virtue manifested on the outside—outward forms that can all be seen; and that harmony, cheerfulness, and compliance are compliant virtue rooted within—inner springs that cannot be suppressed. Exhausting ritual propriety on the outside and exhausting sincerity on the inside, the way of a filial son in serving his parents leaves nothing further to be desired. Even so, in serving his parents, a son simply seeks to exhaust his heart. Therefore, if his heart is truly exhausted, to enjoy the royal revenues of the myriad regions while remaining reverent, fearful, and grave (like Shun) is certainly filial piety; to eat beans and drink water while daily giving his parents their fill of joy is also filial piety. If the heart is not exhausted, the great foundation is already lost; though one offers the three sacrificial animals every day, of what benefit is it? Alas! title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
損之承順皆聖賢所嘉樂也然則欲盡其孝者
宜何如亦曰自色難中求之而後可
第貳場
論
堯舜之仁急親賢
趙爾守
同考試官教諭阮　批〔以熟字立意而推極于同天疊〕
〔疊千言圓轉流暢末復歸于任相尤爲得旨是學識兼到者〕
同考試官教諭何　批〔有開闔有照應古雅精練不蔓〕
===
考試官學正宋　批〔思致精切筆勢雄渾〕
〔不膚可以式士矣〕
考試官教授劉　批〔說出二聖仁天下之心敢〕
聖人之仁覆天下不必其自己出也惟於其幾
焉運之而已蓋聖人之心視天下民物猶吾身
也而况以一身立乎天下民物之上則其所以
憂天下而欲行其愛者甚於天下之自愛其身
夫聖人愛天下之心如此其急苟無幾焉以運
之則天下民物至衆理道至繁悉欲取足於聖
punctuated:
損之承順，皆聖賢所嘉樂也。然則欲盡其孝者，宜何如？亦曰：自「色難」中求之而後可。

第貳場
論
堯舜之仁急親賢

趙爾守
同考試官教諭阮　批〔以熟字立意，而推極于同天。疊〕〔疊千言，圓轉流暢，末復歸于任相，尤爲得旨，是學識兼到者。〕
同考試官教諭何　批〔有開闔，有照應，古雅精練，不蔓〕〔不膚，可以式士矣。〕
考試官學正宋　批〔思致精切，筆勢雄渾。〕
考試官教授劉　批〔說出二聖仁天下之心敢。〕

聖人之仁覆天下，不必其自己出也，惟於其幾焉運之而已。蓋聖人之心，視天下民物猶吾身也，而况以一身立乎天下民物之上，則其所以憂天下而欲行其愛者，甚於天下之自愛其身。夫聖人愛天下之心如此其急，苟無幾焉以運之，則天下民物至衆，理道至繁，悉欲取足於聖
translation_en:
… and Min Sun's [閔損] compliant obedience were both praised and delighted in by the sages and worthies. That being so, how should one who wishes to fulfill his filial piety proceed? It may simply be said: only by seeking it within "the difficulty of maintaining a pleasant countenance" can one succeed.

Second Session
Discourse
"The Benevolence of Yao and Shun Was Urgent in Befriending the Worthy"

By Zhao Ershou 趙爾守

Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Ruan 阮 comments: [He establishes his central idea around the word "urgency" [? 熟 for 急] and pushes it to the ultimate level of matching Heaven. Layer upon layer of a thousand words, well-rounded and fluent, finally returning to the reliance on ministers—this especially grasps the main purport and shows one who possesses both learning and insight.]
Associate Examiner County Director of Studies He 何 comments: [There is opening and closing, and there is structural correspondence. Archaic in elegance and refined, neither sprawling nor superficial, it can serve as a model for scholars.]
Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies Song 宋 comments: [The thought is precise and apt; the force of the brush is vigorous and grand.]
Examiner Prefectural Director of Studies Liu 劉 comments: [He articulates the mind with which the two sages extended benevolence to the world, bold [? 敢].]

When the sage's benevolence covers all under Heaven, it does not necessarily have to issue from his own person; he simply operates it through its pivotal mechanism. title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
人一人之身亦難矣聖人有見於此不以一人
爲天下役而急欲爲天下得其人其人既得則
吾之憂天下者有人以代吾憂而吾之愛天下
者有人以行吾愛吾惟垂衣拱手天下自理自
安此聖人仁天下之要幾也是天道也孟子舉
堯舜之仁而推其急於親賢其知聖人之仁達
諸天者乎今夫天窿然虛而已矣穆然寂而已
矣初何心於萬物也而二氣尸其柄五行布其
令日月雨露風雷霜雪推移以節宣其序然後
===
歲功畢而萬物以生以成焉世之言生成者不
曰二氣五行日月雨露風雷霜雪之功必歸之
天道何也所以宰其幾以運於上者天也其他
不得而與也此天道所以無爲而成化也堯舜
中天而興繼天以出治而其幾則法乎天當是
時堯舜之爲君也視天下民物也視其
身即天下民物也故不以天下累其心亦不以
其心遺天下不遺天下故其憂天下也深憂之
也深故其仁天下也至不累其心故蕩蕩乎無
punctuated: 人一人之身，亦難矣。聖人有見於此，不以一人爲天下役，而急欲爲天下得其人。其人既得，則吾之憂天下者，有人以代吾憂；而吾之愛天下者，有人以行吾愛。吾惟垂衣拱手，天下自理自安，此聖人仁天下之要幾也，是天道也。孟子舉堯、舜之仁，而推其急於親賢，其知聖人之仁達諸天者乎！今夫天，窿然虛而已矣，穆然寂而已矣，初何心於萬物也？而二氣尸其柄，五行布其令，日月、雨露、風雷、霜雪推移以節宣其序，然後歲功畢而萬物以生以成焉。世之言生成者，不曰二氣、五行、日月、雨露、風雷、霜雪之功，必歸之天道，何也？所以宰其幾以運於上者，天也，其他不得而與也。此天道所以無爲而成化也。堯、舜中天而興，繼天以出治，而其幾則法乎天。當是時，堯、舜之爲君也，視天下民物也，視其身即天下民物也。故不以天下累其心，亦不以其心遺天下。不遺天下，故其憂天下也深；憂之也深，故其仁天下也至。不累其心，故蕩蕩乎無
translation_en: … the person of the sage alone, it would indeed be difficult. Seeing this, the sage does not enslave his single person to the empire, but urgently desires to find the right men for the empire. Once those men are found, then in my worrying for the empire, there are men to take on my worries; and in my loving the empire, there are men to carry out my love. I merely let my robes hang down and fold my hands, and the empire becomes well-governed and tranquil of its own accord. This is the essential pivot by which the sage extends benevolence to the empire; this is the Way of Heaven. When Mencius cited the benevolence of Yao and Shun and traced it to their urgency in drawing near to the worthy, did he not understand that the benevolence of the sages reaches to Heaven! Now as for Heaven, it is simply vast and empty, simply profound and silent; what deliberate mind does it initially have toward the myriad things? Yet the two vital forces hold its authority, the five phases spread its commands, and the sun and moon, rain and dew, wind and thunder, frost and snow alternate in succession to regulate and diffuse their order; only then is the year's work completed, and thereby the myriad things are born and brought to completion. When people in the world speak of generation and completion, they do not call it the achievement of the two vital forces, the five phases, the sun and moon, rain and dew, wind and thunder, or frost and snow, but invariably attribute it to the Way of Heaven. Why is this? Because that which governs the pivot and revolves above is Heaven, and none of the others can partake in it. This is how the Way of Heaven achieves transformation through non-action. Yao and Shun arose at the zenith of antiquity, succeeding Heaven in bringing forth governance, and their pivot was modeled upon Heaven. At that time, in their rule as sovereigns, Yao and Shun regarded the people and things of the empire [as themselves?], and regarded their own persons as none other than the people and things of the empire. Therefore, they neither burdened their minds with the empire, nor did their minds neglect the empire. Because they did not neglect the empire, their worry for the empire was deep; because their worry for it was deep, their benevolence toward the empire was utmost. Because they did not burden their minds, how vast and…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
能名巍巍乎有天下而不與夫其憂天下仁天
下如此其切而乃至於不與不可名焉非其法
天之幾舉賢任才以共成天下之治安能不勞
而仁覆天下也哉是故方其賢之未得也吾見
堯舜憂天下之心至急也洪水橫流則憂之黎
民阻饑則憂之百姓不親不遜則憂之蠻夷猾
夏則憂之曆象失紀人時忒序則憂之以至一
民一物一有失所若恫瘝之在身而憂之不已
憂之必思所以爲之所也欲爲之所豈能以其
===
身自爲之哉又豈能以一人而兼其事哉如以
其身自爲之則是以天而下行二氣五行日月
雨露風雷霜雪之職無是理也如以一人而兼
之則是以日月雨露風雷霜雪而皆責望於天
欲求化工之成不可得也如是而安在其爲如
天之仁好生之德哉惟堯舜知其然堯不自用
其仁也惟汲汲求舜而已矣舜不自用其仁也
惟汲汲求禹皐陶而已矣舜與禹皐陶之既得
則又不必自用其仁也凡稷契益夔龍工垂之
punctuated: 能名，巍巍乎有天下而不與。夫其憂天下、仁天下如此其切，而乃至於不與、不可名焉，非其法天之幾，舉賢任才以共成天下之治，安能不勞而仁覆天下也哉？是故方其賢之未得也，吾見堯舜憂天下之心至急也。洪水橫流則憂之，黎民阻饑則憂之，百姓不親不遜則憂之，蠻夷猾夏則憂之，曆象失紀、人時忒序則憂之，以至一民一物一有失所，若恫瘝之在身，而憂之不已。憂之，必思所以爲之所也。欲爲之所，豈能以其身自爲之哉？又豈能以一人而兼其事哉？如以其身自爲之，則是以天而下行二氣、五行、日月、雨露、風雷、霜雪之職，無是理也；如以一人而兼之，則是以日月、雨露、風雷、霜雪而皆責望於天，欲求化工之成，不可得也。如是，而安在其爲如天之仁、好生之德哉？惟堯舜知其然，堯不自用其仁也，惟汲汲求舜而已矣；舜不自用其仁也，惟汲汲求禹、皐陶而已矣。舜與禹、皐陶之既得，則又不必自用其仁也，凡稷、契、益、夔、龍、工垂之
translation_en:
… could find no name for it, and how sublime it was that they possessed the empire and yet remained aloof from it! Now, that their anxiety for the empire and their benevolence toward the empire were so earnest, and yet they reached the point of remaining aloof and being beyond naming—had they not modeled themselves on the subtle mainspring of Heaven, promoting the worthy and employing the talented to jointly accomplish the governance of the empire, how could they have covered the empire with their benevolence without toiling themselves?

Therefore, before those worthies had been found, we see that the minds of Yao and Shun in worrying about the empire were most urgent. When the floodwaters flowed unchecked, they worried about it; when the common people suffered from famine, they worried about it; when the hundred surnames were not affectionate and not compliant, they worried about it; when the Man and Yi barbarians disturbed the central lands, they worried about it; when the calendrical calculations and astronomical phenomena lost their regularity and the seasons of human affairs fell out of order, they worried about it—even to the point that if a single person or a single thing lost its proper place, they felt it as though the pain and sickness were in their own bodies, and worried over it unceasingly.

Worrying over it, they necessarily thought of how to put things in their proper place. Wishing to put things in their proper place, how could they do it all in person? And how could a single man simultaneously handle all those affairs? If the ruler were to do it all in person, that would be like Heaven descending to perform the duties of the two cosmic forces, the five phases, the sun and moon, rain and dew, wind and thunder, and frost and snow—there is no such principle! And if a single man were to simultaneously handle them all, that would be like demanding the work of the sun and moon, rain and dew, wind and thunder, and frost and snow all directly from Heaven itself; if one wished to seek the completion of nature's creative work in that way, it would be impossible to obtain. If it were so, where then would be the benevolence that is like Heaven's and the virtue that loves life?

Only Yao and Shun knew this to be so. Yao did not exercise his benevolence by himself alone; he simply sought out Shun with untiring urgency, and nothing more. Shun did not exercise his benevolence by himself alone; he simply sought out Yu and Gao Yao with untiring urgency, and nothing more. title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
屬及四岳九官十二牧之儔莫不交相舉讓合
天下以共成堯舜之仁由是隨山濬川而萬世
永賴之仁成焉洪水之憂以釋也樹藝五穀而
粒我烝民之仁成焉阻饑之憂以釋也敬敷五
教而勞來匡直之仁成焉不親不遜之憂以釋
也象刑惟明而風動率服之仁成焉猾夏之憂
以釋也治曆明時協月正日而庶績咸熙之仁
成焉失紀忒序之憂以釋也以至幽而天神地
祇微而草木鳥獸凡在覆載之內者靡不各得
===
其所而堯舜之憂可以少釋至是則不自用其
愛而天下莫不被其愛不自用其仁而天下莫
不受其仁堯舜之在當時吾見其垂衣裳而已
矣恭己南面而已矣不猶天道窿然穆然獨運
於上而無所作爲矣乎五臣四岳九官十二牧
之各効其職不猶二氣五行日月雨露風雷霜
雪之各呈其化者乎其地平天成時雍風動太
和在唐虞宇宙間不猶萬彙熙然生成於覆載
之內者乎至於平成雍和之績天下後世不以
punctuated: 屬，及四岳、九官、十二牧之儔，莫不交相舉讓，合天下以共成堯、舜之仁。由是隨山濬川，而萬世永賴之仁成焉，洪水之憂以釋也；樹藝五穀，而粒我烝民之仁成焉，阻饑之憂以釋也；敬敷五教，而勞來匡直之仁成焉，不親不遜之憂以釋也；象刑惟明，而風動率服之仁成焉，猾夏之憂以釋也；治曆明時，協月正日，而庶績咸熙之仁成焉，失紀忒序之憂以釋也。以至幽而天神地祇，微而草木鳥獸，凡在覆載之內者，靡不各得其所，而堯、舜之憂可以少釋。至是，則不自用其愛，而天下莫不被其愛；不自用其仁，而天下莫不受其仁。堯、舜之在當時，吾見其垂衣裳而已矣，恭己南面而已矣，不猶天道窿然穆然，獨運於上，而無所作爲矣乎？五臣、四岳、九官、十二牧之各効其職，不猶二氣、五行、日月、雨露、風雷、霜雪之各呈其化者乎？其地平天成、時雍風動、太和在唐、虞宇宙間，不猶萬彙熙然生成於覆載之內者乎？至於平成雍和之績，天下後世不以
translation_en: …associates, as well as the peers of the Four Peaks (Siyue), the Nine Officers (Jiuguan), and the Twelve Pastors (Shi'er mu)—none failed to recommend and yield to one another, uniting the world to jointly accomplish the benevolence of Yao and Shun. Through this, by following the mountains and dredging the rivers, the benevolence upon which ten thousand generations eternally rely was accomplished, and the worry over the floodwaters was thereby relieved; by planting and cultivating the five grains, the benevolence of feeding the multitude of the people was accomplished, and the worry over famine was thereby relieved; by reverently spreading the five teachings, the benevolence of encouraging, drawing in, correcting, and straightening was accomplished, and the worry over lack of affection and docility was thereby relieved; by making the statutory punishments clear, the benevolence of moving the people like the wind to submit and obey was accomplished, and the worry over subverters of the civilized realm was thereby relieved; by regulating the calendar and clarifying the seasons, harmonizing the months and rectifying the days, the benevolence of making all achievements flourish was accomplished, and the worry over losing the regularities and erring in the seasonal order was thereby relieved. Even down to the unseen spirits of Heaven and deities of Earth, and as minute as the grasses, trees, birds, and beasts—among all that were covered by Heaven and supported by Earth, there was none that did not attain its proper place, and the worries of Yao and Shun could be somewhat relieved. Having reached this point, they did not personally exercise their love, yet none in the world failed to be covered by their love; they did not personally exercise their benevolence, yet none in the world failed to receive their benevolence. As for Yao and Shun in their time, we see them merely letting their robes hang down, merely holding themselves in reverence while facing south! Is this not just like the Way of Heaven, lofty and profound, revolving alone on high without any deliberate action? As for the Five Ministers, the Four Peaks, the Nine Officers, and the Twelve Pastors each fulfilling their respective duties, is this not just like the Two Qi, the Five Phases, the sun and moon, rain and dew, wind and thunder, and frost and snow each manifesting their respective transformations? And as for the earth being leveled and heaven brought to completion, the times being harmonious and the people moved as by the wind, with supreme harmony prevailing throughout the universe of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun], is this not just like the myriad things flourishing and coming to life and maturity within the embrace of Heaven and Earth? When it comes to these achievements of leveling, completion, and harmonious peace, the world and later generations do not…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
歸之効力宣勞之臣必曰大哉堯爲君哉舜爲
不猶萬物以生以成二氣五行不能專其功必
歸諸無爲之天道矣乎堯舜配天之業其大如
此非得其幾舉天下之賢共理之安能仁覆天
下如此哉雖然代天而仁萬物者大君之道也
代君而仁萬民者家相之責也君道不徧求賢
而專其心於任相相道不親衆職而專其心於
求賢譬之爲巨室焉專任大匠而責之成者君
道也掄衆工而示之繩墨者相職也揮斧運斤
===
而執趨勤事者庶官之事也豈惟唐虞爲然風
牧任而皇運昌伊周相而王業盛前後乎此者
何莫不由斯道哉故善理天下者在任相善相
天下者在求賢賢才聚而相道得相道得而萬
國理矣有宗子家相之責而欲仁覆天下者其
亦於幾焉急之
表
擬宋尚書左僕射司馬光進稽古錄表元
祐元年
punctuated:
歸之効力宣勞之臣，必曰：「大哉，堯爲君！哉，舜爲！」不猶萬物以生以成，二氣、五行不能專其功，必歸諸無爲之天道矣乎？堯、舜配天之業其大如此，非得其幾，舉天下之賢共理之，安能仁覆天下如此哉？雖然，代天而仁萬物者，大君之道也；代君而仁萬民者，家相之責也。君道不徧求賢，而專其心於任相；相道不親衆職，而專其心於求賢。譬之爲巨室焉：專任大匠而責之成者，君道也；掄衆工而示之繩墨者，相職也；揮斧運斤而執趨勤事者，庶官之事也。豈惟唐、虞爲然？風、牧任而皇運昌，伊、周相而王業盛，前後乎此者，何莫不由斯道哉？故善理天下者在任相，善相天下者在求賢。賢才聚而相道得，相道得而萬國理矣。有宗子、家相之責而欲仁覆天下者，其亦於幾焉急之。

表
擬宋尚書左僕射司馬光進《稽古錄》表（元祐元年）
translation_en:
…attribute them to the ministers who exerted their strength and expended their toil, but inevitably say, “Great indeed was Yao as a ruler! [Great] indeed was Shun as [a ruler]!” Is this not just as when the myriad things are born and brought to completion, the two breaths and the five phases cannot monopolize the credit, which must instead be attributed to the non-acting Way of Heaven? The achievements of Yao and Shun that matched Heaven were as great as this; had they not grasped the pivotal spring of action and promoted the worthy men of the world to govern it together, how could their benevolence have covered the world like this? Even so, to act on behalf of Heaven and show benevolence to the myriad things is the Way of the great sovereign; to act on behalf of the sovereign and show benevolence to the myriad people is the responsibility of the chief minister (jiaxiang). The Way of the sovereign is not to seek out every worthy man himself, but to focus his mind on entrusting his chief minister; the Way of the chief minister is not to attend personally to the multitude of offices, but to focus his mind on seeking out worthy men. Compare it to building a great house: to give sole charge to the master carpenter and hold him responsible for its completion is the Way of the sovereign; to select the various artisans and show them the marking-line is the duty of the chief minister; to wield the axe and ply the adze, hastening to labor diligently at the work, is the business of the various officials. And was this true only of the eras of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun]? When Feng [Hou] and Li [Mu] were entrusted with office, the august destiny flourished; when Yi [Yin] and the Duke of Zhou served as chief ministers, the kingly enterprise prospered. Before and after them, who did not follow this Way? Therefore, being good at governing the world lies in entrusting the chief minister, and being good at serving as chief minister of the world lies in seeking out worthy men. When worthy talents gather, the Way of the chief minister is fulfilled; when the Way of the chief minister is fulfilled, the myriad states are well governed. Those who bear the responsibilities of the lineal heir [i.e., the sovereign] and the chief minister and who wish their benevolence to cover the world should likewise treat this pivotal spring as their urgent priority.

Memorial
A Draft Memorial on Behalf of Sima Guang, Left Executive of the Department of State Affairs of the Song, Presenting the Record of Investigating Antiquity (Jigu lu) (First Year of the Yuanyou Era [1086])

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
馮祥
同考試官教諭唐　批〔用古人本色語意組織成章不事絺繪而渾雅中自有藻麗是工于四六者〕
同考試官教諭竇　批〔敘述有體締構有法發宋臣忠愛之悃精切懇到錄之〕
考試官學正宋　批〔典則駢麗表之佳者〕
考試官教授劉　批〔溫雅得體〕
元祐元年某月某日臣司馬光恭進纂成
稽古錄者伏以
===
乾符啓運式宏保泰之圖
離象繼明爰重得師之義欲久安而長治必酌
古以準今載輯遺編用昭成憲臣光誠惶
誠恐稽首頓首竊惟勳華肇統虞書垂紀
事之文筆削傳心魯史立編年之灋學古
訓而有獲旨哉說命之詞率舊章以不愆
允矣假樂之咏殷惟鑒夏漢豈續秦蓋先
朝言動之詒瑕瑜莫掩而後代循違之則
方策是憑晉乘楚檮義咸有指孔林汲冢
punctuated:
馮祥

同考試官教諭唐　批〔用古人本色語意組織成章，不事絺繪，而渾雅中自有藻麗，是工于四六者。〕
同考試官教諭竇　批〔敘述有體，締構有法，發宋臣忠愛之悃，精切懇到，錄之。〕
考試官學正宋　批〔典則駢麗，表之佳者。〕
考試官教授劉　批〔溫雅得體。〕

元祐元年某月某日，臣司馬光恭進纂成《稽古錄》者。伏以乾符啓運，式宏保泰之圖；離象繼明，爰重得師之義。欲久安而長治，必酌古以準今；載輯遺編，用昭成憲。臣光誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊惟勳華肇統，《虞書》垂紀事之文；筆削傳心，魯史立編年之灋。「學古訓而有獲」，旨哉《說命》之詞；「率舊章以不愆」，允矣《假樂》之咏。殷惟鑒夏，漢豈續秦？蓋先朝言動之詒，瑕瑜莫掩；而後代循違之則，方策是憑。晉《乘》楚《檮》，義咸有指；孔林汲冢，
translation_en:
Feng Xiang 馮祥

Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Tang 唐 comments: [Weaving the authentic wording and meaning of the ancients into a coherent composition without resorting to artificial embellishment, yet possessing a natural ornate beauty within its dignified elegance—this is someone skilled in four-six parallel prose.]
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Dou 竇 comments: [The narration has proper form, and the structure is methodical. It brings forth the loyal and devoted sincerity of the Song minister with precision and earnestness. Selected for recording.]
Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Song 宋 comments: [Classical in standard and balanced in parallel beauty; an excellent memorial.]
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Liu 劉 comments: [Gentle, elegant, and fitting in style.]

On a certain day of a certain month in the first year of the Yuanyou reign [1086], Your servant Sima Guang 司馬光 respectfully presents the compiled Record of Investigating Antiquity (Jigu lu 稽古錄). Humbly I reflect that as the Heavenly tally opens the cycle of destiny, the grand design for preserving peace and prosperity is expanded; and as the trigram of Radiance succeeds in brightness, the principle of gaining worthy teachers is held in high esteem. To achieve enduring peace and lasting order, one must draw upon antiquity to regulate the present; thus I have compiled these transmitted texts to illuminate the established institutions. Your servant Guang, in utmost awe and trepidation, bows his head to the ground again and again.

I humbly reflect that when Yao and Shun initiated the imperial succession, the Book of Yu (Yushu 虞書) handed down writings that recorded events; and when Confucius transmitted his mind through editing and excision, the History of Lu (Lushi 魯史, i.e., the Spring and Autumn Annals) established the method of chronological annals. "Studying the ancient lessons yields rewards"—how profound are the words of the "Charge to Yue" (Yue ming 說命)! "Following the old statutes without error"—how true is the ode "Jia le" 假樂! Yin took Xia as its mirror; how could Han merely continue Qin? Indeed, in the words and deeds left behind by former dynasties, neither flaws nor merits can be concealed; and the standards for later generations to follow or avoid rely entirely upon the historical tablets and records. The Chariot (Sheng 乘) of Jin and the Block (Tao 檮, i.e., Taowu 檮杌) of Chu both had purposeful meaning; the texts from the Confucian family wall and the Ji commandery tomb…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
傳豈無因朝代遞遷纂脩愈富蘭臺芸省
日華燦毫素之章玉笥琅函雲彩簇汗青
之麗萃石渠之藏貯勞天祿之校讎詞約
事該荀悅見褒于漢紀傷繁溢實劉昫貽
希白虛煩南部之編何物最善益人魏主
發李先之對聚書蜀膺聖世隋文納牛監
之言開局莫盛于明皇懸購亦勤于顯德
勸懲無補述作徒蕃茲蓋伏遇
===
體道繼天
右文憲
祖前星涵瑞元德夙著于
青宮
永日承暉孝道懋隆于
紫閣閱論語究精微之蘊經藝同歸誦
寶訓識創守之囍繼述兼善讜議時聞
嘉納定
punctuated: 傳豈無因。朝代遞遷，纂脩愈富；蘭臺芸省，日華燦毫素之章；玉笥琅函，雲彩簇汗青之麗。萃石渠之藏貯，勞天祿之校讎。詞約事該，荀悅見褒于《漢紀》；傷繁溢實，劉昫貽希白虛煩《南部》之編。「何物最善益人」，魏主發李先之對；「聚書蜀膺聖世」，隋文納牛監之言。開局莫盛于明皇，懸購亦勤于顯德；勸懲無補，述作徒蕃。茲蓋伏遇體道繼天，右文憲祖。前星涵瑞，元德夙著于青宮；永日承暉，孝道懋隆于紫閣。閱《論語》究精微之蘊，經藝同歸；誦《寶訓》識創守之囍，繼述兼善。讜議時聞嘉納，定
translation_en:
… how could their transmission be without cause? As dynasties succeeded one another in turn, historical compilation grew ever richer: in the Orchid Terrace and the Rue Pavilion, the sun's brilliance illuminated writings done with brush and silk; in jade coffers and gemmed cases, cloud-like colors clustered around the beauty of bamboo-slip histories. Gathering the holdings stored in the Stone Canal Pavilion (Shiqu ge), scholars labored over collation in the Pavilion of Heavenly Blessing (Tianlu ge). Because his words were concise and his facts comprehensive, Xun Yue 荀悅 was praised for his Annals of the Han (Han ji 漢紀); marred by verbosity and exceeding the facts, Liu Xu 劉昫 [gap in original—and Qian] Xibai 錢希白 vainly troubled themselves with compiling the New History of the Southern [Tang] (Nanbu xinshu 南部新書) [?]. Asking "what thing in the world is best for benefiting mankind," the ruler of Northern Wei elicited the reply of Li Xian 李先; noting that "the gathering of books suitably falls to a sage age" [?], Emperor Wen of Sui accepted the words of the Director of the Palace Library Niu Hong 牛弘. The opening of historiographical bureaus was never more flourishing than under Emperor Minghuang of Tang, and the offering of rewards to purchase books was likewise diligent during the Xiande era (954–960) of Later Zhou; yet when they offered no aid to encouragement of virtue and warning against vice, such writings merely proliferated in vain.

Now, I humbly encounter Your Majesty, who embodies the Way and succeeds to Heaven, exalting culture and modeling Yourself on Your ancestors. When the Fore-star held auspicious portents, Your primal virtue was already manifest early in the Eastern Palace; through lengthening days receiving the sun's radiance, Your filial piety flourishes grandly in the Purple Towers. Reading the Analects (Lunyu 論語), You probe the subtleties of its profound meaning, showing how the classics and arts converge; reciting the Precious Injunctions (Baoxun 寶訓), You recognize the hardships of founding and preserving the dynasty, excelling in both continuing the work and transmitting the intentions of Your predecessors. Honest counsels are constantly heard and graciously accepted by You, establishing…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
國是以不疑正人疊見登庸快
廟謨之允協如〔臣光〕者甘棲遲于洛社望絕
巖廊被
寵召于台垣榮生劒履扶趨
丹陛感刻赤衷矢心犬馬之餘齡勉圖報稱藉
手蟲魚之小技謹用編摩憶事
先皇曾承
明詔合衆史以爲通鑑藏副本可備
進呈但
===
聖主政總萬幾豈屑尋章摘句而微〔臣〕慮攄一
得當爲挈領提綱必姑撫其大凡刋落俳
諧黃石庶少裨于
清暇比同敬義丹書由昊羲臨御以來迄
英廟治平之末序運祚推移之次上下餘數千
年鉤紀載體要之玄首尾僅二十卷歷年
圖百官表並會輯以成書三君德五治才
仍僭踰而著論心懷惻隱剛斷畢照乎忠
邪運值艱難弘濟常師乎賢智理亂明如
punctuated: 國是以不疑；正人疊見登庸，快廟謨之允協。如〔臣光〕者，甘棲遲于洛社，望絕巖廊；被寵召于台垣，榮生劒履。扶趨丹陛，感刻赤衷；矢心犬馬之餘齡，勉圖報稱；藉手蟲魚之小技，謹用編摩。憶事先皇，曾承明詔，合衆史以爲《通鑑》，藏副本可備進呈。但聖主政總萬幾，豈屑尋章摘句；而微〔臣〕慮攄一得，當爲挈領提綱。必姑撫其大凡，刋落俳諧黃石；庶少裨于清暇，比同敬義丹書。由昊羲臨御以來，迄英廟治平之末，序運祚推移之次，上下餘數千年；鉤紀載體要之玄，首尾僅二十卷。《歷年圖》、《百官表》，並會輯以成書；三君德、五治才，仍僭踰而著論。心懷惻隱，剛斷畢照乎忠邪；運值艱難，弘濟常師乎賢智。理亂明如
translation_en: …the fundamental policy of the state without hesitation; upright men are repeatedly promoted and employed, rejoicing in the fitting harmony of the dynastic counsels. As for one such as Your Servant Sima Guang (光), I was content to live in retirement in the Luoyang society, having abandoned all hope of the high court; yet I received a favored summons to the chief ministerial offices, bringing honor to my sword and shoes. Supported as I hasten to the vermilion steps, gratitude is engraved in my loyal heart; I swear in my remaining years of dog-and-horse service to strive to repay Your grace, and relying on my petty skill in textual scholarship, I have respectfully engaged in compilation. I recall that when serving the late Emperor, I once received his illustrious decree to combine the various histories into the Comprehensive Mirror (Tongjian 通鑑), storing a duplicate copy in readiness for presentation to the throne. However, since the Sage Ruler oversees a myriad of state affairs, how could He deign to pluck out phrases and sentences? And as Your humble servant seeks to offer a single humble insight, I ought to lift the collar and grasp the main cord. I must tentatively gather the broad outlines, pruning away the playful words of the Yellow Stone; perhaps this may slightly benefit Your pure leisure, comparable to the Cinnabar Book of Reverence and Righteousness. From the reign of Taihao Fuxi (昊羲) down to the end of the Zhiping (治平) era (1064–1067) of the late Emperor Yingzong (英廟), it arranges the sequence of the shifting of destinies and thrones, spanning more than several thousand years from beginning to end; drawing out the profound essentials of the historical records, from start to finish it comprises a mere twenty scrolls. The Chronological Charts (Linian tu 歷年圖) and the Tables of Officials (Baiguan biao 百官表) have both been compiled together to complete the work; on the three virtues of a ruler and the five talents of governance, I have furthermore presumptuously composed discourses. When the heart harbors compassion, firm decisiveness fully illuminates loyalty and wickedness; when fortune meets with hardship, great deliverance always takes the worthy and wise as its masters. Order and disorder are as clear as…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
指掌應感易于噬膚取義尚書命名稽古
研丹鉛而抱槧青藜散太乙之精積緗縹
以充囊彤管應文昌之宿謝三長之上乘
學愧左狐立兩漢之下風才非班馬雜組
何資于
宸職薄櫨敢壯乎
宸居忠效傾葵寶鑑續千秋之撰
恩祈采菲瑤編塵
乙夜之觀避覆轍而仰高山深惟華衮斧鉞
===
睠
宵衣而釐
旰食有取穀粟桑麻伏願
緒纘執中惟精惟一
道宗建極是訓是行法不貴新更化必期于
善治人惟求舊稽謀自裕于
格天
聖德集乎大成
帝業隆于富有
punctuated: 指掌，應感易于噬膚。取義《尚書》，命名《稽古》。研丹鉛而抱槧，青藜散太乙之精；積緗縹以充囊，彤管應文昌之宿。謝三長之上乘，學愧左狐；立兩漢之下風，才非班馬。雜組何資于宸職，薄櫨敢壯乎宸居？忠效傾葵，寶鑑續《千秋》之撰；恩祈采菲，瑤編塵乙夜之觀。避覆轍而仰高山，深惟華衮斧鉞；睠宵衣而釐旰食，有取穀粟桑麻。伏願緒纘執中，惟精惟一；道宗建極，是訓是行。法不貴新，更化必期于善治；人惟求舊，稽謀自裕于格天。聖德集乎大成，帝業隆于富有。
translation_en: … pointing to the palm of one's hand, and response and resonance are as easy as biting through tender skin. Drawing its meaning from the Book of Documents (Shangshu), I have named it Investigating Antiquity (Jigu). Grinding cinnabar and lead while clasping my writing tablets, the green goosefoot staff scatters the essence of the Great Unity (Taiyi); amassing light-yellow and pale-blue silk scrolls to fill my satchels, the red-lacquered brush responds to the constellation of Literary Glory (Wenchang). Falling short of the supreme vehicle of the three historiographical excellences, in learning I am ashamed before Zuo Qiuming and Dong Hu; standing downwind of the two Han dynasties, my talent is not that of Ban Gu or Sima Qian. How could such miscellaneous braided ribbons aid the Imperial Duties, or such thin capital-blocks dare to lend majesty to the Imperial Residence? In loyalty I emulate the sunflower leaning toward the sun, offering a precious mirror to continue the compilation of the Thousand Autumns (Qianqiu); for grace I pray that you gather even the humble radish, letting these jade-like pages taint the perusal of your second night-watch. Avoiding overturned ruts and looking up to high mountains, I deeply ponder the ceremonial robe of praise and the battle-axe of censure; gazing with devotion upon your dressing before dawn and ordering your meals after dusk, I find value in the plain sustenance of grain, millet, mulberry, and hemp. I humbly wish that you may continue the heritage of holding fast to the Mean, being refined and single-minded; and take as your principle the Way of establishing the Supreme Standard, instructing in it and putting it into practice. Laws are not prized for novelty, as reforming customs must aim at good governance; in men one seeks only those of old, as consulting their counsels naturally suffices to reach Heaven. May your Sagely Virtue gather the great synthesis, and the Imperial Enterprise flourish in abundant possession. …

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
覲耿光而揚丕烈長爲仁義禮樂之宗
凝景命以迓洪庥永作夷夏臣民之主臣無
任瞻
天仰
聖激切屛營之至謹奉
表隨
進以
聞

策

趙完

祖宗心學淵微之妙綜括對揚章章悉著而陳善矢謨有裨
君德宜錄以
聞
同考試官教諭何　批〔聖學心法敷對精詳且鄭成至言諄諄見于篇末忠愛藹如可誦也〕
punctuated:
覲耿光而揚丕烈，長爲仁義禮樂之宗；凝景命以迓洪庥，永作夷夏臣民之主。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屛營之至，謹奉表隨進以聞。

第叄場

策

第一問

趙完
同考試官教諭阮　批〔帝王道統精邃之傳，祖宗心學淵微之妙，綜括對揚，章章悉著；而陳善矢謨，有裨君德，宜錄以聞。〕
同考試官教諭何　批〔聖學心法，敷對精詳；且鄭成至言，諄諄見于篇末，忠愛藹如，可誦也。〕
translation_en:
…beholding the bright glory and extolling the great achievements, may Your Majesty forever stand as the exemplar of benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and music; consolidating the glorious Mandate to welcome vast blessings, may Your Majesty eternally reign as the sovereign of subjects both Chinese and foreign. Your servant is overcome with the utmost awe and earnest trepidation in gazing up at Heaven and revering Your Sacred Majesty, and respectfully presents this memorial along with the tribute to inform the Throne.

Third Session

Policy Essays (ce)

First Question

Zhao Wan 趙完
Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Ruan comments: [The profound transmission of the orthodox Way of the emperors and kings, and the deep, subtle wonders of the learning of the mind-and-heart of our Imperial Ancestors, are comprehensively summarized and set forth in reply, everything made brilliantly clear. Moreover, its exposition of goodness and presentation of counsels are beneficial to the Sovereign's virtue; it is fitting to record this to inform the Throne.]
Associate Examiner and Instructor He comments: [The method of the mind-and-heart in sage learning is expounded and answered with precision and detail. Furthermore, earnest and consummate words [?] appear repeatedly at the end of the essay, overflowing with loyalty and affection—truly worthy of recitation.]

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正宋　批〔得聖學體要取之〕
考試官教授劉　批〔敘學有據〕
帝王之道一心焉盡之矣本諸心以懋學
則其學也憲乎天而昭日新之盛由是心
以出治則其業也格乎天而顯富有之隆
何謂學凡稽乎古訓往牒者是已苟非心
以端其原則雖炳然蔚然亦詞章之習耳
無以成經緯之能何謂業凡著之成功文
章者是已苟非學以大其基則雖巍然煥
然亦粉飾之具耳何以弘參贊之用惟純
天以端懋學之本而憲天以隆建業之基
則心外無道道外無治而帝王之能事畢
矣嗚呼此心學之傳一盛於唐虞再盛於
我
===
祖宗也其在
今日尤當遠宗近守者乎執事首策諸生而
舉董仲舒正心之言朱熹誠正之學爲問
計欲採芻蕘意也敢不摭拾以對乎宋儒
punctuated:
考試官學正宋　批〔得聖學體要，取之。〕
考試官教授劉　批〔敘學有據。〕
帝王之道，一心焉盡之矣。本諸心以懋學，則其學也憲乎天，而昭日新之盛；由是心以出治，則其業也格乎天，而顯富有之隆。何謂學？凡稽乎古訓往牒者是已。苟非心以端其原，則雖炳然蔚然，亦詞章之習耳，無以成經緯之能。何謂業？凡著之成功文章者是已。苟非學以大其基，則雖巍然煥然，亦粉飾之具耳，何以弘參贊之用？惟純天以端懋學之本，而憲天以隆建業之基，則心外無道，道外無治，而帝王之能事畢矣。嗚呼！此心學之傳，一盛於唐虞，再盛於我祖宗也，其在今日，尤當遠宗近守者乎！執事首策諸生，而舉董仲舒正心之言、朱熹誠正之學爲問，計欲採芻蕘意也，敢不摭拾以對乎？宋儒
translation_en:
Examiner Song, Subprefectural Director of Studies, comments: "He has grasped the substance and essentials of sage learning; select him."
Examiner Liu, Prefectural Director of Studies, comments: "His exposition on learning is well-grounded."
The Way of emperors and kings is exhausted entirely within the single mind. When one bases oneself on the mind to pursue learning diligently, that learning takes Heaven as its model and manifests the flourishing of daily renewal; when one proceeds from this mind to bring forth governance, that enterprise reaches up to Heaven and displays the grandeur of abundant possession. What is meant by "learning"? It refers to all investigation into ancient precepts and past records. If it is not rooted in the mind to rectify its source, then even if it is brilliant and luxuriant, it is merely the habit of ornate composition, incapable of achieving the ability to weave the warp and woof of the realm. What is meant by "enterprise"? It refers to all that is manifested in accomplished merit and cultural brilliance. If it does not rely on learning to enlarge its foundation, then even if it is lofty and resplendent, it is merely an instrument of superficial embellishment—how could it broaden the function of participating in the transformative nourishing of Heaven and Earth? Only by remaining purely aligned with Heaven to rectify the root of diligent learning, and taking Heaven as one's model to elevate the foundation of establishing one's enterprise, will there be no Way outside the mind and no governance outside the Way, and the whole duty of emperors and kings will be complete. Alas! This transmission of the learning of the mind flourished first under Yao and Shun, and flourished a second time under our Imperial Ancestors. Today, ought we not all the more revere the distant model and uphold the near one? Your Honor, in your first policy question to us students, has raised Dong Zhongshu's words on rectifying the mind and Zhu Xi's learning of making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind as your inquiry, planning thereby to gather the views of humble woodcutters and grass-gatherers. How dare I not gather up my thoughts to reply? The Song Confucian…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
胡安國有言曰明君以務學爲急聖學以
正心爲要甚哉有味乎其言也觀書之始
終典學詩之緝熙光明信乎非正心不足
以言學非務學不足以語明也羲皇以前
遐哉邈乎不可尚已自堯傳曆數虞庭紹
之有惟精惟一之旨焉其曰惟危惟微者
言幾之當辨也嗣後若禹之祗台德先湯
之聖敬日躋文之敬止緝熙武之敬勝義
勝而心學之源開矣天啓斯文孔門衍之
===
有誠意正心之訓焉其曰必愼其獨者言
幾之當謹也於時若顔子之四勿曾子之
一貫子思之戒謹恐懼孟子之知言養氣
而心學之流遠矣是數聖賢者雖言有詳
略時有先後淵乎皆聖學宗旨矣三代而
下英君誼辟代有作者治業非不卓然可
觀也然不事詩書如高帝徒騁乎馬上之
風表章六經如武帝無救於輪臺之悔語
治最爲近古者且然矣况唐之大綱未正
punctuated: 胡安國有言曰：「明君以務學爲急，聖學以正心爲要。」甚哉！有味乎其言也。觀《書》之「始終典學」、《詩》之「緝熙光明」，信乎非正心不足以言學，非務學不足以語明也。羲皇以前，遐哉邈乎，不可尚已。自堯傳曆數，虞庭紹之，有「惟精惟一」之旨焉；其曰「惟危惟微」者，言幾之當辨也。嗣後若禹之「祗台德先」、湯之「聖敬日躋」、文之「敬止緝熙」、武之「敬勝義勝」，而心學之源開矣。天啓斯文，孔門衍之，有「誠意正心」之訓焉；其曰「必愼其獨」者，言幾之當謹也。於時若顔子之「四勿」、曾子之「一貫」、子思之「戒謹恐懼」、孟子之「知言養氣」，而心學之流遠矣。是數聖賢者，雖言有詳略，時有先後，淵乎皆聖學宗旨矣。三代而下，英君誼辟代有作者，治業非不卓然可觀也。然不事《詩》《書》如高帝，徒騁乎馬上之風；表章《六經》如武帝，無救於輪臺之悔。語治最爲近古者且然矣，况唐之大綱未正，
translation_en: … Hu Anguo 胡安國 had a saying: "An enlightened ruler takes devotion to learning as his urgent task, and sage learning takes rectifying the mind as its essential point." How profound and full of meaning are his words! Looking at "constant devotion to learning from beginning to end" in the Book of Documents (Shu) and "continuing in bright illumination" in the Book of Odes (Shi), truly, without rectifying the mind one cannot speak of learning, and without devoting oneself to learning one cannot speak of enlightenment. Before the august Fuxi 伏羲, things are so remote and distant that nothing further can be added. From the time Yao 堯 transmitted the calendar-destiny and the court of Yu 虞 [Shun 舜] succeeded him, there was the purport of "be discriminating, be undivided"; when it says "precarious" and "subtle," it speaks of how the incipient springs of action ought to be discerned. Thereafter, through such things as Yu's 禹 "reverently attending to my virtue first," Tang's 湯 "sagely reverence daily ascending," King Wen's 文 "reverently resting and continuing in bright illumination," and King Wu's 武 "reverence prevailing and righteousness prevailing," the source of the learning of the mind (xinxue 心學) was opened up. When Heaven inspired this culture, the school of Confucius 孔子 elaborated it, and there was the instruction of "making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind"; when it says "one must be watchful over oneself when alone," it speaks of how the incipient springs of action ought to be guarded with care. At that time, through such things as Master Yan's 顏子 "four prohibitions," Master Zeng's 曾子 "one thread binding all," Zisi's 子思 "caution, wariness, fear, and trembling," and Mencius's 孟子 "understanding words and nourishing vital energy," the stream of the learning of the mind flowed far. Although among these several sages and worthies their words varied in detail and their eras came earlier or later, how profound—all of them embodied the fundamental doctrine of sage learning! From the Three Dynasties downward, heroic rulers and righteous sovereigns arose in every generation, and their achievements in governance were not without towering distinction worth beholding. Yet one who did not occupy himself with the Odes and Documents, like Emperor Gao 高帝 [of Han], merely galloped along in the manner of ruling from horseback; and one who exalted the Six Classics, like Emperor Wu 武帝 [of Han], could not save himself from the regret of Luntai 輪臺. If even those whose governance is spoken of as closest to antiquity were like this, how much more so the Tang 唐, whose great fundamental principles were never rectified …

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
