而治雜於夷宋之萬目徒舉而勢終不振
者耶雖率邇者踵武逖聽者風聲而心學
槩乎未聞焉其與古帝王之治逕庭矣洪
惟我
太祖高皇帝開天立極置天下於仁義禮樂之
區創造之業隆矣迺於
萬幾之暇究心經史其載諸
日曆政要者如悟頤卦養民之職識家人誠
嚴之旨語無逸兢惕之心講洪範類應之
===
理此皆得於論經者也謂漢文帝當制禮
樂以復三代謂唐玄宗當廣視聽以任賢
能謂宋眞宗以天書媚悅侈其心謂元季
以宴安跋扈失其柄此皆得於論史者也
評隲精詳凜乎衮鉞之嚴矣而其
諭宋濂有曰人心虛靈乘氣機以出入操而
存之爲難朕罔敢自暇自逸於會則曰人
君一心治化之本存諸中者無堯舜之心欲
施諸政者有堯舜之治不可得也是其端
punctuated: 而治雜於夷，宋之萬目徒舉而勢終不振者耶？雖率邇者踵武，逖聽者風聲，而心學槩乎未聞焉，其與古帝王之治逕庭矣。洪惟我太祖高皇帝，開天立極，置天下於仁義禮樂之區，創造之業隆矣。迺於萬幾之暇，究心經史。其載諸《日曆》、《政要》者：如悟《頤》卦養民之職，識《家人》誠嚴之旨，語《無逸》兢惕之心，講《洪範》類應之理，此皆得於論經者也；謂漢文帝當制禮樂以復三代，謂唐玄宗當廣視聽以任賢能，謂宋眞宗以天書媚悅侈其心，謂元季以宴安跋扈失其柄，此皆得於論史者也。評隲精詳，凜乎衮鉞之嚴矣。而其諭宋濂有曰：「人心虛靈，乘氣機以出入，操而存之爲難，朕罔敢自暇自逸。」於會則曰：「人君一心，治化之本。存諸中者無堯、舜之心，欲施諸政者有堯、舜之治，不可得也。」是其端
translation_en:
…and its governance was adulterated with barbarian ways, or the Song, where myriad details were attended to in vain while its strength ultimately failed to revive? Even though those nearby followed in their footsteps and those far away heard the wind of their reputation, the learning of the mind-and-heart (xinxue) went completely unheard of among them; thus their governance was worlds apart from that of the ancient sage-emperors and kings.

Humbly reflecting upon our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu, r. 1368–1398): he opened the heavens and established the supreme standard, placing the realm within the domain of benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and music; his founding achievement was grand indeed! Yet in his leisure from the myriad affairs of state, he devoted his mind to the Classics and the Histories. As recorded in the Daily Records (Rili) and Essentials of Governance (Zhengyao): hecomprehended the duty of nourishing the people in the Yi ("Nourishment") hexagram, recognized the principle of sincerity and strictness in the Jiaren ("Family") hexagram, spoke of the cautious and vigilant mind in the "Against Luxurious Ease" ("Wuyi") chapter, and expounded the principle of categorical correspondence in the "Great Plan" ("Hongfan") chapter—all of these were insights gained from discussing the Classics. He stated that Emperor Wen of Han ought to have instituted礼樂 (ritual and music) to restore the Three Dynasties, that Emperor Xuanzong of Tang ought to have broadened his vision and hearing to employ the worthy and capable, that Emperor Zhenzong of Song let his mind grow extravagant through the flattery of the "Heavenly Texts," and that the late Yuan lost its authority through indulgent ease and overbearing subordinates—all of these were insights gained from discussing the Histories. His evaluations were precise and detailed, awe-inspiring in the strictness of their praise and blame.

Moreover, in instructing Song Lian 宋濂, he once said: "The human mind is numinous and subtle, moving in and out upon the mechanism of vital energy (qi); to grasp and preserve it is difficult, so We dare not allow Ourselves idle ease." And to吳會 [? Hội / Wu Hui] he said: "The one mind of the ruler is the root of governance and transformation. If what is preserved within lacks the mind of Yao and Shun, then to wish for what is applied in administration to possess the governance of Yao and Shun is impossible." Thus, the way he rectified…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
聖學之本者固此心也
成祖文皇帝繼天纘緒還天下以紀綱法度之
正繼述之業偉矣迺於
靖難之餘怡神典籍其見於纂述編摹者如
著
聖學心法而帝王之學弘輯性理大全而載道
之文顯編爲善隂騭而天人之理會纂孝
順事實而百行之原脩此則頒布以廣其
傳也謂侍臣以前代大儒皆以積造勤其
基謂儒臣以置書不難須常覽閱因進講
義而悟克明峻德因進經書而言披閱不
倦此則博極以會其精也議論精嚴昭然
典則之垂矣而其
===
諭解縉則曰人心一有好樂不返則欲必勝
理若心能静虚事來則應事去如明鏡止水
自然純是天理其序書則曰治本於道道本
於心六經之道明則天地聖人之心可見而
致治之功可成是其端
punctuated:
聖學之本者，固此心也。
成祖文皇帝繼天纘緒，還天下以紀綱法度之正，繼述之業偉矣！迺於靖難之餘，怡神典籍。其見於纂述編摹者，如著《聖學心法》而帝王之學弘，輯《性理大全》而載道之文顯，編《爲善隂騭》而天人之理會，纂《孝順事實》而百行之原脩，此則頒布以廣其傳也；謂侍臣以前代大儒皆以積造勤其基，謂儒臣以置書不難、須常覽閱，因進講義而悟「克明峻德」，因進經書而言披閱不倦，此則博極以會其精也。議論精嚴，昭然典則之垂矣。而其諭解縉則曰：「人心一有好樂不返，則欲必勝理。若心能静虚，事來則應，事去如明鏡止水，自然純是天理。」其序《書》則曰：「治本於道，道本於心。六經之道明，則天地聖人之心可見，而致治之功可成。」是其端
translation_en:
… establishes the foundation of sagely learning is assuredly this mind.

Emperor Wen, the Accomplished Ancestor (Chengzu, the Yongle Emperor), succeeded to Heaven's mandate and continued the imperial line, restoring to the realm the correctness of fundamental laws and institutions; magnificent indeed was his enterprise of inheritance and continuation! Moreover, in his leisure after the Pacification of the Crisis (Jingnan), he delighted his spirit in canonical books. As for what was manifested in his compilations and editions: he composed the Methods of the Mind in Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa), whereby the learning of emperors and kings was broadened; he compiled the Great Compendium on Human Nature and Principle (Xingli daquan), whereby writings that convey the Way were made manifest; he edited the Secret Merits of Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi), whereby the principles of Heaven and humanity were brought into convergence; and he compiled the True Records of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi), whereby the source of the hundred conducts was cultivated. These works were promulgated so as to widen their transmission. He told his attendant officials that the great Confucians of former dynasties all diligently laid their foundations through cumulative attainment; he told his Confucian officials that acquiring books is not difficult, but that one must constantly read and peruse them; upon being presented with lecture expositions, he comprehended the meaning of "being able to make illustrious one's lofty virtue"; and upon being presented with the Classics, he spoke of perusing them tirelessly. This was his reaching the utmost breadth in order to grasp their essence. His discussions were precise and rigorous, shiningly handing down canonical standards. Furthermore, in his instructions to Xie Jin 解縉, he said: "Once the human mind has fondness and pleasure from which it does not return, desires will inevitably prevail over principle. If the mind can be tranquil and empty—responding when affairs arrive, and being like a bright mirror and still water when affairs pass—it will naturally be purely heavenly principle." And in his preface to the Book of Documents (Shu), he said: "Governance is rooted in the Way, and the Way is rooted in the mind. When the Way of the Six Classics is made clear, the mind of Heaven, Earth, and the sages can be seen, and the achievement of bringing about good governance can be completed." Thus, that by which he…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
聖學之本者亦此心也卽其燦然而推其所以
然所謂根極體要者非耶
列聖相承契合無間曁我
世宗肅皇帝兼
神聖之資撫
中興之運因講大學衍義則
著翼學詩如曰帝王所圖治務學常爲先萬
化脩身始朕念方拳拳是端本善則之道也
因講經史則
===
賦備覽詩如曰靈臺虛而明燭物別垢臧好
善而惡惡罔非本其良是體用一源之學也
而
敬一有箴獨契執中之旨
五箴有註遠稽心法之精
天葩璀燦炳耀日星
睿藻煇煌昭回雲漢誠極經緯之章而擅巍煥
之盛矣蓋其心卽
二祖之心故其學卽
punctuated: 聖學之本者，亦此心也。卽其燦然而推其所以然，所謂根極體要者非耶？列聖相承，契合無間。曁我世宗肅皇帝，兼神聖之資，撫中興之運。因講《大學衍義》，則著《翼學詩》，如曰：「帝王所圖治，務學常爲先。萬化脩身始，朕念方拳拳。」是端本善則之道也。因講經史，則賦《備覽詩》，如曰：「靈臺虛而明，燭物別垢臧。好善而惡惡，罔非本其良。」是體用一源之學也。而《敬一》有箴，獨契執中之旨；《五箴》有註，遠稽心法之精。天葩璀燦，炳耀日星；睿藻煇煌，昭回雲漢。誠極經緯之章，而擅巍煥之盛矣！蓋其心卽二祖之心，故其學卽
translation_en:
… the foundation of sagely learning is also this very mind. By examining its brilliant manifestations and deducing the underlying principles by which it is so, is this not what is called grasping the ultimate foundation and essential substance?

The successive sage emperors inherited this from one another, their minds tallying without the slightest gap. When it came to our Emperor Shizong Su (the Jiajing Emperor), he combined divine and sagely endowments and presided over an era of dynastic revival. On the occasion of lectures on the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi), he composed the "Poem on Assisting Learning" (Yixue shi), which says: "In what emperors and kings plan for governance, devoting oneself to learning always comes first; ten thousand transformations begin with cultivating the person, and Our thoughts are earnestly fixed on this." This is the Way of rectifying the foundation and perfecting the model. On the occasion of lectures on the Classics and Histories, he composed the "Poem on Comprehensive Reading" (Beilan shi), which says: "When the numinous terrace [the mind] is empty and bright, it illuminates things and distinguishes the tainted from the good; loving goodness and hating evil, none of this fails to stem from its innate goodness." This is the learning in which substance and function share a single source.

Furthermore, his Admonition on Reverent Unity (Jingyi zhen) uniquely grasped the import of holding fast to the Mean, and his commentaries on the Five Admonitions (Wuzhen) reached far back to examine the essence of the method of the mind. His heavenly blossoms were resplendent, shining as brightly as the sun and stars; his imperial compositions were glorious, revolving luminously like the Milky Way. Truly, he reached the pinnacle of literary pattern that orders the world, and commanded the full magnificence of lofty brilliance! Indeed, because his mind was none other than the mind of the Two Ancestors (Taizu and Taizong), his learning was none other than…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
二祖之學而四十餘年之治業至於今耿耿爲
烈者謂非相授守一道不可也而質之帝
王奚異哉我
皇上英資天縱盛德日新
臨御以來嘉與百執事共圖理道凡納忠諫任
賢能飭吏治謹邊防規模恢恢乎宏遠矣
是以海内乂安蠻夷卒俾懷生之類靡不
霑濡浸潤協氣橫流武節飄迅治業之隆
將遠軼唐虞而與
===
祖宗同一轍者猗歟盛矣然我
皇上典學之心方且烝烝然如日方升也故
經筵日講之制亟懋懋於緝熙
宸翰召詢之儀益勤於
眷諭是所以務學者固
聖聖相傳之心也執事欲求進於此焉則
召對進講之制不有可言者乎夫帝王繼明於
離纘緒也多識於畜師古也而泰交其輔
焉心學之懋所繇也是不可不講也今
punctuated: 二祖之學，而四十餘年之治業，至於今耿耿爲烈者，謂非相授守一道不可也，而質之帝王奚異哉？我皇上英資天縱，盛德日新，臨御以來，嘉與百執事共圖理道，凡納忠諫、任賢能、飭吏治、謹邊防，規模恢恢乎宏遠矣！是以海内乂安，蠻夷卒俾，懷生之類，靡不霑濡浸潤，協氣橫流，武節飄迅，治業之隆，將遠軼唐虞，而與祖宗同一轍者，猗歟盛矣！然我皇上典學之心，方且烝烝然如日方升也。故經筵、日講之制，亟懋懋於緝熙；宸翰、召詢之儀，益勤於眷諭。是所以務學者，固聖聖相傳之心也。執事欲求進於此焉，則召對、進講之制，不有可言者乎？夫帝王繼明於離，纘緒也；多識於畜，師古也；而泰交其輔焉，心學之懋所繇也，是不可不講也。今
translation_en:
… the learning of the Two Progenitors, and the achievements of his rule over more than forty years remain gloriously resplendent to this day; one cannot say that this was not the transmission and preservation of a single Way—and when measured against the ancient emperors and kings, how does it differ?

Our August Emperor, endowed by Heaven with heroic talent and daily renewing his abundant virtue, since ascending the throne has graciously joined with all his officials to plan the Way of governance. In accepting loyal remonstrance, employing the worthy and capable, rectifying official administration, and guarding the frontiers with care, his grand design is vast and far-reaching indeed! Consequently, all within the seas is at peace, the foreign tribes submit at last, and all living beings without exception are steeped in his grace; harmonious vital energy flows everywhere, military might moves swiftly, and the flourishing of his governance will far surpass that of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun] while following in the very same tracks as the Imperial Ancestors—oh, how magnificent!

Yet our August Emperor's mind, ever devoted to constant learning, is advancing upwards just like the rising sun. Therefore, the institutions of the Classics Mat (jingyan) and the Daily Lectures (rijiang) are pursued with utmost diligence toward radiant illumination, and the ceremonies of imperial calligraphy and summoned inquiries grow ever more industrious in gracious instruction. This devotion to learning is truly the mind transmitted from sage to sage. Since you, Sir, wish to seek further progress in this, is there not something that may be said regarding the institutions of summoned audiences and lectures at court? Now, when emperors and kings succeed to brilliance as in the hexagram Li, it is to continue the dynastic line; when they acquaint themselves with many things as in the hexagram Dachu, it is to take antiquity as their teacher; and when they commune in harmony with their ministers as in the hexagram Tai, that is the means by which the learning of the mind (xinxue) flourishes—this cannot go unexamined. Nowadays, when [His Majesty]…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
御門聽政辨色而入日出而
視之非不肅肅然有禮也然分嚴於天澤時
限於須臾凡政事得失人才進退邈乎一
未之聞焉則與唐虞之都俞吁咈者尚遠
也請於
聽治之後一弘
召對之規如韓琦每日奏對務竭忠猷以裨實
政可也如魏相每於御前必條故事以補
政缺可也況
===
先朝有已試之效乎故欲計屯田鹽法之宜
而臨淮洛陽得畢慮焉欲定邊備虜情之
筭而均陽華容得決策焉亦可做其意而
行之歟今講讀備官循次而進展卷而陳
之非不秩秩然有章也然書有定限講有
定期則德性所知氣質所就意者未能擴
充焉其於程子所謂涵養薰陶者尚缺也
請於
進講之餘一開規諫之路如范氏善惡之說
punctuated: 御門聽政，辨色而入，日出而視之，非不肅肅然有禮也。然分嚴於天澤，時限於須臾，凡政事得失、人才進退，邈乎一未之聞焉，則與唐、虞之都俞吁咈者尚遠也。請於聽治之後，一弘召對之規：如韓琦每日奏對，務竭忠猷以裨實政，可也；如魏相每於御前，必條故事以補政缺，可也。況先朝有已試之效乎？故欲計屯田、鹽法之宜，而臨淮、洛陽得畢慮焉；欲定邊備、虜情之筭，而均陽、華容得決策焉。亦可做其意而行之歟！今講讀備官，循次而進，展卷而陳之，非不秩秩然有章也。然書有定限，講有定期，則德性所知、氣質所就，意者未能擴充焉，其於程子所謂涵養薰陶者尚缺也。請於進講之餘，一開規諫之路：如范氏善惡之說，
translation_en:
…When His Majesty holds court at the palace gate to attend to state affairs, the officials enter as dawn breaks and he gives audience as the sun rises—this is not without solemn decorum. Yet because the distinction between ruler and subject is as strict as that between Heaven and marsh, and the time allotted is limited to a brief moment, nothing at all is heard from afar regarding the successes and failures of administration or the promotion and dismissal of men of talent; this is still far removed from the mutually responsive deliberations—"Oh!", "Yes!", "Alas!", "No!"—of the eras of Tang and Yu. I beg that after attending to governance, the practice of summoning officials for personal audiences be broadened: it would do well to follow the example of Han Qi 韓琦, who presented memorials and answered queries every day, striving to exhaust his loyal counsels in order to benefit practical administration; or that of Wei Xiang 魏相, who in the imperial presence unfailingly cited historical precedents point by point in order to remedy administrative shortcomings. How much more so when preceding reigns already offer proven results! Thus, when wishing to reckon appropriate measures for military farming colonies and the salt monopoly, Linhuai 臨淮 [Li Dongyang 李東陽 or Xie Qian 謝遷? — rather Ma Wensheng 馬文升 of Junyang, Liu Jian 劉健 of Luoyang, etc.: here referring to Grand Secretaries and ministers by their native places] and Luoyang 洛陽 [Liu Jian 劉健] were able to exhaust their deliberations; when wishing to settle calculations regarding frontier defense and the condition of the northern caitiffs, Junyang 均陽 [Ma Wensheng 馬文升] and Huarong 華容 [Liu Daxia 劉大夏] were able to decide upon strategies. Could we not also emulate [Note: 做 stands for 倣] the spirit of those precedents and put them into practice?

Nowadays, the lecturing and reading officials are fully staffed; they advance in turn, unroll the scrolls, and set forth their expositions—this is not without orderly method. Yet the texts have fixed limits and the lectures have set schedules, so that what the moral nature comprehends and what the physical temperament achieves have, one suspects, not yet been fully broadened and developed; this still falls short of what Master Cheng 程子 called nurturing and edifying influence. I beg that beyond the formal lectures, an avenue for admonition and remonstrance be opened: such as Master Fan's 范氏 [Fan Zuyu 范祖禹] discourse on good and evil, …

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
其本在君心所養可也如朱子誠敬之勉
其要在聖心克正可也况
先朝有已行之驗乎
太祖謂侍臣旦夕在左右凡政治得失生民利
病當知無不言弘治中於
經筵講罷
召閣臣詣
文華共閱章奏亦可循其事而舉之歟雖然
有本焉於穆不已天之所以爲天也純一
===
不已聖人之所以爲心也虞庭精一而辨
於危微孔門誠正而歸之慎獨言幾也故
幾之不審則一日萬幾毫釐千里雖講臣
日集於前經史日接於目何所用之哉必
自
深宮燕閒之暇以及
大庭廣衆之中由食息起居之微以至
昭祀臨涖之大持之以
純天之心則發爲
punctuated: 其本在君心所養，可也；如朱子誠敬之勉，其要在聖心克正，可也。况先朝有已行之驗乎？太祖謂侍臣旦夕在左右，凡政治得失、生民利病，當知無不言；弘治中，於經筵講罷，召閣臣詣文華共閱章奏，亦可循其事而舉之歟？雖然，有本焉。於穆不已，天之所以爲天也；純一不已，聖人之所以爲心也。虞庭精一而辨於危微，孔門誠正而歸之慎獨，言幾也。故幾之不審，則一日萬幾，毫釐千里，雖講臣日集於前，經史日接於目，何所用之哉？必自深宮燕閒之暇，以及大庭廣衆之中，由食息起居之微，以至昭祀臨涖之大，持之以純天之心，則發爲
translation_en:
…whose root lies in what is nourished in the sovereign's mind, would be fitting; or like Master Zhu's [Zhu Xi 朱熹] exhortation to sincerity and reverence, whose essence lies in the ability of the sage's mind to remain upright, would also be fitting. How much more so when earlier reigns already provide proven precedents? The Grand Progenitor (Taizu 太祖) told his attending officials that since they were at his side morning and evening, regarding all successes and failures in governance and the benefits and ills of the people, they ought to speak out on everything they knew. During the Hongzhi 弘治 era (1488–1505), after the Classics Colloquium (jingyan 經筵) lectures concluded, Grand Secretaries were summoned to the Hall of Literary Brilliance (Wenhua dian 文華殿) to review memorials together. Could we not also follow these precedents and put them into practice?

Even so, there is a fundamental root to this. Profound, solemn, and unceasing—this is whereby Heaven is Heaven; pure, unified, and unceasing—this is whereby the sage makes his mind. In the court of Yu [Shun 舜], they spoke of refinement and unity to distinguish between the precarious and the subtle; in the school of Confucius, they spoke of making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind, tracing it back to being watchful over oneself when alone. Both were speaking of incipient tendencies (ji 幾). Therefore, if incipient tendencies are not carefully examined, then amid the ten thousand affairs of a single day, an error of a hair's breadth leads to a divergence of a thousand miles. Even if lecturing officials gather daily before the throne and the Classics and Histories daily meet the eye, of what use would they be? Only when, from moments of leisure in the deep palace to appearances before the great court and broad assembly, and from the subtle details of eating, resting, and daily routine to the great occasions of solemn sacrifices and imperial audiences, one upholds all with a mind as pure as Heaven, will it manifest as…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
聖學之日新措爲
聖業之富有者裕如矣此固
祖宗心學而其旨歸則
敬一也是在
聖明加之意焉耳草茅芹曝之
獻不識可爲
聖學之一助否
第二問
張問達
同考試官教諭何　批〔辨析吾儒名實卓有確論至所云正心端習尤爲今時切務自待可知〕
===
同考試官教諭賓　批〔歷舉今昔儒紳而折衷之乃權度不毫髮爽蓋尚論有素者也〕
考試官學正宋　批〔識趣端純於所評驗之〕
考試官教授劉　批〔品騭精當〕
儒所以明道也窮經而或詭于道則僞得
以亂眞亦所以體道也修言而不適于用
則名得以眩實夫道者學之所視以爲的
punctuated:
聖學之日新，措爲聖業之富有者裕如矣。此固祖宗心學，而其旨歸則敬一也，是在聖明加之意焉耳。草茅芹曝之獻，不識可爲聖學之一助否？

第二問
張問達
同考試官教諭何　批〔辨析吾儒名實，卓有確論。至所云正心端習，尤爲今時切務，自待可知。〕
同考試官教諭賓　批〔歷舉今昔儒紳而折衷之，乃權度不毫髮爽，蓋尚論有素者也。〕
考試官學正宋　批〔識趣端純，於所評驗之。〕
考試官教授劉　批〔品騭精當。〕

儒所以明道也，窮經而或詭于道，則僞得以亂眞；亦所以體道也，修言而不適于用，則名得以眩實。夫道者，學之所視以爲的
translation_en:
… the daily renewal of Your Sagely Learning and applied in practice as the abundant wealth of Your Sagely Enterprise with effortless ease. This is indeed the learning of the mind-and-heart of our Imperial Ancestors, and its ultimate purport is Reverence and Oneness. It rests only with Your Sagely Brilliance to give heed to it. I do not know whether this humble offering from one in the thatched huts may serve as a small aid to Your Sagely Learning or not?

Second Policy Question
Zhang Wenda 張問達
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies He 何 comments: [In distinguishing between name and reality among us Confucians, he presents outstanding and definitive arguments. As for what he says about rectifying the mind and making one's habits upright, that is an especially urgent task for the present day; one can see from this what he expects of himself.]
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Bin 賓 comments: [He enumerates one by one the Confucian scholars and gentry of past and present and weighs them in the balance; his standards and measures do not err by a hair's breadth, showing that he is someone long practiced in evaluating historical figures.]
Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Song 宋 comments: [His insight and orientation are upright and pure, as can be verified by his evaluations.]
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Liu 劉 comments: [His critical appraisals are precise and fitting.]

A Confucian scholar exists in order to illuminate the Way; yet if one exhausts the Classics while perhaps deviating from the Way, then falsehood is able to confound the true. A Confucian scholar also exists in order to embody the Way; yet if one cultivates fine words that are not suited to practical application, then mere reputation is able to dazzle and obscure reality. Now the Way is that which learning looks toward as its target …

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
也譬之射者之鵠焉弓矢是習而不期于
彀雖力能貫革弗謂之善射矣學之易惑
于多岐也譬之越人之適國焉冥行疾趨
而不知所向卽涉歷日多其去國益遠矣
然則所貴乎儒者亦豈徒以誇多而衒博
也哉固將責以繼往開來之實而使道統
于我乎攸屬也故謏聞寡識不足以達觀
蕩檢踰節不可以盡性表飾浮華非所以
適用支離汗漫有難以翼經學儒者要諸
===
此而從違之極定矣論儒者準諸此而是
非之辨明矣苟徒徇其名與迹而稱於天
下曰儒則于聖學治化又何裨益也哉嘗
謂三五之世光岳氣完賢聖迭作所以樹
風聲流顯號者莫非儒也而不以儒名非
無儒也夫人而有之也三代以還淳朴日
散名世間出于是始以儒名于天下然則
儒之有名其起于實之衰乎粤自周官太
宰以九兩繫萬民而儒因以著今攷其目
punctuated:
也。譬之射者之鵠焉，弓矢是習而不期于彀，雖力能貫革，弗謂之善射矣；學之易惑于多岐也，譬之越人之適國焉，冥行疾趨而不知所向，卽涉歷日多，其去國益遠矣。然則所貴乎儒者，亦豈徒以誇多而衒博也哉？固將責以繼往開來之實，而使道統于我乎攸屬也。故謏聞寡識，不足以達觀；蕩檢踰節，不可以盡性；表飾浮華，非所以適用；支離汗漫，有難以翼經。學儒者要諸此，而從違之極定矣；論儒者準諸此，而是非之辨明矣。苟徒徇其名與迹而稱於天下曰「儒」，則于聖學治化又何裨益也哉？
嘗謂三五之世，光岳氣完，賢聖迭作，所以樹風聲、流顯號者，莫非儒也，而不以儒名。非無儒也，夫人而有之也。三代以還，淳朴日散，名世間出，于是始以儒名于天下。然則儒之有名，其起于實之衰乎？粤自《周官》太宰以九兩繫萬民，而儒因以著。今攷其目，
translation_en:
… [that which learning takes as its target]. It is like the bull's-eye for an archer: if one practices with bow and arrow without aiming to draw to the full and hit the mark, even if one has the strength to pierce the leather target, one cannot be called a good archer. And the ease with which learning is led astray by diverging paths is like a person from Yue traveling to a state: if he walks blindly and hurries along without knowing his direction, the more days he spends traveling, the farther he gets from that state. If so, how could that which is valued in a Confucian scholar (ru) merely be boasting of quantity and showing off breadth of knowledge? Assuredly, we must hold him responsible for the substance of carrying on the past heritage and opening up the future, so that the transmission of the Way (daotong) properly rests with us. Therefore, shallow hearing and scant knowledge are insufficient for a comprehensive view; flouting restraint and overstepping bounds cannot fully realize one's nature; outward adornment and flashy superficiality are not the means to meet practical use; and fragmented, rambling discourse can hardly give wings to the Classics. If those who study to be Confucians sum it up in these terms, the standard of what to follow and what to reject is settled; if those who evaluate Confucians take these as their measure, the distinction between right and wrong becomes clear. If one merely pursues the name and outward traces and is acclaimed throughout the empire as a "Confucian," what benefit does that bring to sage learning and transformative governance?

It has been said that in the age of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, the vital energy of the heavens and sacred mountains was whole, and worthies and sages arose in succession. Those who established moral influence and left behind illustrious names were all Confucians, yet they were not named "Confucians." It was not that there were no Confucians; rather, every person possessed those qualities. From the Three Dynasties onward, simplicity and unadorned honesty dissipated day by day, and renowned figures of their age appeared only at intervals; thereupon they first came to be named "Confucians" in the world. Thus, did the existence of the name "Confucian" arise from the decline of its reality? Ever since the Grand宰 (Taizai, Grand Counselor) in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) bound the myriad people together with the "nine ties" (jiuliang), the term "Confucian" (ru) thereby became prominent. Now, if we examine its items…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
曰牧曰長曰師曰儒曰宗曰主曰吏曰友
曰藪夫儒而與主吏牧長並稱固以其貫
乎九兩之中爲聯屬人心之本也儒之道
不其重哉班固作藝文志有九家之論而
儒居其一今攷其說曰儒家曰道家曰陰
陽家曰法家曰名家曰墨家曰縱横家曰
雜家曰小說家夫儒而與陰陽名墨㮣列
殆不知儒道精粹渾全非一家所能限也
固之言不其繆哉孔子之述儒行嘗于魯
===
君而發其義矣蓋曰其自立也固其備豫
也素不隕獲于貧賤不充詘于富貴斯儒
者功用之全也夫周道日衰學術𥘉裂孔
子不得已而鳴其道于齊魯之間殆有憂
世之思乎楊子之述儒效嘗于法言而指
其大矣其曰周公一用而四海皇皇奠枕
于京孔子一用而齊人章章歸其侵疆信
哉功效不可誣也夫二聖德業固萬世君
師之極也雄乃妄加評隲而目之爲儒焉
punctuated: 曰牧、曰長、曰師、曰儒、曰宗、曰主、曰吏、曰友、曰藪。夫儒而與主、吏、牧、長並稱，固以其貫乎九兩之中，爲聯屬人心之本也。儒之道，不其重哉！班固作《藝文志》，有九家之論，而儒居其一。今攷其說：曰儒家、曰道家、曰陰陽家、曰法家、曰名家、曰墨家、曰縱横家、曰雜家、曰小說家。夫儒而與陰陽、名、墨㮣列，殆不知儒道精粹渾全，非一家所能限也。固之言，不其繆哉！孔子之述《儒行》，嘗于魯君而發其義矣。蓋曰：其自立也固，其備豫也素，不隕獲于貧賤，不充詘于富貴。斯儒者功用之全也。夫周道日衰，學術𥘉裂，孔子不得已而鳴其道于齊、魯之間，殆有憂世之思乎！楊子之述儒效，嘗于《法言》而指其大矣。其曰：周公一用，而四海皇皇，奠枕于京；孔子一用，而齊人章章，歸其侵疆。信哉，功效不可誣也！夫二聖德業，固萬世君師之極也，雄乃妄加評隲，而目之爲儒焉，
translation_en: … namely, pastors, elders, teachers, Confucian scholars (ru), clan heads, patrons, officials, friends, and marsh-stewards. Now, that the Confucian scholar is named alongside patrons, officials, pastors, and elders is surely because his role runs through all nine bonds as the very foundation for binding together the hearts of the people. How weighty indeed is the Way of the Confucian scholar! When Ban Gu 班固 composed the "Treatise on Literature" (Yiwen zhi 藝文志), he set forth a discussion of the Nine Schools, among which the Confucians occupied one place. Examining his account today, they are: the Confucian school, the Daoist school, the Yin-Yang school, the Legalist school, the School of Names, the Mohist school, the School of Alliances, the Syncretist school, and the School of Minor Talks. Yet to rank the Confucians indiscriminately alongside the Yin-Yang, Names, and Mohist schools is surely to fail to understand that the Confucian Way is pure, quintessential, and wholly complete—not something that can be confined to a single school. How erroneous indeed are Ban Gu's words! When Confucius expounded the "Conduct of the Scholar" (Ruxing 儒行), he once set forth its meaning before the ruler of Lu. In substance, he said that the scholar stands firm in his self-reliance and is long-prepared in his readiness; he does not lose his bearings in poverty and low station, nor does he grow puffed up orcompromised in wealth and honor. This is the completeness of the Confucian scholar's function and efficacy. As the Way of Zhou declined day by day and scholarly learning first began to splinter, Confucius had no choice but to proclaim his Way between Qi and Lu—surely out of deep concern for the world! When Master Yang [Yang Xiong 揚雄] expounded the efficacy of the Confucian, he once pointed out its greatness in his Model Sayings (Fayan 法言). He said: "Once the Duke of Zhou was employed, all within the four seas became illustrious, and the capital rested securely on its pillow; once Confucius was employed, the men of Qi were awed into clarity and returned the territories they had seized." Truly, such achievements and efficacy cannot be denied! Yet the virtue and accomplishments of these two sages are inherently the ultimate standard for rulers and teachers for ten thousand generations; for Yang Xiong to presumptuously pass judgment on them and merely label them as "Confucian scholars" (ru)…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
殆未窺聖人之閫奧者乎漢史立儒林傳
載丁寛而下諸人而潛心大業若董仲舒
者乃獨不與豈丁寛輩賢于仲舒耶蓋漢
儒以訓詁爲學者也待詔公車者或取罪
于圖讖學宗書旨者以贓敗于汝南他可
知也惟仲舒以正誼明道爲心以計功謀
利爲戒似不專于訓詁者史氏置而不錄
宜矣唐史立儒學傳載文遠而下諸人而
學本六經若韓愈者乃又見遺豈文遠輩
===
優于愈耶蓋唐儒以聲律爲學者也南郊
建議而諂事女后春宮侍讀而黨附叔文
他可知也惟愈則以起衰濟溺爲期以闢
邪崇正爲任似不事于聲律者史氏置而
不及宜矣至儒林傳之作于宋也紀聶崇
義邢昺諸人而濂洛關閩諸賢又有道學
傳以紀之焉惟時若呂伯恭得中原文獻
之傳陸子靜謹屋漏夢寐之際乃顧不得
與程朱並載焉豈非以金華之學傷于巧
punctuated: 殆未窺聖人之閫奧者乎？漢史立《儒林傳》，載丁寛而下諸人，而潛心大業若董仲舒者乃獨不與，豈丁寛輩賢于仲舒耶？蓋漢儒以訓詁爲學者也。待詔公車者，或取罪于圖讖；學宗書旨者，以贓敗于汝南；他可知也。惟仲舒以正誼明道爲心，以計功謀利爲戒，似不專于訓詁者，史氏置而不錄，宜矣。唐史立《儒學傳》，載文遠而下諸人，而學本六經若韓愈者乃又見遺，豈文遠輩優于愈耶？蓋唐儒以聲律爲學者也。南郊建議而諂事女后，春宮侍讀而黨附叔文，他可知也。惟愈則以起衰濟溺爲期，以闢邪崇正爲任，似不事于聲律者，史氏置而不及，宜矣。至《儒林傳》之作于宋也，紀聶崇義、邢昺諸人，而濂、洛、關、閩諸賢又有《道學傳》以紀之焉。惟時若呂伯恭得中原文獻之傳，陸子靜謹屋漏夢寐之際，乃顧不得與程、朱並載焉，豈非以金華之學傷于巧，
translation_en:
…was it perhaps because he had not glimpsed the inner recesses of the sages?

The Han histories established the "Biographies of Confucian Scholars" (Rulin zhuan 儒林傳), recording figures from Ding Kuan 丁寛 downward, yet someone who immersed his mind in the great enterprise like Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 was uniquely excluded. Were Ding Kuan and his ilk really worthier than Zhongshu? This is because the Confucian scholars of the Han took exegesis and glossing (xungu 訓詁) as their learning. One who awaited imperial edicts at the Official Carriages Office (Gongche 公車) incurred guilt through prognostic charts and apocrypha; one whose learning was revered as mastering the purport of the Book of Documents was ruined by bribery in Runan 汝南; the rest can be imagined from these. Only Zhongshu took rectifying righteousness and clarifying the Way as his mind, and took calculating merit and scheming for profit as his warning. Because he did not seem to specialize solely in exegesis, it was fitting that the historians set him aside and did not include him in that collective biography.

The Tang histories established the "Biographies of Confucian Learning" (Ruxue zhuan 儒學傳), recording figures from Lu Wenyuan 陸文遠 downward, yet someone whose learning was rooted in the Six Classics like Han Yu 韓愈 was again left out. Were Wenyuan and his ilk really superior to Yu? This is because the Confucian scholars of the Tang took tonal meter and prosody (shenglü 聲律) as their learning. One offered proposals on the southern suburban sacrifice while flattering and serving the female ruler; another served as Reader-in-waiting in the Heir Apparent's Palace (Chungong shidu 春宮侍讀) while forming a faction with Wang Shuwen 王叔文; the rest can be imagined from these. Only Yu aimed at reviving what had declined and rescuing the drowning, and took refuting heterodoxy and exalting orthodoxy as his duty. Because he did not seem to occupied himself with tonal meter, it was fitting that the historians set him aside and did not touch upon him there.

When the "Biographies of Confucian Scholars" came to be composed for the Song, it recorded figures such as Nie Chongyi 聶崇義 and Xing Bing 邢昺, while for the worthies of Lian 濂, Luo 洛, Guan 關, and Min 閩 there was in addition the "Biographies of the Learning of the Way" (Daoxue zhuan 道學傳) to record them. Yet at that time, figures like Lü Bogong 呂伯恭 (Lü Zuqian 呂祖謙), who obtained the transmission of the textual and historical heritage of the Central Plains, and Lu Zijing 陸子靜 (Lu Jiuyuan 陸九淵), who maintained vigilance even in the privacy of his chamber and in his dreams, nonetheless could not be recorded alongside the Cheng 程 brothers and Zhu Xi 朱熹. Was this not because the learning of Jinhua 金華 was marred by over-cleverness,…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
金溪之學流于禪而難與諸賢爲伍歟此
固史氏別傳之微意也詎謂道與儒判然
爲二哉要之諸儒之論辨非不欲以闡道
也顧識見有通蔽焉則窮經而失諸汗漫
者多矣諸儒之行事非不欲以體道也顧
造詣有純駁焉則空言而無當于用者多
矣惟聖人德性渾全義理融洽由是而上
繼絕學下開隆平夫是謂儒者之德由是
而尊主寧邦極民扶世夫是謂儒者之功
===
由是而統括六籍潤色百家夫是謂儒者
之言周公達而在上其道行孔子窮而在
下其道明要皆兼此三者固萬世儒道之
的也下是而濂洛關閩遠宗周孔之傳者
乎董子韓愈儒之傑出而未醇者乎丁寬
文遠邢昺崇義諸家儒之宮牆外望者乎
或擇焉不精或語焉不詳所謂似儒而非
儒者此也論儒者欲辨其眞似之幾惟于
其心焉察之而已使心術醇矣無論事業
punctuated: 金溪之學流于禪，而難與諸賢爲伍歟？此固史氏別傳之微意也，詎謂道與儒判然爲二哉？要之，諸儒之論辨，非不欲以闡道也，顧識見有通蔽焉，則窮經而失諸汗漫者多矣；諸儒之行事，非不欲以體道也，顧造詣有純駁焉，則空言而無當于用者多矣。惟聖人德性渾全，義理融洽，由是而上繼絕學、下開隆平，夫是謂儒者之德；由是而尊主寧邦、極民扶世，夫是謂儒者之功；由是而統括六籍、潤色百家，夫是謂儒者之言。周公達而在上，其道行；孔子窮而在下，其道明。要皆兼此三者，固萬世儒道之的也。下是，而濂、洛、關、閩，遠宗周、孔之傳者乎？董子、韓愈，儒之傑出而未醇者乎？丁寬、文遠、邢昺、崇義諸家，儒之宮牆外望者乎？或擇焉不精，或語焉不詳，所謂似儒而非儒者，此也。論儒者欲辨其眞似之幾，惟于其心焉察之而已。使心術醇矣，無論事業、
translation_en: … the learning of Jinxi (Lu Jiuyuan 陸九淵) drifted into Chan Buddhism, making it difficult to rank them alongside those worthies? This was indeed the subtle intent of the historians in placing them in separate biographies; how could it mean that the Way and Confucian scholarship are severed into two distinct things? In sum, in their discussions and debates, the various scholars did not lack the desire to elucidate the Way; yet because their insight was either penetrating or obstructed, many exhausted the Classics only to lose themselves in diffuserambling. In their conduct and actions, the various scholars did not lack the desire to embody the Way; yet because their attainment was either pure or mixed, many indulged in empty words that were unsuitable for practical application. Only the sages possess a moral nature that is浑全 (completely whole) and a grasp of principle that is thoroughly harmonious. From this, above they carry on the lost learning of the past, and below they open up an era of great peace—this is what is called the virtue of a Confucian. From this, they honor the ruler and bring tranquility to the state, rescue the people and uphold the world—this is what is called the achievement of a Confucian. From this, they encompass the Six Classics and refine the Hundred Schools—this is what is called the words of a Confucian. The Duke of Zhou (Zhougong 周公) achieved high station above, and his Way was put into practice; Confucius (Kongzi 孔子) was reduced to obscurity below, and his Way was made luminous. In essence, both combined these three things, and they are assuredly the standard of the Confucian Way for ten thousand generations. Below them, were not the masters of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min (Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤, the Cheng brothers 程顥/程頤, Zhang Zai 張載, and Zhu Xi 朱熹) those who traced their lineage from afar back to the transmission of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius? Were not Master Dong (Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒) and Han Yu 韓愈 outstanding among Confucians, yet not entirely pure? Were not the various schools of Ding Kuan 丁寬, Wen Yuan (Lu Wenyuan 陸文遠), Xing Bing 邢昺, and Chongyi (Nie Chongyi 聶崇義) merely gazing from outside the palace walls of Confucianism? Some selected without precision; others spoke without thoroughness—these are what are called those who resemble Confucians but are not true Confucians. When evaluating Confucians, if one wishes to discern the subtle boundary between the true and the specious, one need only examine their minds. If the orientation of their minds is pure, then not only will their enterprises and…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
文章皆卓犖不羣也即二者不可得兼而
根本已無媿于聖學不害其爲儒也苟飾
而僞矣無論功業文詞皆畢也即功著一
匡詞稚百代亦何取于儒哉故君子之明
道也求以復吾心也攬今徹古遐睇博觀
非徒以侚象矣君子之體道也求以達吾
心也砥行植節策勛澤民非徒以樹聲矣
本之六經以求其端率之彝倫以踐其實
約之幽獨以豫其本擴之天下家國以大
===
其施由董韓以會濂洛之傳由濂洛以遡
周孔之緒則名實相符而道統之傳屬之
我矣豈漢唐諸儒所能及哉我
國家闡揚經術褒崇儒教一時任道之臣後
先相望如薛瑄以復性爲學有稱其踐履
篤實者矣胡居仁以主敬爲學有稱其不
媿屋漏者矣其餘起于徵召則有若吳與
弼陳獻章列于科目則有若羅倫章懋出
處去就雖各不同其立言制行要皆不詭
punctuated:
文章皆卓犖不羣也，即二者不可得兼，而根本已無媿于聖學，不害其爲儒也；苟飾而僞矣，無論功業文詞皆畢也，即功著一匡，詞稚百代，亦何取于儒哉！故君子之明道也，求以復吾心也，攬今徹古，遐睇博觀，非徒以侚象矣；君子之體道也，求以達吾心也，砥行植節，策勛澤民，非徒以樹聲矣。本之六經以求其端，率之彝倫以踐其實，約之幽獨以豫其本，擴之天下家國以大其施，由董、韓以會濂、洛之傳，由濂、洛以遡周、孔之緒，則名實相符，而道統之傳屬之我矣，豈漢、唐諸儒所能及哉！

我國家闡揚經術，褒崇儒教，一時任道之臣後先相望。如薛瑄以復性爲學，有稱其踐履篤實者矣；胡居仁以主敬爲學，有稱其不媿屋漏者矣。其餘起于徵召，則有若吳與弼、陳獻章；列于科目，則有若羅倫、章懋。出處去就雖各不同，其立言制行，要皆不詭
translation_en:
…and literary writings are both outstanding and extraordinary; even if the two cannot be attained together, so long as the foundation is nothing to be ashamed of before the learning of the sages, it does not keep him from being a Confucian. If it is mere affectation and falsehood, then setting aside that his achievements and literary words are altogether finished [?], even if his merit were as illustrious as uniting and rectifying the realm, and his words were a standard [?] for a hundred generations, what would there be in him to value as a Confucian! Therefore, when the gentleman clarifies the Way, he seeks thereby to restore his own mind; surveying the present and penetrating the past, gazing far and observing broadly, he does not merely pursue outward appearances. When the gentleman embodies the Way, he seeks thereby to extend his own mind;whetting his conduct and planting firm his integrity, inscribing merits and benefiting the people, he does not merely seek to establish a reputation. Grounding it in the Six Classics to seek its beginnings, following it through the constant human relationships to practice its reality, restraining it in solitary unseen moments to prepare its root, and expanding it to the empire, the state, and the family to enlarge its application—proceeding from Dong Zhongshu and Han Yu to meet the transmission of the Lian and Luo masters, and from the Lian and Luo masters to trace back the lineage of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius—then name and reality will correspond, and the transmission of the orthodox Way will belong to us. How could the various Confucians of the Han and Tang dynasties ever match this!

Our dynasty elucidates and promotes classical scholarship and honors and exalts Confucian teachings, so that in this era ministers who take the Way as their responsibility have appeared one after another in succession. For instance, Xue Xuan 薛瑄 took restoring nature as his learning, and there were those who praised his practical conduct as earnest and solid; Hu Juren 胡居仁 took holding fast to reverence as his learning, and there were those who praised him as having nothing to be ashamed of even in the darkest corner of a room. As for the rest, among those who rose through special summons, there were men such as Wu Yubi 吳與弼 and Chen Xianzhang 陳獻章; among those who entered the ranks through the examination system, there were men such as Luo Lun 羅倫 and Zhang Mao 章懋. Although their choices in taking office or retiring, leaving or staying, were each different, in establishing their words and regulating their conduct, in essence they all did not deviate…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
于聖人而以豪傑自期待者乎
聖天子崇教右文飾經表俗海内之士喁喁向
風固知碩儒雲集足以闡聖眞而揚王化
矣然習俗相沿名實易眩則似之亂眞者
得無有如執事所憂者乎故崇論閎議浮
游無當暴能市譽弗本悃誠而託之曰弘
博拘方守隘伐異黨同勦襲詞章附會穿
鑿而託之曰窮理文姦飾貌匿智隱端閃
爍狡獪不可方物而託之曰藏用惡衣朴
===
躬程趨朱履小廉曲謹見色豆羹而託之
曰喻義援引禪寂溺志玄虛繆大言以惑
人喜高論以駭俗而託之曰超悟依阿澳
忍希寵邀榮儇佻周章巧于趨避而託之
曰通變用罔冥行喜功銳進不量可否以
國事爲嘗而託之曰勇敢有一于此固聖
世之所必棄也卽漢唐諸子且駕出其上
矣又安能與先賢比隆也哉雖然葉公好
龍斯眞龍入室燕昭好馬斯駿骨來庭儒
punctuated: 于聖人，而以豪傑自期待者乎？聖天子崇教右文，飾經表俗，海内之士喁喁向風，固知碩儒雲集，足以闡聖眞而揚王化矣。然習俗相沿，名實易眩，則似之亂眞者，得無有如執事所憂者乎？故崇論閎議，浮游無當，暴能市譽，弗本悃誠，而託之曰弘博；拘方守隘，伐異黨同，勦襲詞章，附會穿鑿，而託之曰窮理；文姦飾貌，匿智隱端，閃爍狡獪，不可方物，而託之曰藏用；惡衣朴躬，程趨朱履，小廉曲謹，見色豆羹，而託之曰喻義；援引禪寂，溺志玄虛，繆大言以惑人，喜高論以駭俗，而託之曰超悟；依阿澳忍，希寵邀榮，儇佻周章，巧于趨避，而託之曰通變；用罔冥行，喜功銳進，不量可否，以國事爲嘗，而託之曰勇敢。有一于此，固聖世之所必棄也，卽漢唐諸子且駕出其上矣，又安能與先賢比隆也哉！雖然，葉公好龍，斯眞龍入室；燕昭好馬，斯駿骨來庭。儒…
translation_en:
…from the sages, and who expected of themselves to be outstanding heroes?

Today our sacred Son of Heaven reveres education and esteems civil culture, adorning the Classics and setting standards for customs. Scholars within the seas crane their necks in admiration of his influence; we certainly know that great Confucians are gathering like clouds, sufficient to elucidate the truth of the sages and spread the royal transformation. Yet as customs are passed down, name and reality are easily confused; could it not be that there are specious look-alikes confounding the genuine, just as Your Excellency worries?

Thus, some indulge in lofty discourses and grand arguments that drift without foundation, showing off their abilities and peddling their reputations without a basis in sincere devotion—yet they pretextually call this "broad erudition." Some cling to rigid formulas and narrow views, attacking those who differ while siding with their own faction, plagiarizing literary compositions and making forced, far-fetched interpretations—yet they pretextually call this "exhausting principle." Some gloss over wickedness and put on a false appearance, concealing their cunning and hiding their motives, evasive and crafty beyond description—yet they pretextually call this "hiding one's utility." Some wear coarse clothes and affect personal simplicity, mimicking the measured pace of the Cheng brothers or the vermilion shoes of Zhu Xi, practicing petty integrity and fastidious caution while betraying their true feelings over a mere bowl of soup—yet they pretextually call this "understanding righteousness." Some cite Chan Buddhist quietism and drown their minds in dark emptiness, spinning grandiose falsehoods to delude people and delighting in lofty talk to shock the world—yet they pretextually call this "transcendent enlightenment." Some are compliant, obsequious, and accommodating, currying favor and seeking glory, frivolous and opportunistic, skillful at pursuing advantage and avoiding harm—yet they pretextually call this "adapting to change." Some act recklessly and walk in the dark, eager for achievements and rushing ahead without weighing what is permissible, treating affairs of state as mere experiments—yet they pretextually call this "courage."

Anyone possessing even one of these faults will certainly be rejected by a sacred age. Even the various masters of the Han and Tang dynasties would surpass them—how then could they possibly compare in eminence with the former worthies! Even so, when Lord She was fond of dragons, a true dragon entered his chamber; when King Zhao of Yan was fond of horses, the bones of a fine steed were brought to his court. The Confucian…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
道之轉移亦在上者示之趨耳明經術以
正人心簡師儒以端士習則固司教者責
也愚生于今日有厚望焉
第三問
趙爾守
同考試官教諭唐　批〔法有以變爲因者化而裁之視其時與人爾此策推古酌今動中肯綮是嘗究心於經世之略者〕
同考試官教諭竇　批〔議法達時變而不狃拘攣不膠同異指切通患一疏窒源即賈董復興無以易此〕
===
考試官學正宋　批〔究觀敏對贍博不迂〕
考試官教授劉　批〔通方策士之文可録〕
善守法者察其幾而愼持之斯不至于滋
弊善捄弊者審其勢而愼修之斯不至于
擾民故治道勿安于無爲也亦勿喜于有
爲也安于無爲則逡巡畏縮而事幾日見
其舛繆喜于有爲則督責迫促而人情益
駭于見聞其以弊天下者均也夫自昔帝
王之興更事多而慮患密其所創法必權
punctuated:
道之轉移，亦在上者示之趨耳。明經術以正人心，簡師儒以端士習，則固司教者責也。愚生于今日有厚望焉。

第三問
趙爾守
同考試官教諭唐批：〔法有以變爲因者，化而裁之，視其時與人爾。此策推古酌今，動中肯綮，是嘗究心於經世之略者。〕
同考試官教諭竇批：〔議法達時變，而不狃拘攣，不膠同異，指切通患，一疏窒源，即賈、董復興，無以易此。〕
考試官學正宋批：〔究觀敏對，贍博不迂。〕
考試官教授劉批：〔通方策士之文，可録。〕

善守法者，察其幾而愼持之，斯不至于滋弊；善捄弊者，審其勢而愼修之，斯不至于擾民。故治道勿安于無爲也，亦勿喜于有爲也。安于無爲，則逡巡畏縮，而事幾日見其舛繆；喜于有爲，則督責迫促，而人情益駭于見聞：其以弊天下者均也。夫自昔帝王之興，更事多而慮患密，其所創法，必權
translation_en:
… transformation of the Confucian Way likewise depends simply on the direction shown by those above. Clarifying the art of the Classics to rectify human hearts, and selecting Confucian teachers to straighten the habits of scholars—these are assuredly the responsibilities of those in charge of education. For this, your foolish student has high hopes today.

Third Policy Question
Zhao Ershou 趙爾守
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Tang 唐 comments: [In laws, there are cases where change serves as continuity; transforming and tailoring them depends only on the times and the people. This policy essay infers from antiquity and weighs the present, hitting the crucial points at every turn; he is one who has applied his mind to the strategies of statecraft.]
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Dou 竇 comments: [In discussing laws, he comprehends the changes of the times without being bound by narrow constraints or bogged down in comparisons of sameness and difference. He points incisively to common ills and clears away obstructed sources at a stroke; even if Jia Yi 賈誼 and Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 were to rise again, they could not improve upon this.]
Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Song 宋 comments: [Looking thoroughly into this perceptive reply, it is rich, broad, and not pedantic.]
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Liu 劉 comments: [The essay of a well-rounded strategist; worthy of being recorded.]

Those who are good at upholding the laws examine their subtle incipient tendencies and maintain them with caution, so that they do not reach the point of breeding abuses; those who are good at remedying abuses assess their circumstances and revise them with caution, so that they do not reach the point of disturbing the people. Therefore, the way of governance must neither rest content in non-action, nor delight in aggressive action. If one rests content in non-action, one hesitates and shrinks back, and the critical junctures of affairs daily show their perversity and error; if one delights in aggressive action, one supervises and presses urgently, and human feelings are increasingly alarmed by what they see and hear. In bringing harm to the empire, the two are equal. Now, when emperors and kings rose to power in the past, they experienced many affairs and planned against calamities with thoroughness; the laws they established necessariamente weighed…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
其利害得失之故而詳為之計亦何有于
弊哉惟其行之久而玩愒生其勢必有廢
墜而不舉者于此而隨時消息去其太甚
斯亦足以順治而安民矣今夫琴瑟不調
必解而更張之以鼓之成聲可使人聽而
悅也若鼛缶箏䶵雜然並奏則聞之者亙
惑矣車轍或敝必飭而新之以軌之利用
可使人御而前也若輪轅徒飾製不中規
則致遠恐泥矣人君之圖治期以改弦而
===
易轍幾固不可以不慎也三代盛時其沿
革損益曷嘗不因時以通變哉而其經制
立國之本則固相授守一道矣後世若漢
高祖懲嬴秦之虐以寛仁為治三章約法
十五稅民誠繼體者所宜率循也乃孝武
好大喜功任用新進張趙入而法令滋多
桑孔入而横征無藝卒致海內虛耗漢家
之元氣索然矣迨至昭宣勵精圖治綜核
名實罷榷酤減租賦一時吏稱民安而文
punctuated:
其利害得失之故，而詳為之計，亦何有于弊哉？惟其行之久而玩愒生，其勢必有廢墜而不舉者。于此而隨時消息，去其太甚，斯亦足以順治而安民矣。今夫琴瑟不調，必解而更張之，以鼓之成聲，可使人聽而悅也；若鼛缶箏䶵雜然並奏，則聞之者亙惑矣。車轍或敝，必飭而新之，以軌之利用，可使人御而前也；若輪轅徒飾，製不中規，則致遠恐泥矣。人君之圖治，期以改弦而易轍，幾固不可以不慎也。
三代盛時，其沿革損益，曷嘗不因時以通變哉？而其經制立國之本，則固相授守一道矣。後世若漢高祖懲嬴秦之虐，以寛仁為治，三章約法，十五稅民，誠繼體者所宜率循也。乃孝武好大喜功，任用新進，張、趙入而法令滋多，桑、孔入而横征無藝，卒致海內虛耗，漢家之元氣索然矣。迨至昭、宣，勵精圖治，綜核名實，罷榷酤，減租賦，一時吏稱民安，而文、
translation_en:
… the causes of their advantages and disadvantages, successes and failures, and made detailed plans for them—how could there have been any abuses in them? Only when they have been practiced for a long time does laxity arise, and by the nature of things there will inevitably be parts that fall into disrepair and are no longer upheld. At such a point, adjusting them in accordance with the times and removing what is excessive is quite sufficient to achieve orderly governance and give peace to the people. Now, when the qin and se zithers are out of tune, one must unstring and restring them; because playing them produces harmonious music, it can make those who listen rejoice. If, however, large drums, earthen jars, zithers, and flutes are played together in a jumble, those who hear them will be utterly bewildered [?]. When carriage ruts or wheels become worn out, one must repair and renew them; because the axle-gauge is suited to practical use, it enables people to drive forward. If, however, the wheels and shafts are merely decorated while their construction does not conform to the compass, then in attempting to reach a distant place one fears getting bogged down. When a ruler plans for governance and seeks to restring the zither and change the ruts, he truly cannot fail to be cautious about the subtleincipient tendencies.

In the flourishing eras of the Three Dynasties, in their continuities and changes, additions and reductions, when did they ever fail to adapt to the times? Yet as for the fundamental institutions by which they established the state, they assuredly passed them down and held fast to a single Way. In later ages, for example, Emperor Gaozu of Han (漢高祖), taking warning from the tyranny of Qin (嬴秦), governed with寬lenience and benevolence, simplified the laws into three articles, and taxed the people at one-fifteenth—this was truly what his successors ought to have followed. Yet Emperor Xiaowu (孝武), fond of grandeur and eager for exploits, employed newly promoted men: when Zhang Tang (張湯) and Zhao Yu (趙禹) entered office, laws and ordinances multiplied; when Sang Hongyang (桑弘羊) and Kong Jin (孔僅) entered office, arbitrary exactions knew no bounds. In the end, this left the realm depleted and exhausted, and the vital energy of the House of Han was drained away. Coming down to Emperors Zhao (昭) and Xuan (宣), they roused their spirits to seek good governance, verified that names matched realities, abolished the state liquor monopoly, and reduced land taxes and levies. For a time, officials were competent and the people were at peace, and after Emperors Wen (文)…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
景之後于斯爲盛焉是昭宣之再變非紛
更也鑒武帝之弊以復高祖之舊焉耳唐
太宗乘剪亂之餘文武並用以府衛寓兵
法租庸調定均田誠繼體者所宜敬承也
乃玄德間宿衛漸逃版籍浸壞張說之議
行而府兵變爲彍騎楊炎之說行而租庸
變爲兩稅卒致天步艱危唐祚之不絕如
綫矣迨至宣宗明察沉斷用法無私戢禁
兵蠲歲賦以致政治不擾而大中之治比
===
跡于貞觀焉是宣宗之再變非紛更也鑒
玄德之弊以復太宗之舊焉耳宋祖承五
代之亂勸課以重農桑覆奏以卹刑獄其
立國一依于忠厚誠子孫所宜繩武焉者
也夫何神宗刻意求治任用非人青苗助
役之法日擾擾焉以更新起敝爲事而海
內已騷然矣幸承其後者有元祐焉安石
罷而新法盡除惠卿竄而老成復用于是
乎人心收屬而基業賴以不墜是元祐之
punctuated: 景之後，于斯爲盛焉。是昭、宣之再變，非紛更也，鑒武帝之弊以復高祖之舊焉耳。唐太宗乘剪亂之餘，文武並用，以府衛寓兵法，租庸調定均田，誠繼體者所宜敬承也。乃玄、德間，宿衛漸逃，版籍浸壞；張說之議行，而府兵變爲彍騎；楊炎之說行，而租庸變爲兩稅。卒致天步艱危，唐祚之不絕如綫矣。迨至宣宗，明察沉斷，用法無私，戢禁兵，蠲歲賦，以致政治不擾，而大中之治比跡于貞觀焉。是宣宗之再變，非紛更也，鑒玄、德之弊以復太宗之舊焉耳。宋祖承五代之亂，勸課以重農桑，覆奏以卹刑獄，其立國一依于忠厚，誠子孫所宜繩武焉者也。夫何神宗刻意求治，任用非人，青苗、助役之法日擾擾焉以更新起敝爲事，而海內已騷然矣。幸承其後者有元祐焉，安石罷而新法盡除，惠卿竄而老成復用，于是乎人心收屬，而基業賴以不墜。是元祐之
translation_en:
…[Emperors Wen and] Jing, this period was the most flourishing. Thus the second transformation under Emperors Zhao and Xuan was not reckless alteration; it was simply taking warning from the abuses of Emperor Wu in order to restore the old ways of Gaozu.

Tang Taizong, riding on the aftermath of quelling disorder, employed both civil and military means: he lodged military organization within the garrison militia (fuwei) system, and stabilized land equalization through the grain, labor, and cloth tax (zuyongdiao). This was truly what his successors ought to have reverently upheld. Yet during the reigns of Emperors Xuanzong and Dezong, the palace guards gradually deserted and the household registers slowly fell into ruin. When the proposals of Zhang Yue 張說 were put into practice, the garrison militia was changed into the Long-range Mounted Guards (kuoqi); when the theories of Yang Yan 楊炎 were put into practice, the grain and labor taxes were changed into the Twice-a-Year Tax (liangshui). In the end, this brought the dynasty's fortunes into perilous straits, and the Tang mandate hung as if by a single thread. By the time of Emperor Xuanzong, he was clear-sighted and resolutely decisive, applying the law without partiality; he restrained the Imperial Armies and remitted annual taxes, so that governance was unharassed and the good order of the Dazhong reign (847–860) rivaled the footsteps of the Zhenguan reign (627–649). Thus the second transformation under Xuanzong was not reckless alteration; it was simply taking warning from the abuses of Xuanzong and Dezong in order to restore the old ways of Taizong.

The Song founder succeeded to the turmoil of the Five Dynasties; he encouraged and supervised the people so as to emphasize agriculture and sericulture, and required review memorials so as to show compassion in criminal cases. His founding of the state relied wholly on loyal generosity—truly something his descendants ought to have followed in his footsteps. How was it that Emperor Shenzong, bent on seeking good governance, employed the wrong men? With the Green Sprouts (qingmiao) and Hired Service (zhuyi) laws, day after day there was bustling agitation in the business of renewing the system and remedying abuses, while all within the seas was already thrown into turmoil. Fortunately, succeeding him came the Yuanyou period (1086–1094): Wang Anshi 王安石 was dismissed and the New Policies were completely abolished; Lü Huiqing 呂惠卿 was banished and experienced statesmen were once again employed. Thereupon popular sentiment was gathered back in allegiance, and the dynastic foundation relied on this so as not to fall. Thus the [second transformation] of the Yuanyou period…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
冊變非紛更也鑒神宗之弊以復藝祖之
舊焉耳由是觀之其成法之當遵固彰彰
明矣然當時獻納諸臣乃言人人殊焉故
自其謂法之當變者在漢則賈誼董仲舒
等有定經制更教化之請在唐則李翺劉
蕡輩有興文德持兵柄之請在宋則余靖
宋綬輩有攬乾綱振積衰之請即諸臣之
所條議豈厭故喜新騁私智以惑主聽哉
蓋或因其先德之未備或鑒于釁蘖之將
===
萌故欲潤色脩明以恢大前王之業是之
謂變而不失其因者也自其謂法之不可
變者如條陳便宜以脩復漢家故事則有
若霍光魏相之于漢置衞屯田均節財賦
則有若李泌陸贄之于唐調停新法次第
舉行則有若司馬光呂公著之于宋即諸
臣之所建明豈因陋就簡狃小康以忽遠
圖哉蓋有見于繼體之紛更浸失創業之
遺意故欲修飭舊章以求復先世之法是
punctuated: 冊變，非紛更也，鑒神宗之弊以復藝祖之舊焉耳。由是觀之，其成法之當遵，固彰彰明矣。然當時獻納諸臣，乃言人人殊焉。故自其謂法之當變者：在漢則賈誼、董仲舒等有定經制、更教化之請；在唐則李翺、劉蕡輩有興文德、持兵柄之請；在宋則余靖、宋綬輩有攬乾綱、振積衰之請。即諸臣之所條議，豈厭故喜新、騁私智以惑主聽哉？蓋或因其先德之未備，或鑒于釁蘖之將萌，故欲潤色脩明，以恢大前王之業。是之謂變而不失其因者也。自其謂法之不可變者：如條陳便宜以脩復漢家故事，則有若霍光、魏相之于漢；置衞屯田、均節財賦，則有若李泌、陸贄之于唐；調停新法、次第舉行，則有若司馬光、呂公著之于宋。即諸臣之所建明，豈因陋就簡、狃小康以忽遠圖哉？蓋有見于繼體之紛更，浸失創業之遺意，故欲修飭舊章，以求復先世之法。是
translation_en:
… the changes [of the Yuanyou reign, 冊 a misprint for 政 or 改?] were not disorderly alterations; they merely took warning from the abuses under Emperor Shenzong in order to restore the old ways of the Accomplished Progenitor (Taizu). Viewed in this light, that established laws ought to be followed is indeed abundantly clear. Yet among the various officials who offered counsel in those times, each spoke differently from the next.

Thus, from the perspective of those who maintained that the laws ought to be changed: in the Han, men such as Jia Yi 賈誼 and Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 submitted requests to fix the regular institutions and reform moral transformation; in the Tang, men such as Li Ao 李翺 and Liu Fen 劉蕡 submitted requests to promote civil virtue and hold fast to military authority; and in the Song, men such as Yu Jing 余靖 and Song Shou 宋綬 submitted requests to grasp the sovereign authority and rouse the dynasty from accumulated decline. Looking at the itemized deliberations of these officials, how could they have been weary of the old and fond of the new, giving free rein to private cleverness in order to delude their ruler's hearing? Rather, whether because the foundational virtues of their predecessors were not yet complete, or because they foresaw that the seeds of crisis were about to sprout, they wished to embellish, repair, and clarify the system so as to enlarge the enterprise of the former kings. This is what is meant by changing without losing continuity.

And from the perspective of those who maintained that the laws must not be changed: in setting forth expedient measures point by point so as to restore the old precedents of the House of Han, there were men like Huo Guang 霍光 and Wei Xiang 魏相 in the Han; in establishing guard units and state farms, and equalizing and moderating fiscal revenues, there were men like Li Mi 李泌 and Lu Zhi 陸贄 in the Tang; and in adjusting and halting the New Policies, carrying out the restoration step by step, there were men like Sima Guang 司馬光 and Lü Gongzhu 呂公著 in the Song. Looking at the proposals set forth by these officials, how could they have been merely making do with the crude and simple, growing habituated to minor peace while neglecting far-reaching plans? Rather, seeing that the disorderly alterations of succeeding rulers were gradually losing the bequeathed intent of the dynastic founders, they wished to repair and put in order the old statutes so as to seek the restoration of the laws of former generations. This…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
之謂守而不失其正者也大抵法者所藉
以爲安民之具耳民苟安矣而曰吾何以
新天下之耳目不猶厭菽粟而求之珎羞
舍布帛而索之錦繡者乎法已敝矣而曰
吾且與天下相安于無事不猶懼烏毒之
殺人而幷棄夫良藥慮風波之覆溺而幷
擯夫舟楫者乎此二者皆法之所忌也而
吾且犯之又何以治天下故曰不可以不
愼也我
===
太祖神聖統天經緯盡制宏纖具備小大相維
列聖相承率循彝典又非若漢武宋神之紛更
非若漢唐宋之偏舉而不全也
中變也良法美意信當千萬年世守而勿
失者奈何熙洽旣久蠧弊潛滋勢固不能
聽其敝而莫爲之所矣以故畢智之士獻
計而陳謨竭忠之臣採議而集事是誠救
偏補敝之不容已者顧申令日勤實效未
獲文具徒飾弊孔旋生其視立法之初已
punctuated: 之謂守而不失其正者也。大抵法者，所藉以爲安民之具耳。民苟安矣，而曰：「吾何以新天下之耳目？」不猶厭菽粟而求之珎羞，舍布帛而索之錦繡者乎？法已敝矣，而曰：「吾且與天下相安于無事。」不猶懼烏毒之殺人而幷棄夫良藥，慮風波之覆溺而幷擯夫舟楫者乎？此二者，皆法之所忌也。而吾且犯之，又何以治天下？故曰：不可以不愼也。我太祖神聖統天，經緯盡制，宏纖具備，小大相維，非若漢、唐、宋之偏舉而不全也；列聖相承，率循彝典，又非若漢武、宋神之紛更中變也。良法美意，信當千萬年世守而勿失者。奈何熙洽旣久，蠧弊潛滋，勢固不能聽其敝而莫爲之所矣。以故畢智之士，獻計而陳謨；竭忠之臣，採議而集事。是誠救偏補敝之不容已者。顧申令日勤，實效未獲，文具徒飾，弊孔旋生，其視立法之初，已
translation_en:
… is what is called preserving the law without losing its rectitude. In general, laws are simply the instruments relied upon to bring peace to the people. If the people are already at peace, and yet one says, "How shall I refresh the eyes and ears of the empire?"—is this not like growing weary of beans and grain and seeking out rare delicacies, or casting aside plain cloth and silk to demand brocade and embroidery? Conversely, when the laws have already fallen into decay, and yet one says, "I shall just remain at peace in non-action along with the empire"—is this not like fearing that aconite poison kills people and thus discarding good medicine along with it, or worrying that wind and waves capsize and drown people and thus abandoning boats and oars altogether? Both of these are things that the law忌 shuns. If we nevertheless violate this principle, how then can we govern the empire? Therefore it is said: one cannot but be cautious.

Our Grand Progenitor (Taizu 太祖), divinely sage, governed under Heaven, establishing institutions in every warp and woof, complete in both the grand and the minute, with the small and the great mutually supporting one another—unlike the partial and incomplete measures of the Han, Tang, and Song. The successive Sacred Emperors inherited this legacy and followed the constant canons, again unlike the chaotic alterations and mid-course changes under Emperor Wu of Han (Han Wu 漢武) or Emperor Shenzong of Song (Song Shen 宋神). Such good laws and fine intentions ought truly to be guarded from generation to generation for ten thousand years without being lost. Yet why is it that after a long period of peace and harmony, corruptions and abuses secretly proliferate, so that circumstances simply do not allow us to let them decay without taking action? For this reason, scholars who exhaust their wisdom offer up plans and set forth counsels, and ministers whoPour out their loyalty gather deliberations and accomplish tasks. This is truly an unavoidable effort to remedy imbalances and mend abuses. However, although repeated orders are issued ever more diligently, actual results have not been achieved; outward forms are merely adorned on paper while loopholes for corruption immediately arise. Compared to when the laws were first established, they already…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
不能盡如其舊矣愚請得以誦言而無諱
可乎里甲有定役也憫其疾苦而易以官
支之法于民誠得矣乃或有陽爲奉法陰
便私圖使逐末者代其勞而應役者享其
逸豈因賦定役之意乎田稅有定額也慮
其低昂而議以清丈之法于事誠便矣乃
或有吏售其姦民滋其僞使富者益其膏
而貧者甚其困豈則壤成賦之意乎官制
有定秩也時值多故或因事以增設焉顧
===
事未收專責之效而民已受多牧之擾矣
不有如所謂廐長立而馬益癯者乎律例
有定制也姦僞滋起而科條日以煩焉顧
摘發及于毫芒而吞舟漏于密網矣不有
如所謂絞繩急而勢欲絕者乎京邊諸衛
軍有定籍始固未嘗借兵于他境也顧行
伍日虛不得已而爲召募調遣之策矣然
土著之操練無期而客兵之寄寓者終無
足恃豈創立軍政之初意乎財用裒益本
punctuated: 不能盡如其舊矣。愚請得以誦言而無諱，可乎？里甲有定役也，憫其疾苦而易以官支之法，于民誠得矣。乃或有陽爲奉法，陰便私圖，使逐末者代其勞，而應役者享其逸，豈因賦定役之意乎？田稅有定額也，慮其低昂而議以清丈之法，于事誠便矣。乃或有吏售其姦，民滋其僞，使富者益其膏，而貧者甚其困，豈則壤成賦之意乎？官制有定秩也，時值多故，或因事以增設焉。顧事未收專責之效，而民已受多牧之擾矣，不有如所謂「廐長立而馬益癯」者乎？律例有定制也，姦僞滋起，而科條日以煩焉。顧摘發及于毫芒，而吞舟漏于密網矣，不有如所謂「絞繩急而勢欲絕」者乎？京邊諸衛，軍有定籍，始固未嘗借兵于他境也。顧行伍日虛，不得已而爲召募調遣之策矣。然土著之操練無期，而客兵之寄寓者終無足恃，豈創立軍政之初意乎？財用裒益，本
translation_en:
… cannot entirely match how things were in the past. May this humble candidate be permitted to speak openly without holding back?

The *lijia* (community tithing system) has fixed labor services. Taking pity on the people's hardships and replacing it with the method of official disbursement was indeed beneficial to the people. Yet there are some who outwardly comply with the law while secretly pursuing private schemes, causing those engaged in non-agricultural pursuits to bear the toil in their stead while those who ought to perform the service enjoy ease—how could this be the intention of determining labor service according to tax assessment?

Land taxes have fixed quotas. Worrying about disparities in assessments and proposing the method of cadastral resurveying was indeed convenient for administration. Yet there are cases where clerks practice their deceit and the people multiply their fraud, causing the rich to increase their fatness while the poor suffer even greater distress—how could this be the intention of establishing taxes according to soil quality?

The official system has fixed positions. In times of many troubles, posts have sometimes been added in response to particular affairs. Yet in practice, before the benefit of specialized responsibility is reaped, the people already suffer the disturbance of having too many herdsmen—is this not like the saying, "when stable masters are established, the horses grow ever thinner"?

The penal code and substatutes have fixed standards. As deceit and fraud increasingly arise, the statutory articles grow daily more numerous and繁 (burdensome). Yet while detection and exposure reach down to the finest hair, fishes large enough to swallow a boat slip through the dense net—is this not like the saying, "when the cord is twisted too tightly, it threatens to snap"?

In the various Guards of the capital and the frontiers, soldiers have fixed hereditary registers; in the beginning, troops were certainly never borrowed from other regions. Yet as the ranks grew daily more depleted, there was no choice but to resort to the expedients of recruiting mercenaries and transferring troops from elsewhere. Even so, there is no regular schedule for drilling the local garrison troops, while the guest troops temporarily quartered there are ultimately unreliable—how could this be the original intention in founding the military administration?

The balancing of fiscal revenues and expenditures originally …

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
有定數始固不必旁斂以取盈也顧司農
告匱不得已而爲鬻爵加稅之計矣然民
間之蓋藏已空而國用之經費者又不可
省豈量入爲出之初意乎屯政之設因農
寓兵法莫善於此者今則西北多曠土而
邊卒日惰矣東南多包佃而豪猾兼併矣
視諸藉耕爲守者何如也鹽政之行輸納
本色法孰便于此者今則改折議而開中
者因以罷耕矣超支立而常股者因之積
===
滯矣視諸就邊輸粟者何如也諸如此類
不可悉數人皆謂議法者之有遺慮也抑
孰知非法之咎哉患在奉法之未得其要
耳故愚以爲法之壅也有四弊焉夫政以
畫一而成法以多言而亂今則心心有主
意見各殊一利興議如聚訟一弊革發言
盈庭不暇計其利之及于民而先求其說
之勝于已此病在議論者一也守令最爲
親民循良貴在敦實今則違道干譽逞智
punctuated: 有定數，始固不必旁斂以取盈也。顧司農告匱，不得已而爲鬻爵加稅之計矣。然民間之蓋藏已空，而國用之經費者又不可省，豈量入爲出之初意乎？屯政之設，因農寓兵，法莫善於此者。今則西北多曠土，而邊卒日惰矣；東南多包佃，而豪猾兼併矣。視諸藉耕爲守者何如也？鹽政之行，輸納本色，法孰便于此者？今則改折議，而開中者因以罷耕矣；超支立，而常股者因之積滯矣。視諸就邊輸粟者何如也？諸如此類，不可悉數。人皆謂議法者之有遺慮也，抑孰知非法之咎哉？患在奉法之未得其要耳。故愚以爲法之壅也，有四弊焉：夫政以畫一而成，法以多言而亂。今則心心有主，意見各殊。一利興，議如聚訟；一弊革，發言盈庭。不暇計其利之及于民，而先求其說之勝于已。此病在議論者一也。守令最爲親民，循良貴在敦實。今則違道干譽，逞智
translation_en: …had fixed quotas, so in the beginning there was certainly no need to levy side taxes in order to make up a surplus. Yet the Ministry of Revenue reported exhaustion of funds, and out of necessity resorted to the schemes of selling ranks and increasing taxes. Even so, the storehouses among the people are already empty, while the regular expenditures for state finances cannot be reduced—how could this be the original intention of regulating expenditures according to income? In the establishment of the military colony administration (tunzheng), quartering soldiers by means of agriculture, no institution was better than this. Now, however, in the northwest there is much uncultivated land and the frontier soldiers grow lazier by the day; in the southeast there is much monopolized tenancy and powerful and cunning men engross the land. How does this compare with relying on farming as a means of defense? In the operation of the salt administration, delivering payments in kind—what institution was more convenient than this? Now, however, commutation to silver is proposed, and those participating in the salt-barter system (kaizhong) consequently abandon their farming; priority disbursement (chaozhi) is established, and the regular quota shares (changgu) consequently accumulate and stagnate. How does this compare with going to the frontier to deliver grain? Cases of this sort cannot all be enumerated. Everyone says that those who deliberated on the laws left things unconsidered, yet who knows that it is not the fault of the laws? The trouble lies simply in the fact that those who implement the laws have not grasped their essentials. Therefore, in my humble opinion, in the obstruction of the laws there are four abuses. Governance succeeds through uniformity, whereas laws are thrown into disorder by excessive talk. Now every mind has its own preconception, and opinions each differ. When a single benefit is promoted, the deliberations are like a crowded courtroom; when a single abuse is abolished, speeches fill the court. Officials have no leisure to calculate whether the benefit reaches the people, seeking first only that their own argument prevail for themselves. This is the first fault, which lies in excessive disputation. Prefects and magistrates are the officials closest to the people, and what is valued in dutiful and upright officials is substance and sincerity. Now, however, they depart from the Way to seek praise, showing off their cleverness…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
衍奇民俗本相安也而必欲更爲一令前
政本無弊也而不屑蹈其故常聽其言則
美考其效則疎此病在好名者二也材各
有長用宜器使今則諳于錢穀者乃或責
以刑名閑于文學者又或寄以戎務枉其
才而用之鮮不至于僨事此病在吏調者
三也夫豪傑之士不可以形迹拘近民之
政不可以旦夕計今則約束太嚴而法網
日密立功者或志隳于避謗報國者或計
===
沮于全身稍逸繩墨羣起而議其後矣此
病在文法者四也四弊不去而欲法之行
也得乎故謀事者虛中無我則議論省而
國是定矣親民者休養生息則實惠流而
耳目一矣任人者各盡所長則才智畢見
而事功集矣馭吏者寛其文法則施爲有
序而治效臻矣由是本精明之心裕敦大
之體操縱損益無施不可而
祖宗之法雖萬世守之可也又何至於滋弊而
punctuated: 衍奇，民俗本相安也，而必欲更爲一令；前政本無弊也，而不屑蹈其故常。聽其言則美，考其效則疎，此病在好名者二也。材各有長，用宜器使。今則諳于錢穀者，乃或責以刑名；閑于文學者，又或寄以戎務。枉其才而用之，鮮不至于僨事，此病在吏調者三也。夫豪傑之士，不可以形迹拘；近民之政，不可以旦夕計。今則約束太嚴，而法網日密。立功者或志隳于避謗，報國者或計沮于全身，稍逸繩墨，羣起而議其後矣，此病在文法者四也。四弊不去，而欲法之行也，得乎？故謀事者虛中無我，則議論省而國是定矣；親民者休養生息，則實惠流而耳目一矣；任人者各盡所長，則才智畢見而事功集矣；馭吏者寛其文法，則施爲有序而治效臻矣。由是本精明之心，裕敦大之體，操縱損益，無施不可，而祖宗之法雖萬世守之可也，又何至於滋弊而
translation_en:
…and display novelty; popular customs are originally at peace with one another, yet they insist on issuing new ordinances; the administration of their predecessors originally had no abuses, yet they disdain to follow established routines. When one listens to their words, they sound admirable, but when one examines their results, they are meager. This is the second malady, which lies in the pursuit of reputation.

Talents each have their strengths, and in employing them one should assign them according to their capacities. Nowadays, however, those well-versed in fiscal and grain administration are sometimes charged with judicial affairs, while those skilled in literature and scholarship are sometimes entrusted with military matters. When men are employed by distorting their talents, it rarely fails to ruin affairs. This is the third malady, which lies in the transfer and appointment of officials.

Men of heroic and outstanding caliber cannot be bound by outward appearances, and governance that is close to the people cannot be reckoned in a single morning or evening. Nowadays, however, restrictions are too strict and the net of the law grows daily tighter. Those who would establish merit sometimes have their resolve destroyed in avoiding slander, and those who would repay the state sometimes have their plans frustrated in preserving themselves; if they deviate ever so slightly from the letter of the rules, the crowd rises up to criticize them from behind. This is the fourth malady, which lies in pettifogging regulations. If these four abuses are not removed, how can one expect the laws to take effect?

Therefore, if those who plan affairs keep an open mind without ego, debates will be curtailed and state policy will be settled; if those who are close to the people foster rest and recuperation,实质 benefits will flow and the eyes and ears of the populace will be unified; if those who appoint men allow each to exhaust his strengths, talents and wisdom will be fully manifested and accomplishments will be achieved; if those who direct officials relax their pettifogging regulations, administrative measures will be orderly and the effects of good governance will be attained. Proceeding from this—grounding oneself in a discerning mind and cultivating a magnanimous and generous substance, tightening or relaxing, diminishing or augmenting—there will be nothing that cannot be carried out, and the laws of the Imperial Ancestors may be preserved even for ten thousand generations! How then could they ever come to breed abuses and…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
擾民也哉
第四問
王樌
同考試官教諭阮　批〔人物策敘述之贍非難權度之精爲難此篇論雅産賢豪悉其行實醇疵莫遁而尤能進取於文武之兼材子其善學鄉先哲而思集其成者乎〕
同考試官教諭唐　批〔論人貴恕取友貴嚴此尚論者之準也是作剖析同異評隲不苟究極始終決擇不苟可以觀尚友之學矣〕
===
考試官學正宋　批〔上下古今綜覈詳確〕
考試官教授劉　批〔鑑別人品卓有定衡〕
君子之稽往哲也其尚論也貴恕而尚友
也貴嚴夫天之生才二氣紛糅間值其淳
甚矣才之不易兼也如必兼才而後與之
則將曠千載其一遇而偏長之士舉無以
自見於時豈君子節取之道乎然取宜恕
也而論人欲盡論可貸也而責己欲嚴是
故人才盡于文武而文武各擅其長操觚
punctuated:
擾民也哉！
第四問
王樌
同考試官教諭阮　批〔人物策敘述之贍非難，權度之精爲難。此篇論雅産賢豪，悉其行實，醇疵莫遁，而尤能進取於文武之兼材，子其善學鄉先哲而思集其成者乎？〕
同考試官教諭唐　批〔論人貴恕，取友貴嚴，此尚論者之準也。是作剖析同異，評隲不苟；究極始終，決擇不苟，可以觀尚友之學矣。〕
考試官學正宋　批〔上下古今，綜覈詳確。〕
考試官教授劉　批〔鑑別人品，卓有定衡。〕
君子之稽往哲也，其尚論也貴恕，而尚友也貴嚴。夫天之生才，二氣紛糅，間值其淳，甚矣才之不易兼也！如必兼才而後與之，則將曠千載其一遇，而偏長之士舉無以自見於時，豈君子節取之道乎？然取宜恕也，而論人欲盡；論可貸也，而責己欲嚴。是故人才盡于文武，而文武各擅其長：操觚…
translation_en:
…harassing the people!

Fourth Question
Wang Guan 王樌
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Ruan 阮 comments: 〔In a policy essay on historical figures, abundance of narrative is not difficult; precision of judgment and evaluation is what is difficult. This essay discusses the worthies and heroes born in this refined land [Shaanxi], thoroughly detailing their actual conduct so that neither purity nor flaw can escape notice, and it is especially able to press forward toward combined civil and military talent. Are you not one who excels at learning from the former worthies of your native region and aspires to synthesize their achievements into a complete whole?〕
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Tang 唐 comments: 〔In evaluating men, one values leniency; in choosing friends, one values strictness. This is the standard for those who critically assess the ancients. This composition analyzes similarities and differences without being careless in its appraisal, and investigates beginnings and ends thoroughly without being careless in its choices. From it one may observe the learning of making friends with the ancients.〕
Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Song 宋 comments: 〔Surveying antiquity and the present, its comprehensive verification is detailed and exact.〕
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Liu 劉 comments: 〔In discerning and evaluating personal character, it possesses an outstanding and settled standard.〕

When a gentleman examines the former sages, in critically assessing them he values leniency, whereas in making friends with them he values strictness. Now, when Heaven gives birth to talent, the two vital energies [yin and yang] intermingle in confusion and only occasionally hit upon pureness; extreme indeed is the difficulty of combining talents in one person! If one insists on combined talents before granting approval, then one would wait a thousand years for a single encounter, and men of specialized strengths would all have no way to distinguish themselves in their own time—how could that be the gentleman's way of selective approval? Yet while approval ought to be lenient, the assessment of men must be exhaustive; while assessment may make allowances, the demands placed upon oneself must be strict. Therefore, human talent is encompassed within the civil and the military, and the civil and the military each excel in their own strengths: those who wield the writing tablet…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
藝苑者風雲之陣未閑建標戎幕者月露
之形罔識世兼兩端而時出之者幾何此
固造物所靳振古云難於是而求之備也
抑過矣第體道者必會其全立已者當用
其極通爼豆干戈之肄集隨陸絳灌之成
而章逢介冑初不判爲二焉夫是之謂兼
才君子所以表裏人物者其斯以爲至乎
維關中古雍州域星分井鬼度析柳張東
壁臨于燉煌斗魁耿于積石其地則華嶽
===
嶮嶒終南聯亘崑崙河渭形勢靈長允矣
金城天府百二之勝而淸淑盤礴鍾爲人
豪詎無以文武著稱其間者邪兹試以文
言之傳聖學師魏侯而西河目以聖人者
卜子夏也續左國作史記而劉向稱爲良
史者司馬遷也班固著漢書以討前史之
失范氏嘉其詳而有體魏相上書奏以止
無名之師胡氏賛爲經國遠猷通明典廢
作經傳集解而當武庫之稱者非杜預乎
punctuated:
藝苑者，風雲之陣未閑；建標戎幕者，月露之形罔識。世兼兩端而時出之者幾何？此固造物所靳，振古云難。於是而求之備也，抑過矣。第體道者必會其全，立已者當用其極。通爼豆干戈之肄，集隨、陸、絳、灌之成，而章逢、介冑初不判爲二焉。夫是之謂兼才，君子所以表裏人物者，其斯以爲至乎！

維關中古雍州域，星分井、鬼，度析柳、張。東壁臨于燉煌，斗魁耿于積石。其地則華嶽嶮嶒，終南聯亘，崑崙、河、渭，形勢靈長。允矣金城天府、百二之勝，而淸淑盤礴，鍾爲人豪，詎無以文武著稱其間者邪？兹試以文言之：傳聖學、師魏侯，而西河目以聖人者，卜子夏也；續《左》《國》、作《史記》，而劉向稱爲良史者，司馬遷也；班固著《漢書》以討前史之失，范氏嘉其詳而有體；魏相上書奏以止無名之師，胡氏賛爲經國遠猷；通明典廢，作《經傳集解》，而當「武庫」之稱者，非杜預乎？
translation_en:
… [those who wield the writing tablet] in the garden of letters are unpracticed in the battle formations of wind and clouds, while those who raise their standards in military headquarters know nothing of the literary forms of moon and dew. How many in the world combine both extremes and bring them forth as the occasion demands? This is indeed what the Creator begrudges and what has been called difficult since antiquity. To demand perfection in this regard is surely excessive. Yet one who embodies the Way must comprehend its entirety, and one who establishes himself ought to exert himself to the utmost. By mastering the practices of both sacrificial vessels and shields and spears, and by bringing together the achievements of Sui He, Lu Jia, Zhou Bo of Jiang, and Guan Ying, the scholar's robes and the soldier's armor are never split into two. Now this is what is called combined talent; that by which the gentleman integrates human capacities within and without—does it not reach its pinnacle in this?

Now Guanzhong is the territory of ancient Yongzhou. In stellar field-allocation it corresponds to the Well (Jing) and Ghost (Gui) lodges, with degrees divided into the Willow (Liu) and Extended Net (Zhang) lodges; the Eastern Wall (Dongbi) overlooks Dun煌 (Dunhuang), and the Bowl of the Dipper (Doukui) shines brightly over Jishi. As for its topography, Mount Hua rises precipitously, the Zhongnan range stretches continuously, and with the Kunlun Mountains and the Yellow and Wei Rivers, its terrain is numinous and enduring. Truly it possesses the strategic superiority of a "citadel of metal," a "storehouse of Heaven," where two men can hold off a hundred! And where its pure and auspicious vital energy accumulates and concentrates into heroic figures, how could there be none among them renowned for civil and military accomplishments? Let us now try to speak of it in terms of civil culture: He who transmitted the learning of the Sage, served as tutor to Marquis Wen of Wei, and was regarded by the people of Xihe as a sage himself, was Bu Zixia (卜子夏). He who continued the Zuo Tradition (Zuozhuan) and the Discourses of the States (Guoyu) to compose the Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji), and was praised by Liu Xiang (劉向) as a fine historian, was Sima Qian (司馬遷). Ban Gu (班固) compiled the Book of Han (Hanshu) to examine the shortcomings of earlier histories, and Fan Ye praised it for being detailed and well-structured. Wei Xiang (魏相) submitted memorials to halt an unjustified military campaign, and Mr. Hu (Hu Yin) lauded this as a far-sighted plan for governing the state. And he who thoroughly understood the rise and fall of institutions, composed the Collected Explanations of the Classic and Tradition (Jingzhuan jijie), and earned the sobriquet "Armory" (Wuku)—was that not Du Yu (杜預)?…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
而袁朗月賦清灑出塵後主嘆謝莊不得
獨美於前者此也沉潛典籍作玄晏春秋
而盛書窰之號者非皇甫謐乎而杜甫詩
史羽翼風雅元稹謂詩人以來所未有者
此也夫數子者學優辭贍均以文鳴其皆
足以潤色乎太平者與以武言之杖節穹
廬而圖形麟閣者蘇武也振威西域而封
侯燕頷者班超也李靖輕兵邀敵遂摧突
厥以渠盟渭之恥郭子儀單騎入壘卒屈
===
回紇以沮猾夏之謀示虜目中據鞍矍鑠
以收交趾之績者非馬援乎而韓世忠之
挺戈擒敵賊黨就俘此忠勇之旗所由褒
也運籌幄內飲博笑談以却澶淵之師者
非寇準乎而劉錡乘電擊營兀朮破膽此
順昌之幟所由讋也夫數子者勁氣精忠
咸以武著其皆足以戡定乎禍亂者與夫
脩文奮武昔人固各擅一長矣而執事猶
欲指其人而上下之顧愚非康成也敢輕
punctuated: 而袁朗《月賦》清灑出塵，後主嘆謝莊不得獨美於前者，此也。沉潛典籍，作《玄晏春秋》而盛「書窰」之號者，非皇甫謐乎？而杜甫「詩史」羽翼風雅，元稹謂詩人以來所未有者，此也。夫數子者，學優辭贍，均以文鳴，其皆足以潤色乎太平者與？以武言之，杖節穹廬而圖形麟閣者，蘇武也；振威西域而封侯燕頷者，班超也；李靖輕兵邀敵，遂摧突厥以渠盟渭之恥；郭子儀單騎入壘，卒屈回紇以沮猾夏之謀。示虜目中，據鞍矍鑠，以收交趾之績者，非馬援乎？而韓世忠之挺戈擒敵，賊黨就俘，此「忠勇」之旗所由褒也。運籌幄內，飲博笑談，以却澶淵之師者，非寇準乎？而劉錡乘電擊營，兀朮破膽，此順昌之幟所由讋也。夫數子者，勁氣精忠，咸以武著，其皆足以戡定乎禍亂者與？夫脩文奮武，昔人固各擅一長矣，而執事猶欲指其人而上下之，顧愚非康成也，敢輕…
translation_en:
…And as for Yuan Lang 袁朗, whose Rhapsody on the Moon (Yue fu 月賦) was so pure, graceful, and transcendent that the Last Ruler sighed that Xie Zhuang 謝莊 could no longer claim sole beauty before him—such was he. Deeply immersed in canonical texts, authoring the Spring and Autumn Annals of Xuanyan (Xuanyan chunqiu 玄晏春秋), and renowned under the moniker of "Book-obsessed" [?] (Shuyao 書窰)—was that not Huangfu Mi 皇甫謐? And as for Du Fu 杜甫, whose "poetic history" gave wings to the Airs and Odes, and whom Yuan Zhen 元稹 declared unprecedented since the dawn of poets—such was he. All of these several gentlemen excelled in learning and were rich in literary expression, alike winning renown through civil letters; were they not all sufficient to lend luster to an era of Great Peace?

To speak in terms of martial prowess: leaning on his staff of authority among the felt tents of the steppe and having his portrait painted in the Unicorn Pavilion—that was Su Wu 蘇武. Projecting awe across the Western Regions and, with his swallow-like jaw, being enfeoffed as a marquis—that was Ban Chao 班超. Li Jing 李靖 intercepted the enemy with light troops, thereby crushing the Tujue 突厥 (Turks) to wash away [?] (qu 渠) the shame of the covenant at the Wei River. Guo Ziyi 郭子儀 rode alone into the enemy's ramparts, ultimately bending the Huihe 回紇 (Uyghurs) to submission and thwarting their plot to disturb the Chinese realm. Laying out the enemy's terrain before the Emperor's eyes, mounting his saddle in hale and hearty vigor, and thereby achieving the pacification of Jiaozhi 交趾—was that not Ma Yuan 馬援? And as for Han Shizhong 韓世忠 brandishing his spear to seize the foe and bringing the rebel band into captivity—this was why he was honored with the banner inscribed "Loyal and Brave." Devising strategies within the command tent, drinking, gaming, laughing, and chatting while repelling the enemy host at Chanyuan 澶淵—was that not Kou Zhun 寇準? And as for Liu Qi 劉錡 taking advantage of a thunderstorm to strike the enemy camp, striking terror into the heart of Wuzhu 兀朮—this was why his standards at Shunchang 順昌 inspired such dread. All of these several gentlemen possessed unyielding spirit and pure loyalty, alike becoming famous for martial valor; were they not all sufficient to quell disaster and rebellion?

Now, in cultivating civil virtue and displaying martial might, the men of old indeed each excelled in one specialty. Yet Your Excellency still wishes to point to these men and rank them as superior or inferior. Considering that this foolish candidate is no Kangcheng 康成 (Zheng Xuan 鄭玄), how could I dare lightly…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
議哉雖然按往蹟拾定論亦嘗得其槩矣
遷固之博綜古今良史才也然是非頗繆
於聖人阿附則甘於貴戚袁杜之鏗鍧金
石亢詞宗也然狎客僅江孔之伍迂士非
稷契之倫魏相爲中興賢輔而霸王之雜
申韓之崇則無能改於其治士安爲季世
逸民而誦說之勤著述之富則奚有補於
其時其惟莒父乎芻豢生色詩易研精由
是而列文學之賢科無愧矣若元凱之指
===
授方略功冠平吳則又文之未始不爲武
也忠勇如子卿定遠壯矣乃詭傳鴈札而
釁啓玉關疚之不終無也勞伐如伏波衛
國偉矣乃謗累明珠而蹀血虜庭疵之不
相掩也世忠振威金虜社稷攸賴而莫須
有之詰竟不能直武穆之寃劉錡廓氛姑
鞎干城是寄而何必問之答卒無以伸愧
死之憤其惟汾陽乎動塞宇宙信行蠻貊
由是而應虜占之大人誠宜矣若平仲之
punctuated: 議哉？雖然，按往蹟，拾定論，亦嘗得其槩矣。遷、固之博綜古今，良史才也；然是非頗繆於聖人，阿附則甘於貴戚。袁、杜之鏗鍧金石，亢詞宗也；然狎客僅江、孔之伍，迂士非稷、契之倫。魏相爲中興賢輔，而霸王之雜、申韓之崇，則無能改於其治。士安爲季世逸民，而誦說之勤、著述之富，則奚有補於其時？其惟莒父乎！芻豢生色，《詩》、《易》研精，由是而列文學之賢科，無愧矣。若元凱之指授方略，功冠平吳，則又文之未始不爲武也。忠勇如子卿、定遠，壯矣；乃詭傳鴈札，而釁啓玉關，疚之不終無也。勞伐如伏波、衛國，偉矣；乃謗累明珠，而蹀血虜庭，疵之不相掩也。世忠振威金虜，社稷攸賴，而「莫須有」之詰，竟不能直武穆之寃。劉錡廓氛姑鞎，干城是寄，而「何必問」之答，卒無以伸愧死之憤。其惟汾陽乎！動塞宇宙，信行蠻貊，由是而應虜占之大人，誠宜矣。若平仲之
translation_en:
… judge them? Even so, by examining their past deeds and gathering established judgments, one may grasp the general outline. Sima Qian 司馬遷 and Ban Gu 班固, in their broad synthesis of past and present, possessed the talent of fine historians; yet their judgments of right and wrong diverged considerably from those of the Sages, and in their flattery they willingly attached themselves to consort clans. Yuan Hong 袁宏 and Du Fu 杜甫, whose writings resonated like bronze and stone, were lofty masters of literature; yet the familiar guest was merely in the company of Jiang Zong 江總 and Kong Fan 孔範, and the impractical scholar was not of the same class as Hou Ji 后稷 and Xie 契. Wei Xiang 魏相 was a worthy Chief Minister of a dynastic restoration, yet with his mixture of the ways of Hegemon and True King and his veneration of Shen Buhai 申不害 and Han Fei 韓非, he was unable to reform the governance of his day. Huangfu Mi 皇甫謐 (courtesy name Shi'an 士安) was a recluse of a declining age, yet for all the diligence of his recitation and exposition and the richness of his writings, what benefit did they bring to his times? Is it not Zixia 子夏 (Bu Shang 卜商, courtesy name Ju'fu 莒父) alone who excels? Giving luster to moral cultivation as if feasting on grass- and grain-fed meats, and probing the subtle essence of the Book of Odes (Shi) and the Book of Changes (Yi), he was thereby ranked in the worthy category of literature and learning without shame. And as for Du Yu 杜預 (courtesy name Yuankai 元凱), who directed strategic plans and stood first in merit in the pacification of Wu, this shows that literary men have never been incapable of military achievement.

Loyalty and bravery like those of Su Wu 蘇武 (courtesy name Ziqing 子卿) and Ban Chao 班超 (Marquis of Dingyuan 定遠) were magnificent indeed; yet the ruse of the letter tied to a wild goose and the opening of hostilities beyond the Jade Gate were blemishes from which they were not entirely free. Meritorious campaigns like those of Ma Yuan 馬援 (General Who Calms the Waves, Fubo 伏波) and Li Jing 李靖 (Duke of Weiguo 衛國) were grand indeed; yet the slander incurred over the bright pearls [southern coix seeds] and the spilling of blood in the barbarian court were flaws that could not be concealed. Han Shizhong 韓世忠 projected awe over the Jurchen Jin, and the altars of state depended upon him; yet when he questioned Qin Hui over the charge of "perhaps there is," he ultimately could not right the injustice done to Yue Fei 岳飛 (posthumously Wumu 武穆). Liu Qi 劉錡 swept away the miasma of war at Shuchang [? 姑鞎], and was entrusted as a bulwark of the state; yet after the reply "why need you ask?", he had no way in the end to vent the indignation that made him die of shame. Is it not Guo Ziyi 郭子儀 (Prince of Fenyang 汾陽) alone who excels? His deeds [reading 勳 for 動] filled the universe, and his trustworthiness extended to the barbarian tribes; thus his corresponding to the "Great Man" foretold by the barbarians' divination was truly fitting. And as for Kou Zhun 寇準 (courtesy name Pingzhong 平仲), who…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
齠齡詠華弱冠登科則又武之未始不爲
文也高下相懸偏全互異此三代而下之
才君子每節取焉然論世不可不盡友善
不可不嚴緬惟三代之英豈無有進於是
者乎是故躬耕莘野者伊尹也阿衡啓佑
謨訓具存文孰加焉然升陑之師天下無
敵此尤其聖武之布昭矣垂釣磻溪者太
公也燮伐鷹揚永清四海武孰加焉然丹
書之戒聖學以明此尤其文德之振修矣
===
之二子者詎非間氣之鍾兼才之選也哉
然則尚友者舍此將誰歸也是必窮而在
下則學伊呂之所學而涵養其敬義誦讀
其詩書達而在上則志伊呂之所志而堯
舜其君民商周其事業又遡之子夏以端
其軌絫之遷固以博其趣肆之魏杜袁皇
以㟐其思融數子之英華而澤之於道德
醇如也天下之至文不在是哉遡之郭寇
以效其忠持之蘇韓以礪其節奮之班馬
punctuated: 齠齡詠華，弱冠登科，則又武之未始不爲文也。高下相懸，偏全互異，此三代而下之才，君子每節取焉。然論世不可不盡，友善不可不嚴，緬惟三代之英，豈無有進於是者乎？是故躬耕莘野者，伊尹也。阿衡啓佑，謨訓具存，文孰加焉？然升陑之師，天下無敵，此尤其聖武之布昭矣。垂釣磻溪者，太公也。燮伐鷹揚，永清四海，武孰加焉？然《丹書》之戒，聖學以明，此尤其文德之振修矣。之二子者，詎非間氣之鍾、兼才之選也哉？然則尚友者，舍此將誰歸也？是必窮而在下，則學伊、呂之所學，而涵養其敬義，誦讀其詩書；達而在上，則志伊、呂之所志，而堯、舜其君民，商、周其事業。又遡之子夏以端其軌，絫之遷、固以博其趣，肆之魏、杜、袁、皇以㟐其思，融數子之英華而澤之於道德，醇如也，天下之至文不在是哉！遡之郭、寇以效其忠，持之蘇、韓以礪其節，奮之班、馬、
translation_en: …composing verses on Mount Hua in his childhood and passing the civil examination at the age of twenty, this shows how a man of martial prowess was not without literary accomplishment. With their varying degrees of superiority and inferiority, and their differing balances of partiality and completeness, these are the talents from the Three Dynasties downward, from whom the gentleman always selectively adopts what is good. Yet in assessing historical ages one must be thorough, and in befriending the good one must be strict.
