Reflecting back upon the heroes of the Three Dynasties, could there not be those who surpassed them? Therefore, he who personally plowed in the wilds of Youxin was Yi Yin 伊尹. As Protector-Minister (Aheng) he guided and assisted his ruler, and his counsels and instructions are fully preserved—what literary achievement could surpass this? Yet in the campaign at Sheng'er, his army was unmatched in the world, which especially manifested the brilliance of his sacred martial valor. He who cast his fishing line in the Pan Stream was Duke Tai 太公 (Lü Shang 呂尚). Harmoniously smiting and soaring like a hawk, he forever pacified the Four Seas—what martial achievement could surpass this? Yet through the admonitions of the Cinnabar Book (Danshu), the learning of the sages was illuminated, which especially demonstrated the cultivation and flourishing of his civil virtue. Were not these two worthies endowed with the finest vital essence of the universe and the very models of combined civil and martial talent? If so, to whom else should one who seeks friendship with the ancients turn? Thus, when in obscurity and in a lowly station, one must study what Yi Yin and Lü Shang studied, nurturing one's reverence and righteousness and reciting the Odes and Documents; when prominent and in a high station, one must set one's ambition on what Yi Yin and Lü Shang aspired to, making one's ruler and people like Yao and Shun, and one's achievements like those of the Shang and Zhou. Furthermore, one should trace back to Zixia 子夏 (Bu Shang 卜商) to rectify one's path, accumulate from Sima Qian 司馬遷 and Ban Gu 班固 to broaden one's sensibilities, and give free rein through Wei Zheng 魏徵, Du Ru晦 杜如晦 [or Du You 杜佑/Du Fu 杜甫], Yuan Shu 袁樞, and Huangfu Mi 皇甫湜/皇甫謐 to elevate one's thoughts; fusing the finest blossoms of these several masters and enriching them with moral virtue until they are pure and mellow—does not the supreme literary achievement of the world lie herein? One should also trace back to Guo Ziyi 郭子儀 and Kou Zhun 寇準 to emulate their loyalty, uphold Su Wu 蘇武 and Han Qi 韓琦 [or Han Yu] to sharpen one's integrity, and rouse oneself through Ban Chao 班超, Ma Yuan 馬援, …

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
韓劉以壯其猷衰數子之智力而約之於
韜略淵如也天下之大武不在是哉允若
玆則合德業而會其全兼文武而時其出
庶幾尚友之極而於豐鎬思皇之士星躔
河嶽之靈爲無負矣雖然此固士之自待
也而非所以語國家之待士也蓋律身如
良冶用人如大匠故太阿鑄于洪爐必堅
鋼百鍊而後可以試盤錯巨室成于衆美
必寸朽不棄而後可以樹崇高此造優貴
===
精而掄材者當器使也若求文武於天下
必欲如士之責已者而求備焉斯下有遺
才上多廢事矣必也法虞廷之翕受敷施
如周官之因能授任以兼才者握樞機以
偏才者典職守于凡濡毫投石之士足以
贊文德翼武功者舉得以自效其技庶濟
濟多士熙載奮庸鷹揚之傑不終老於磻
溪一德之英不躬耕於莘野以至文如班
馬武若蘇韓者莫不攄猷宣力奮勇效謀
punctuated: 韓、劉以壯其猷，衰數子之智力而約之於韜略，淵如也，天下之大武不在是哉！允若玆，則合德業而會其全，兼文武而時其出，庶幾尚友之極，而於豐、鎬思皇之士，星躔河嶽之靈，爲無負矣。雖然，此固士之自待也，而非所以語國家之待士也。蓋律身如良冶，用人如大匠。故太阿鑄于洪爐，必堅鋼百鍊，而後可以試盤錯；巨室成于衆美，必寸朽不棄，而後可以樹崇高。此造優貴精，而掄材者當器使也。若求文武於天下，必欲如士之責已者而求備焉，斯下有遺才，上多廢事矣。必也法虞廷之翕受敷施，如周官之因能授任，以兼才者握樞機，以偏才者典職守，于凡濡毫投石之士，足以贊文德、翼武功者，舉得以自效其技。庶濟濟多士，熙載奮庸，鷹揚之傑不終老於磻溪，一德之英不躬耕於莘野，以至文如班、馬，武若蘇、韓者，莫不攄猷宣力，奮勇效謀，
translation_en:
… Han [Chongguo] and Liu [Qi] to strengthen his strategic plans—gathering [衰, read 裒] the wisdom and strength of these several masters and condensing them into military strategy, how profound it will be! Does not the greatest martial prowess in the world lie right here? If one truly acts thus, uniting moral virtue and practical achievement in their entirety, combining civil and military capabilities and bringing them forth at the proper time, one will come close to the pinnacle of befriending the ancients, and will not fail the abundant and august scholars of Feng and Hao or the numinous spirit of the stellar mansions, rivers, and mountains.

Even so, this is assuredly how a scholar holds expectations for himself, and not how one speaks of the state's treatment of scholars. For disciplining oneself is like being a master smith, whereas employing others is like being a master carpenter. Thus, when the Tai'e sword is cast in a great furnace, its hard steel must be tempered a hundred times before it can be tested on gnarled knots; when a great mansion is completed from an array of fine timbers, not even an inch of decayed wood is discarded before it can be erected to a lofty height. This is because in cultivating excellence [造優, or 造士?] one values refinement, whereas in selecting talent one ought to employ men according to their specific capacities. If, in seeking civil and military talents throughout the realm, the state insists on demanding perfection just as a scholar demands it of himself, then below there will be overlooked talents, and above there will be many neglected affairs.

Instead, the state must model itself on the court of Yu in broadly receiving talents and广泛 deploying them, and follow the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) in bestowing posts according to ability—putting those with comprehensive talents in charge of the pivotal mechanisms of government, and assigning those with specialized talents to specific offices. Thus, among all scholars who moisten the writing brush or hurl stones, everyone who is capable of assisting civil virtue or supporting martial merit will be able to dedicate his skills. In this way, the multitude of dignified scholars will brighten the imperial undertakings and exert themselves in meritorious service; heroes soaring like eagles [such as Lü Shang] will not grow old and die by the Pan Stream, and paragons of pure, single-minded virtue [such as Yi Yin] will not remain plowing with their own hands in the wilds of Shen; and even those with literary brilliance like Ban [Gu] and Sima [Qian], or martial valor like Su [Wu] and Han [Chongguo], will all without exception unfold their plans, put forth their strength, rouse their courage, and offer their counsel, …

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
則安攘得人而經緯益著所以鋪張鴻業
建威銷萌者不特雍士為然矣又安有乏
才之嘆也哉
第五問
馮祥
同考試官教諭賫　批〔遠稽古制近酌時宜內畫上中二計責在得人而篇終復歸本〕
朝廷皆不易之論也孰謂救荒無奇策乎
同考試官教諭何　批〔為國者不患歲祲特患無以備之此策指陳荒政根極源委而尤惓惓於監司守令是責備荒無遺〕
===
考試官學正宋　批〔條答成周各代救荒之法甚悉而歷陳時政皆鑿鑿可行真俊傑之才也〕
筭矣
考試官教授劉　批〔論賑貸在豫詳確可行〕
嘗聞先時而計者易為力後時而謀者難
為功蓋計苟先矣則事立於豫即有卒然
之變可恃以無恐若謀之不先而變之來
也徒苟且以應之其曷以濟譬諸理家者
punctuated:
則安攘得人，而經緯益著。所以鋪張鴻業、建威銷萌者，不特雍士為然矣，又安有乏才之嘆也哉！

第五問
馮祥
同考試官教諭賫　批〔遠稽古制，近酌時宜，內畫上中二計，責在得人，而篇終復歸本〕朝廷，皆不易之論也。孰謂救荒無奇策乎？
同考試官教諭何　批〔為國者不患歲祲，特患無以備之。此策指陳荒政，根極源委，而尤惓惓於監司、守令是責，備荒無遺〕筭矣。
考試官學正宋　批〔條答成周各代救荒之法甚悉，而歷陳時政，皆鑿鑿可行，真俊傑之才也。〕
考試官教授劉　批〔論賑貸在豫，詳確可行。〕

嘗聞先時而計者易為力，後時而謀者難為功。蓋計苟先矣，則事立於豫，即有卒然之變，可恃以無恐；若謀之不先，而變之來也，徒苟且以應之，其曷以濟？譬諸理家者，
translation_en:
…then the right men will be found for bringing peace within and repelling threats without, and the warp and woof of governance will become ever more manifest. Thus, those who spread forth the grand enterprise, establish awe, andnip rebellion in the bud will not be limited to the scholars of Yongzhou [Shaanxi] alone—how then could there still be any lament over a scarcity of talent!

Fifth Question
Feng Xiang 馮祥
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Ji 賫, comments: 〔He reaches far back to examine ancient institutions and weighs immediate circumstances to suit the needs of the time. Within, he outlines the best and second-best plans, placing the responsibility on finding the right men, and at the end of the essay returns the root of the matter to〕 the Imperial Court—all of these are unalterable arguments. Who says there is no extraordinary policy for famine relief?
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) He 何, comments: 〔Those who govern a state do not worry about years of dearth, but only about having nothing with which to prepare for them. This policy essay points out and sets forth famine-relief administration, tracing it thoroughly from root to branch, and is especially earnest in holding the Surveillance Officials (jiansi) and the Prefects and Magistrates (shouling) responsible—in preparing for famine it leaves no〕 miscalculation [or: unreckoned detail].
Examiner, Director of Studies (xuezheng) Song 宋, comments: 〔He responds point by point regarding the famine-relief methods of the flourishing Zhou and successive dynasties in great detail, and sets forth current governance item by item, all of it concrete and practicable—truly an outstanding talent.〕
Examiner, Instructor (jiaoshou) Liu 劉, comments: 〔His discussion of relief and lending rests on advance preparation; it is detailed, precise, and practicable.〕

I have heard that planning ahead of time makes effort easy, whereas scheming after the fact makes achievement difficult. For if plans are made beforehand, affairs are established through advance preparation, and even if a sudden crisis occurs, one can rely on those preparations and have nothing to fear. If, however, one does not plan beforehand, and when a crisis arrives merely responds to it in a makeshift manner, how can that be of any help? Take, for example, one who manages a household: …

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
勤於力本積貯豐矣素封之樂豈間於祲
歲哉否則其本撥其用易窮卽有小歉不
至於枵腹啼寒也者幾希知此可以策救
荒復明問矣昔人謂救荒無奇策固矣然
九年之水堯不能必天之不久溢也而堯
之民卒無捐瘠者非以協和時雍備之豫
乎七年之旱湯不能必天之無恒暘也而
湯之民卒無捐瘠者非以子惠輯寧備之
豫乎嗣是而後語救荒者莫過於周禮王
===
制二書周禮所載遺人掌鄉里之委積以
恤民之囏阨縣都之委積以待凶荒廩人
掌九穀之數以歲之上下數邦國以詔年
之豐凶而又有鄉師以歲時賙民其詳蓋
錯見於六官之書當其時民皆受田矣又
有田畯以率甸人匠人以治溝洫遂人以
興水利稻人以祛水害是以三年耕有一
年之食九年耕有三年之食以三十年之
通雖有凶旱水溢民無菜色誠有如王制
punctuated:
勤於力本，積貯豐矣，素封之樂，豈間於祲歲哉？否則，其本撥，其用易窮，卽有小歉，不至於枵腹啼寒也者幾希！知此，可以策救荒、復明問矣。

昔人謂「救荒無奇策」，固矣。然九年之水，堯不能必天之不久溢也，而堯之民卒無捐瘠者，非以協和時雍，備之豫乎？七年之旱，湯不能必天之無恒暘也，而湯之民卒無捐瘠者，非以子惠輯寧，備之豫乎？嗣是而後，語救荒者，莫過於《周禮》、《王制》二書。《周禮》所載：遺人掌鄉里之委積，以恤民之囏阨，縣都之委積，以待凶荒；廩人掌九穀之數，以歲之上下數邦國，以詔年之豐凶；而又有鄉師以歲時賙民。其詳蓋錯見於六官之書。當其時，民皆受田矣，又有田畯以率甸人，匠人以治溝洫，遂人以興水利，稻人以祛水害。是以三年耕有一年之食，九年耕有三年之食，以三十年之通，雖有凶旱水溢，民無菜色，誠有如《王制》…
translation_en:
…is diligent in exerting effort at the root [agriculture], his stored reserves will be abundant; how could the enjoyment of such untitled wealth be interrupted by a year of calamity? Otherwise, when the root is overturned and one's resources are easily exhausted, even if there is only a minor crop failure, few indeed will avoid going hungry and crying out from the cold! Understanding this, one can formulate policies on famine relief and reply to Your enlightened inquiry.

People of the past said that "for relieving famine there is no miraculous policy," which is certainly true. Yet during nine years of floods, Yao could not guarantee that Heaven would not inundate the land for long; that Yao's people ultimately did not die of starvation or waste away—was it not because through harmony and concord he had prepared for it in advance? During seven years of drought, Tang could not guarantee that Heaven would not send constant scorching sun; that Tang's people ultimately did not die of starvation or waste away—was it not because through paternal kindness and tranquil order he had prepared for it in advance? Thereafter, among those works that discuss famine relief, none surpass the two texts, the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) and the "Royal Regulations" (Wangzhi). As recorded in the Rites of Zhou: the Granary Master for Relief (Weiren) was in charge of the accumulated stores of the districts and neighborhoods in order to relieve the people's hardships and distress, and the accumulated stores of the counties and cities in order to await famines and crop failures; the Granary Master (Linren) was in charge of the quantities of the nine grains, calculating the needs of the state according to the high or low yields of the year in order to announce whether the year was abundant or lean; and there were also the District Preceptors (Xiangshi) to give seasonal aid to the people. The details of this are interspersed throughout the books of the Six Offices. At that time, the people all received allocations of land, and there were also Agricultural Overseers (Tianjun) to lead the Suburb Administrators (Dianren), Ditch Diggers (Jiangren) to manage the ditches and channels, Outlying-District Directors (Suiren) to promote water conservancy, and Paddy Masters (Daoren) to eliminate flood damage. Therefore, three years of plowing yielded one year's surplus of food, and nine years of plowing yielded three years' surplus of food. Calculated over a thirty-year period, even if there were bad droughts or floodwaters, the people did not have the sallow complexion of those subsisting on wild greens—truly just as the "Royal Regulations"…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
所云也其爲先事之防者何豫哉迨夫旱
溢適遭則發倉廩行荒政焉旣出夫鄉里
縣都之積矣而司徒之聚萬民者其法爲
尤詳旣食其三年九年之蓄矣而司救之
宣王命者其惠爲尤溥散利薄征未已也
而緩刑弛力與夫舍禁去幾者無弗至焉
眚災殺哀未已也而蕃樂多昏與夫索鬼
神除盜賊者無弗至焉太宰九式之掌均
節物用有喪荒之式具在秋官班班可考
===
其爲遇變之計者何至哉顧井田廢於阡
陌王籍去於兼倂卒有饑歲卽困流離故
臨事而曲爲之制亦有不可廢者如平糴
之法肇自李悝其糴也視歲稔以爲之等
其糴也視歲饑以爲之則蓋倣管仲之平
準者常平之倉建自漢耿壽昌穀賤則增
價而糴以利農穀貴則減價而糴以濟民
蓋倣李悝之平糴者義倉始於唐戴胄其
法欲王公以下輸穀賑民厥後太和累增
punctuated: 所云也。其爲先事之防者，何豫哉！迨夫旱溢適遭，則發倉廩、行荒政焉。旣出夫鄉里、縣都之積矣，而司徒之聚萬民者，其法爲尤詳；旣食其三年、九年之蓄矣，而司救之宣王命者，其惠爲尤溥。散利、薄征未已也，而緩刑、弛力，與夫舍禁、去幾者，無弗至焉；眚災、殺哀未已也，而蕃樂、多昏，與夫索鬼神、除盜賊者，無弗至焉。太宰九式之掌，均節物用，有喪荒之式，具在《秋官》，班班可考，其爲遇變之計者，何至哉！顧井田廢於阡陌，王籍去於兼倂，卒有饑歲，卽困流離。故臨事而曲爲之制，亦有不可廢者。如平糴之法，肇自李悝：其糴也，視歲稔以爲之等；其糴也，視歲饑以爲之則，蓋倣管仲之平準者。常平之倉，建自漢耿壽昌：穀賤則增價而糴以利農，穀貴則減價而糴以濟民，蓋倣李悝之平糴者。義倉始於唐戴胄：其法欲王公以下輸穀賑民，厥後太和累增
translation_en:
… states. How foresighted were its precautions taken beforehand! When droughts or floods chanced to occur, they opened the granaries and implemented famine relief policies. Not only did they distribute the reserves of the districts, neighborhoods, counties, and capitals, but the methods by which the Minister of Education (Situ) gathered the myriad people were especially detailed; not only did the people eat from the three-year and nine-year stores, but the benevolence with which the Mediator (Sijiu) proclaimed the king's commands was especially widespread. It did not stop at distributing goods and lightening taxes: mitigating punishments, relaxing corvée labor, lifting prohibitions, and removing customs inspections were all carried out to the utmost. It did not stop at economizing on rites and reducing mourning ceremonies: putting away musical instruments, encouraging marriages, offering prayers to spirits and deities, and eliminating bandits and thieves were all carried out to the utmost. Among the Nine Formulas (jiushi) managed by the Grand宰 (Taizai, Grand Steward) to equalize and regulate material expenditures, there is the formula for mourning and famine, all set forth in the Offices of Autumn (Qiuguan) [?], clearly verifiable one by one. How thorough were its plans for meeting emergencies!

Yet once the well-field system was abolished for field embankments and pathways, and the royal registers were discarded amid land annexations, whenever a year of famine suddenly struck, the people immediately suffered destitution and displacement. Therefore, ad hoc measures devised meticulously when crises arise also cannot be dispensed with. For instance, the method of equitable grain purchasing (pingdi) originated with Li Kui 李悝: in buying up grain, it graded quantities according to the degree of the harvest's abundance; in selling [printed as buying, 糴] grain, it set rules according to the severity of the year's famine—modeled, in fact, on the price equalization (pingzhun) of Guan Zhong 管仲. The Ever-Normal Granaries (changping cang) were established by Geng Shouchang 耿壽昌 of the Han: when grain was cheap, they bought it at an increased price to benefit the farmers; when grain was dear, they sold [printed as bought, 糴] it at a reduced price to relieve the people—modeled, in fact, on Li Kui's equitable grain purchasing. The Charitable Granaries (yicang) began with Dai Zhou 戴胄 of the Tang: his method required everyone from princes and dukes downward to contribute grain to relieve the people; thereafter, during the Taihe reign, they repeatedly increased…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
其儲備宋祖復銳於脩置焉社倉昉於隋
長孫平其法酌戶上中下入粟充賑厥後
朱熹請建於浙東眞德秀踵行於長沙焉
凡此皆權宜濟變之術雖未能先事豫圖
然其因時區畫拯賴元元猶不失周官之
遺意者乎乃若河內凶則移民河東河東
凶則移粟河內此惠王之行於梁也關中
饑則徙民蜀漢山東水則徙民關西此高
武之行於漢也丞相而下入穀助貧非漢
===
宣帝之詔乎郡國富室給稟堇獨非漢光
武之令乎宋神宗以空名度牒付兩浙鬻
米賑濟蘇軾請令轉運司約度諸郡米數
下諸路封樁雖其救災憫患非不懇惻周
悉顧帑竭藏空智窮力絀亦豈得爲救荒
之長策耶合而觀之堯湯不可及已周禮
王制策之上者平糴之法霸術之餘耳常
平至東漢時已有劉般之議若曰豪右因
緣爲姦小民不得其平而義倉社倉在朱
punctuated: 其儲備，宋祖復銳於脩置焉。社倉昉於隋長孫平，其法酌戶上、中、下入粟充賑；厥後朱熹請建於浙東，眞德秀踵行於長沙焉。凡此，皆權宜濟變之術。雖未能先事豫圖，然其因時區畫，拯賴元元，猶不失《周官》之遺意者乎？乃若河內凶則移民河東，河東凶則移粟河內，此惠王之行於梁也；關中饑則徙民蜀漢，山東水則徙民關西，此高、武之行於漢也。丞相而下入穀助貧，非漢宣帝之詔乎？郡國富室給稟堇，獨非漢光武之令乎？宋神宗以空名度牒付兩浙鬻米賑濟，蘇軾請令轉運司約度諸郡米數，下諸路封樁。雖其救災憫患，非不懇惻周悉，顧帑竭藏空，智窮力絀，亦豈得爲救荒之長策耶？合而觀之，堯、湯不可及已，《周禮》、《王制》，策之上者；平糴之法，霸術之餘耳。常平至東漢時已有劉般之議，若曰「豪右因緣爲姦，小民不得其平」；而義倉、社倉在朱
translation_en:
…its reserves, and the Song founder (Taizu) was again keen on establishing and restoring them. Community granaries (shecang 社倉) originated with Zhangsun Ping 長孫平 of the Sui; his method weighed households into upper, middle, and lower tiers to contribute grain for relief. Thereafter, Zhu Xi 朱熹 petitioned to establish them in eastern Zhejiang (Zhedong), and Zhen Dexiu 真德秀 followed suit by implementing them in Changsha. All of these were expedient techniques for meeting emergencies. Even if they could not plan ahead before events occurred, by making arrangements according to the times and rescuing the common people, did they not still preserve the surviving intent of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan 周官)?

As for moving people to Hedong when there was famine in Henei, and moving grain to Henei when there was famine in Hedong, this was practiced by King Hui in Liang; relocating people to Shu and Han when there was famine in Guanzhong, and relocating people to Guanxi when there were floods in Shandong, this was practiced by Emperors Gaozu and Wu in the Han. Having the Counselor-in-Chief (chengxiang 丞相) and those below contribute grain to aid the poor—was this not the edict of Emperor Xuan of the Han? Having wealthy families in the commanderies and principalities provide grain rations [?] (bingjin 稟堇)—was this alone not the order of Emperor Guangwu of the Han? Emperor Shenzong of the Song issued blank monk-ordination certificates to Liangzhe to sell for rice to provide relief, and Su Shi 蘇軾 requested that the Fiscal Intendants (zhuanyun si 轉運司) estimate the amount of rice needed across the prefectures and draw upon the reserved funds (fengzhuang 封樁) in the circuits. Although their efforts to relieve disaster and pity distress were not lacking in earnestness and thoroughness, when the treasuries were exhausted and the storehouses empty, and wisdom and strength were depleted, how could such measures be considered long-term policies for famine relief?

Viewed together, Yao and Tang are beyond reach, while the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli 周禮) and the Royal Regulations (Wangzhi 王制) represent the highest policy; the method of price-stabilizing grain purchases (pingdi 平糴) is merely a remnant of hegemonic statecraft. By the Eastern Han, the ever-normal granaries (changping 常平) had already drawn the criticism of Liu Ban 劉般, who said in effect that "powerful families take advantage of them to commit fraud, and the common people do not receive fair benefit"; while regarding charity granaries (yicang 義倉) and community granaries, in Zhu…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
子建安之記亦曰里社不皆可用之人欲
聽其所爲恐計私以害公欲謹其出入則
上下相遁其害爲尤甚誠如是若無一可
者然與其移粟就食助貸給廩於臨時毋
寧權貴賤平豐歉如平糴之爲愈乎與其
降度牒發封樁於臨變毋寧廣儲積便貸
藉如諸倉之爲愈乎肆我
皇明立法定制悉倣周禮天下郡縣咸有預備
卽廩人之掌九穀也鄉有四倉卽遺人之
掌委積也災傷一聞蠲䘏隨及卽賑民施
惠之意也
===
列聖相承靡不注念於是至我
皇上嗣服
泰運洪開崇節儉寛宿逋停不急之工罷非
時之獻祇德格天時和歲稔若無可過計
者乃臺臣上言司農覆奏申明
先朝故事責成守令量里積穀豈非有見於
豫之道乎愚聞之蘇軾曰九年之蓄常閒
punctuated: 子建安之記，亦曰：「里社不皆可用之人，欲聽其所爲，恐計私以害公；欲謹其出入，則上下相遁，其害爲尤甚。」誠如是，若無一可者。然與其移粟就食、助貸給廩於臨時，毋寧權貴賤、平豐歉，如平糴之爲愈乎？與其降度牒、發封樁於臨變，毋寧廣儲積、便貸藉，如諸倉之爲愈乎？肆我皇明立法定制，悉倣《周禮》。天下郡縣，咸有預備，卽廩人之掌九穀也；鄉有四倉，卽遺人之掌委積也；災傷一聞，蠲䘏隨及，卽賑民施惠之意也。列聖相承，靡不注念於是。至我皇上嗣服，泰運洪開，崇節儉，寛宿逋，停不急之工，罷非時之獻，祇德格天，時和歲稔，若無可過計者。乃臺臣上言，司農覆奏，申明先朝故事，責成守令，量里積穀，豈非有見於豫之道乎？愚聞之蘇軾曰：「九年之蓄，常閒
translation_en:
… Zi's (Zhu Xi 朱熹) record in Jian'an, it is also said: "In the rural communities, not everyone is a trustworthy person. If we let them do as they please, it is to be feared that they will scheme for private gain to the detriment of the public good; if we strictly supervise their receipts and disbursements, then superiors and inferiors will collude to evade oversight, and the harm will be even worse." If it is truly like this, it seems as though not a single measure is workable. Yet rather than transferring grain, moving people to where food is, or providing aid, loans, and rations only when an emergency strikes, would it not be better to balance high and low prices and even out abundant and lean harvests, as in the method of equitable grain purchasing (pingdi)? And rather than issuing ordination certificates or releasing sealed reserve funds only when disaster is at hand, would it not be better to expand reserves and facilitate borrowing, as with those various granaries?

Thus, when our august Ming established its laws and fixed its institutions, it modeled everything on the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli). Every prefecture and county in the empire has preparatory granaries (yubei cang), which corresponds to the Granary Masters (linren) managing the nine grains; each rural district has four granaries, which corresponds to the Surplus Grain Masters (weiren) managing accumulated stores; and as soon as word of natural disaster or crop damage is heard, tax remissions and relief immediately follow, which embodies the intent of relieving the people and bestowing benevolence. Successive sacred emperors have inherited this tradition, and none has failed to focus his concern upon it.

Now that His Majesty has succeeded to the throne, a great era of peace and prosperity has opened wide. He exalts frugality, pardons old tax arrears, halts non-urgent construction works, and abolishes unseasonable tribute presentations. His reverent virtue reaches Heaven, the seasons are harmonious, and the harvests are abundant, so that there would seem to be nothing requiring excessive worry. Even so, Censorate officials have submitted memorials, and the Minister of Revenue (sinong) has replied in endorsement, reiterating the precedents of former reigns and holding prefects and magistrates (shouling) responsible for accumulating grain in proportion to the size of the communities (li). Is this not because they have insight into the principle of advance preparation? I have heard Su Shi 蘇軾 say: "Having nine years' worth of reserves, constantly lying idle …"

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
而無用者萬世之計也一歲之入纔足一
歲之出一時之計也量出爲入用之不給
則取之益多此不終月之計也夫不終月
之計計之下者一時之計計之中者萬世
之計計之上者此非策士之至言而籌國
之石畫歟是故計之下者非
聖世所宜有不足以凟執事之聽矣乃若墾荒
僻之田通水泉之利復故額於屯營釐宿
蠹於鹽法追呼不擾催科以時而去三宂
===
酌三盈則計之上者其可行乎尋四倉之
制裁斂散之規在社者不得轉而爲縣在
縣者不得轉而爲郡民見其出亦見其入
則計之中者其可行乎雖然世無王良則
騕褭非異足時無子野則玉徽鮮奇音用
法非人則亦徒法耳昔人有曰天下之本
在於郡縣郡縣之責付之監司又曰君者
父母民者赤子郡縣乳保也是故在郡縣
者必主以撫摩之心而出爲平易之政不
punctuated: 而無用者，萬世之計也；一歲之入，纔足一歲之出，一時之計也；量出爲入，用之不給，則取之益多，此不終月之計也。」夫不終月之計，計之下者；一時之計，計之中者；萬世之計，計之上者。此非策士之至言，而籌國之石畫歟？是故計之下者，非聖世所宜有，不足以凟執事之聽矣。乃若墾荒僻之田，通水泉之利，復故額於屯營，釐宿蠹於鹽法，追呼不擾，催科以時，而去三宂、酌三盈，則計之上者其可行乎？尋四倉之制，裁斂散之規，在社者不得轉而爲縣，在縣者不得轉而爲郡，民見其出，亦見其入，則計之中者其可行乎？雖然，世無王良，則騕褭非異足；時無子野，則玉徽鮮奇音。用法非人，則亦徒法耳。昔人有曰：「天下之本在於郡縣，郡縣之責付之監司。」又曰：「君者父母，民者赤子，郡縣乳保也。」是故在郡縣者，必主以撫摩之心，而出爲平易之政。不
translation_en: … and remaining unused, that is a plan for ten thousand generations; when one year's revenue barely suffices for one year's expenditure, that is a plan for the moment; when revenue is determined by expenditure, and if spending is insufficient then more and more is extracted, that is a plan that will not last a month." Now, a plan that will not last a month is the lowest kind of plan; a plan for the moment is a middling plan; a plan for ten thousand generations is the highest kind of plan. Are these not the supreme words of a strategist and a rock-solid design for statecraft? Therefore, the lowest kind of plan is not what ought to exist in a sacred age, and is unworthy of defiling the ears of Your Excellency. As for reclaiming wild and remote lands, opening the benefits of streams and springs, restoring the old quotas in military agricultural colonies, clearing out chronic abuses in the salt monopoly, not harassing the people with summonses, collecting taxes at the proper seasons, eliminating the three redundancies, and weighing the three surpluses—could the highest kind of plan then be put into practice? Investigating the system of the four granaries and regulating the rules for collection and distribution, so that grain in the community granaries cannot be transferred to the counties, and grain in the counties cannot be transferred to the prefectures, allowing the people to see both its disbursement and its intake—could the middling kind of plan then be put into practice? Even so, if the age lacks a Wang Liang, the finest steed is no extraordinary mount; if the times lack a Ziye [Shi Kuang], jade lute-stops rarely yield wondrous tones. If laws are applied without the right men, they remain mere laws. Someone in the past said: "The foundation of the Empire lies in the prefectures and counties, and the responsibility for the prefectures and counties is entrusted to the Surveillance Officials." And it was also said: "The ruler is the father and mother, the people are newborn infants, and the prefectures and counties are the wet nurses." Therefore, those who serve in the prefectures and counties must hold fast to a heart that comforts and nurtures, and manifest it as gentle and accessible governance. They do not…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
曰歲稔可喜也爲不世之謀而不計目前
之勞費不曰無事可安也爲不世之利而
不計今日之怨尤未荒則以飭倉廩以慎
出納如劉晏之月察豐歉可也將荒則酌
其盈縮悉其貧富如趙抃之書問屬邑可
也既荒則計口發粟里胥不得售其姦華
腴不得侵其利如曾鞏所謂鄞乏得濟可
也斯稱乳保之任乎在監司則巡行郡邑
而廉察之計其大不責其細取其實不采
===
其華時政未飭者則申令以昭其度如李
膺刺青州守令畏服可也實績已著者則
酌賞以昭其勸如賈琮刺冀州羣吏望風
可也事難固滯者則毋拘文法許其便宜
如汲黯之矯制可也斯稱表率之任乎苟
非其人則郡縣之倉雖建也而或上下其
手或漁獵其利虛文簿以罔上者不終無
矣量里之穀雖積也而悖入以取盈嚴威
以重賾開餽局於私囊者不終無矣雖有
punctuated: 曰歲稔可喜也，爲不世之謀而不計目前之勞費；不曰無事可安也，爲不世之利而不計今日之怨尤。未荒，則以飭倉廩、以慎出納，如劉晏之月察豐歉可也；將荒，則酌其盈縮、悉其貧富，如趙抃之書問屬邑可也；既荒，則計口發粟，里胥不得售其姦，華腴不得侵其利，如曾鞏所謂鄞乏得濟可也。斯稱乳保之任乎！在監司，則巡行郡邑而廉察之，計其大不責其細，取其實不采其華。時政未飭者，則申令以昭其度，如李膺刺青州、守令畏服可也；實績已著者，則酌賞以昭其勸，如賈琮刺冀州、羣吏望風可也；事難固滯者，則毋拘文法、許其便宜，如汲黯之矯制可也。斯稱表率之任乎！苟非其人，則郡縣之倉雖建也，而或上下其手，或漁獵其利，虛文簿以罔上者，不終無矣；量里之穀雖積也，而悖入以取盈，嚴威以重賾，開餽局於私囊者，不終無矣。雖有
translation_en: … not say that a bountiful harvest is cause for complacency, but rather make plans for generations to come without begrudging immediate toil and expense; they do not say that peace and quiet are cause for comfort, but rather create benefits for generations to come without worrying about present resentment and blame. Before famine strikes, they should put the granaries in order and exercise care over receipts and disbursements, just as Liu Yan 劉晏 inspected the harvests every month. When famine is about to strike, they should weigh surpluses and shortfalls and thoroughly ascertain who is rich and who is poor, just as Zhao Bian 趙抃 sent letters of inquiry to his subordinate counties. Once famine has struck, they should distribute grain according to the number of mouths, so that village clerks cannot practice their deceit and the wealthy and powerful cannot usurp the benefits—just as Zeng Gong 曾鞏 described how the needy of Yin 鄞 were relieved. Would this not fulfill the duty of a wet nurse and guardian? As for the Surveillance Commissioners, they should tour the prefectures and counties and investigate them with integrity, reckoning their major achievements without nitpicking minor faults, and valuing substantive results without adopting mere flashiness. Where current administration is not yet in order, they should reiterate regulations to make clear the standards, just as Li Ying 李膺 served as Regional Inspector of Qingzhou 青州 and the Grand Protectors and Magistrates submitted in awe. Where actual achievements are already manifest, they should deliberate on rewards to make clear their encouragement, just as Jia Cong 賈琮 served as Regional Inspector of Jizhou 冀州 and the assembled officials responded at the mere rumour of his approach. Where affairs are difficult and cannot be rigidly bound, they should not cling to the letter of the law, but allow officials to act at their own discretion, just as Ji An 汲黯 forged an imperial edict to open the granaries. Would this not fulfill the duty of setting an example? If the right men are not found, then even though prefectural and county granaries are established, there will inevitably be those who manipulate the rules, prey upon the profits, and falsify registers and account books to deceive their superiors; and even though grain is stored across the measured villages, there will inevitably be those who extort illicitly to create a surplus, use harsh intimidation to exact heavy demands [?], and open channels for bribes to fill their private purses. Even if there are …

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
良法將安用之是故不惟其法惟其人不
惟其人惟其心則常平義社卽周之荒政
卽堯湯之所以救民於當時者也魏漢叔
季之制奚足言哉抑又聞之天子不言有
無諸侯不言多寡爲之臣者順五行脩五
事以安百姓興學校明禮義以厚風俗而
聖天子端拱穆清執中以立其道敘倫以立其
教分職率屬以立其官脩明紀綱以立其
法培植基本以立其國譬諸善理家者不
===
徒豐其財貨而且本仁由義淪禮浹樂則
精神所及德化所通天不能爲之災地不
能爲之害薄海內外舉樂利於熙皞之域
蘭臺螭螭之手屢書大有之不暇奚必救
荒爲哉
punctuated: 良法，將安用之？是故不惟其法，惟其人；不惟其人，惟其心。則常平、義、社，卽周之荒政，卽堯、湯之所以救民於當時者也。魏、漢叔季之制，奚足言哉！抑又聞之：天子不言有無，諸侯不言多寡。爲之臣者，順五行、脩五事以安百姓，興學校、明禮義以厚風俗；而聖天子端拱穆清，執中以立其道，敘倫以立其教，分職率屬以立其官，脩明紀綱以立其法，培植基本以立其國。譬諸善理家者，不徒豐其財貨，而且本仁、由義、淪禮、浹樂。則精神所及，德化所通，天不能爲之災，地不能爲之害，薄海內外，舉樂利於熙皞之域，蘭臺螭螭之手，屢書大有之不暇，奚必救荒爲哉！
translation_en:
… good laws, of what use will they be? Therefore, it does not depend merely on the laws, but on the men; it does not depend merely on the men, but on their minds. Then the ever-normal, charity, and community granaries are none other than the famine-relief policies of the Zhou dynasty, and none other than the means by which Yao and Tang rescued the people in their own times. How are the institutions of the declining eras of Wei and Han even worth mentioning!

Moreover, I have heard that the Son of Heaven does not speak of having or not having, and the feudal lords do not speak of much or little. Those who serve as ministers should accord with the Five Phases and cultivate the Five Demeanors in order to bring peace to the common people, and promote schools and clarify ritual and righteousness in order to enrich customs. Meanwhile, the sacred Son of Heaven sits in dignified repose with folded hands in serene purity: holding fast to the Mean to establish his Way, ordering human relationships to establish his teachings, dividing offices and leading subordinates to establish his bureaucracy, cultivating and clarifying regulations and discipline to establish his laws, and nurturing the fundamental root to establish his state. It is like one who is skilled at managing a household, who not only enriches its wealth and goods, but also grounds himself in benevolence, follows righteousness, steeps it in ritual, and suffuses it with music. Then, wherever his vital spirit reaches and wherever his virtuous transformation penetrates, Heaven cannot visit calamities upon it and Earth cannot inflict harm upon it. Within and beyond the four seas, all will rejoice in the benefits of a realm of prosperous tranquility. The hands of the court historians at the Orchid Terrace, poised by the carved-dragon balustrades [? 螭螭, likely for 螭頭], will be so busy repeatedly recording years of great abundance that they will have no leisure—what need will there be for famine relief!

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
陝西鄉試録後序
皇上嗣命聖哲謙恩曰若古初惟
得人理咨于舊章時求俊乂
以康敘四方乃元年癸酉秋
八月
詔天下貢士與計偕而〔崇　獻〕具員
陝西考試官乃以大夫執事
===
之意申告于諸偕計士曰嗟
而士也而亦聞曩者人之詆
訾而文士者乎人之言曰畫
楮爲纈非纈也有衣者纈也
刻木爲驥非驥也有駕者驥
也夫文亦畫楮之纈刻木之
驥也非異日士所以效之君
punctuated:
陝西鄉試録後序

皇上嗣命，聖哲謙恩，曰：「若古初，惟得人理。」咨于舊章，時求俊乂，以康敘四方。乃元年癸酉秋八月，詔天下貢士與計偕。而〔崇　獻〕具員陝西考試官，乃以大夫執事之意，申告于諸偕計士曰：「嗟，而士也！而亦聞曩者人之詆訾而文士者乎？人之言曰：『畫楮爲纈，非纈也，有衣者纈也；刻木爲驥，非驥也，有駕者驥也。』夫文，亦畫楮之纈、刻木之驥也，非異日士所以效之君
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shaanxi Provincial Examination

When His Majesty succeeded to the Mandate, in his sage wisdom and humble grace [?] he declared: "Examining into antiquity, good governance depends solely upon obtaining the right men." Consulting the old statutes, he seasonably sought out men of eminent talent in order to bring peace and order to the four quarters of the realm. Accordingly, in the eighth month in the autumn of the guiyou year, the first year of the reign (1573), he issued an edict summoning the tribute scholars of the empire to proceed to the capital along with the local administrative reports. I, Chongxian, filling a post as Examiner for Shaanxi, thereupon set forth the intentions of the grandees and officiating authorities in an admonition to all the scholars selected to accompany the reports, saying: "Alas, you scholars! Have you also heard how people in the past disparaged and criticized you literary scholars? People say: 'Patterned silk painted on paper is not patterned silk; only that which can be worn is patterned silk. A fine steed carved from wood is not a fine steed; only that which can be harnessed is a fine steed.' Now literary composition is likewise patterned silk painted on paper and a fine steed carved from wood; it is not the instrument by which a scholar in future days renders service to his sovereign…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
者具也仕則弃之耳噫使上
不信士學而忘其本必繇
斯言矣夫士布衣發畎畝而
來也卒一旦不可官而使也
誠未有以甞之不一考其言
其道無繇故使有司者召問
而置對焉曰而士也其諷析
===
於聖人之言也其伏而習於
國家之故筴於當世之務也紬
之以觀其業辯之以觀其志
錯而問之以觀其蓄引端而
詰射之以觀其智曰吾以此
測士幸不失矣豈曰文而已
哉而士也亦既以其所誦法
punctuated: 者，具也，仕則弃之耳。」噫！使上不信士學，而忘其本，必繇斯言矣。夫士布衣發畎畝而來也，卒一旦不可官而使也，誠未有以甞之。不一考其言，其道無繇。故使有司者召問而置對焉，曰：「而士也，其諷析於聖人之言也，其伏而習於國家之故，筴於當世之務也。紬之以觀其業，辯之以觀其志，錯而問之以觀其蓄，引端而詰射之以觀其智。曰：吾以此測士，幸不失矣，豈曰文而已哉？」而士也，亦既以其所誦法
translation_en: … are merely an instrument; once they take office, they simply cast it aside." Alas! What causes the ruler above to distrust the learning of scholars, and causes you to forget your fundamental purpose, must surely stem from such words as these. Now, when scholars come forth from the furrowed fields in plain cloth garments, they cannot suddenly in a single morning be appointed to office and employed, for truly there has not yet been any means to test them. Without first examining their words, there is no way to ascertain their principles. Therefore, the authorities are commissioned to summon and question them and have them set down their replies, thinking: "You scholars have recited and analyzed the words of the Sages; in private you have familiarized yourselves with the precedents of the state and devised plans for the affairs of the present age. We draw out your learning to observe your scholarship, have you argue issues to observe your aspirations, pose intertwined questions to observe your accumulated store of knowledge, and raise initial premises to probe and test you to observe your wisdom. Thus we say: Using these means to gauge scholars, we may hope not to miss the mark; how could this be called merely literary composition and nothing more?" And you scholars, for your part, have already taken that whereby you recite and model yourselves on…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
聖人討論當世者而稍薦陳
之矣固曰吾將以其所聞共
之乎吾
君也夫寧曰吾直用爲介藉而已
乎如曰徒介藉耳吾且有所
奉吾
君者或乃倍而謾之是賈人之智
===
也賈之爲市也衒其貨美以
翹於人已乃易而售其惡轉
爲巧謾以偷逐什什之利弗
恥也士固亦若此乎非吾故
所謂文者也士不若是雖然
工人不爲直木而廢繩射者
不爲良弓而輟檠崇獻不佞
punctuated: 聖人、討論當世者，而稍薦陳之矣。固曰：「吾將以其所聞，共之乎吾君也。」夫寧曰：「吾直用爲介藉而已乎？」如曰：「徒介藉耳，吾且有所奉吾君者。」或乃倍而謾之，是賈人之智也。賈之爲市也，衒其貨美以翹於人，已乃易而售其惡，轉爲巧謾，以偷逐什什之利，弗恥也。士固亦若此乎？非吾故所謂文者也。士不若是。雖然，工人不爲直木而廢繩，射者不爲良弓而輟檠。崇獻不佞，
translation_en: … the sages and debated regarding contemporary affairs, have already somewhat presented and set them forth. They surely say: "I shall take what I have learned and offer it in service to my Sovereign." Could they possibly say: "I merely use this as a stepping-stone and nothing more?" Or suppose someone says: "It is merely a stepping-stone; I shall later have something else to present to my Sovereign"—and then perhaps turns his back on his words and deceives him: this is the cunning of a merchant. When a merchant conducts business in the market, he shows off the fineness of his goods to stand out before others, yet afterward swaps them and sells his inferior wares, turning to clever deceit to stealthily chase tenfold profits without shame. Could scholars indeed be like this too? That is not what I originally meant by literary composition. Scholars are not like this. Even so, a carpenter does not discard his ink-line because the timber is straight, nor does an archer set aside his bow-press because the bow is fine. Though I, Chongxian, am untalented, …

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
請得一言爲繩檠可乎昔者
子貢謂子夏曰吾他日見子
有菜色今見芻豢之色何也
子夏曰鄉也吾入見夫子之
義則悅之出見紛華則榮之
二者交戰乎中故菜色今吾
戰勝故也賢者之於內外固
===
戰而後勝之耶夫士方其未
遇菜糲蒙褐穴牖而闚夫子
之義守之易耳故今者吾見
諸士指經術占對言循循然
入而見諸大夫而趨僂然其
質全也其未見紛華之時乎
少焉踰函谷陟都邑過睨蓋
punctuated: 請得一言爲繩檠，可乎？昔者，子貢謂子夏曰：「吾他日見子有菜色，今見芻豢之色，何也？」子夏曰：「鄉也，吾入見夫子之義則悅之，出見紛華則榮之。二者交戰乎中，故菜色。今吾戰勝，故也。」賢者之於內外，固戰而後勝之耶？夫士方其未遇，菜糲蒙褐，穴牖而闚夫子之義，守之易耳。故今者，吾見諸士指經術占對，言循循然，入而見諸大夫而趨僂然，其質全也，其未見紛華之時乎？少焉，踰函谷，陟都邑，過睨蓋…
translation_en: …begs leave to offer a word to serve as a marking line and bow-frame—may I? In former times, Zigong 子貢 said to Zixia 子夏: “On another day when I saw you, you had the pallid look of one fed on greens; today I see the rosy complexion of one fed on grain-fed meats. Why is that?” Zixia replied: “Previously, when I went inside and beheld the Master’s righteousness, I delighted in it; when I went outside and beheld the bustle and splendor of the world, I gloried in it. The two battled within my breast, and therefore I had a pallid look. Now I have won the battle—that is why.” Even for a worthy man, when it comes to the inner and the outer, must he indeed battle before overcoming it? Now, while a scholar has not yet met with advancement, eating coarse greens and wearing rough homespun, peering through a hole-in-the-wall window into the Master’s righteousness, it is easy enough to hold fast to it. Thus at present, when I see the scholars pointing to the classical arts to compose their replies, speaking in an orderly and methodical manner, and entering to present themselves before the grandees with brisk, deferential steps, their native substance is intact—is this not the time when they have not yet seen the bustle and splendor of the world? Before long, they will cross Hangu 函谷 Pass, ascend to the capital and great cities, and cast sidelong glances in passing at canopied…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
駟涉乎利害得失之途而戰
紛華矣吾願諸士之戰而勝
之也蓋昔有二人者並之市
一人顧見衣偽愀然而返其
一人者悅而效之所見同而
好惡趨舍致相遠不可不慎
也士自愛毋回謬其途域毋
利害失得而滑其室毋沒沒
于俗而離而質毋身是謀而
不殫于
===
國使人謂而爲畫繢木驥也有
如一不當卽忠信之士見不
信而蒙詆嗤矣抑語有之深
山大澤龍蛇生焉詩不云乎
punctuated: 駟，涉乎利害得失之途，而戰紛華矣，吾願諸士之戰而勝之也。蓋昔有二人者並之市，一人顧見衣偽，愀然而返；其一人者悅而效之。所見同而好惡趨舍致相遠，不可不慎也。士自愛，毋回謬其途域，毋利害失得而滑其室，毋沒沒于俗而離而質，毋身是謀而不殫于國，使人謂而爲畫繢、木驥也。有如一不當，卽忠信之士見不信而蒙詆嗤矣。抑語有之：「深山大澤，龍蛇生焉。」《詩》不云乎：
translation_en: …four-horse carriages, stepping onto the path of advantage and disadvantage, gain and loss, and battling against the attractions of worldly splendor—I hope that all you scholars will fight this battle and triumph. In the past, two men went together to the marketplace. One looked back and saw someone in ostentatious [?] attire, grew somber, and turned back; the other was delighted and imitated it. What they saw was the same, yet their likes and dislikes, what they pursued and what they shunned, ended up worlds apart—one cannot but be cautious! Scholars, cherish your own integrity: do not stray into crooked and erroneous paths and bounds; do not let calculation of advantage and disadvantage, loss and gain, throw your inner chamber into disorder; do not sink into vulgar custom and depart from your native substance; and do not scheme only for yourselves while failing to exhaust your strength for the state, causing others to call you mere painted ornaments or wooden steeds. Should even a single one of you fail to live up to your station, then even scholars of loyalty and good faith will be distrusted and subjected to slander and ridicule. Yet as the saying goes, "In deep mountains and great marshes, dragons and serpents are born." And does not the Book of Odes (Shi) say:…

title: 萬曆元年陝西鄉試錄
text:
鳳凰鳴矣于彼高岡梧桐生
矣于彼朝陽夫陝固岐豳豐
鎬之都而天府之國也士生
兹地際
聖時亦既敬應矣尚思自效以鳴
國家之盛哉
山西汾州儒學學正宋〔崇獻〕
===
謹序
punctuated:
「鳳凰鳴矣，于彼高岡。梧桐生矣，于彼朝陽。」夫陝固岐、豳、豐、鎬之都，而天府之國也。士生兹地，際聖時，亦既敬應矣，尚思自效以鳴國家之盛哉！
山西汾州儒學學正宋〔崇獻〕謹序。
translation_en:
…“The phoenixes sing, on that high ridge. The parasol trees grow, in that morning sunlight.” Now Shaanxi is indeed the site of the ancient capitals of Qi, Bin, Feng, and Hao, and a land of heavenly abundance. Scholars born in this region, encountering a sagely era, have already respectfully responded to the call; may they further strive to devote themselves to singing the praises of the flourishing of the State!

Respectfully written as a postface by Song Chongxian 宋崇獻, Instructor in the Confucian School of Fenzhou Department in Shanxi.
